title: 解密FBI文件揭中共諜網 美需升級反間諜法
summary: 【大紀元2026年10月18日訊】（英文大紀元記者Sean Tseng撰文／張紫珺編譯）一位美國記者曾經在中共官方媒體擔任專欄作家和編輯長達16年之久。在此期間，他有七年時間受僱於中共國家安全部（Ministry of State Security，簡稱MSS），該部門是中共負責對外情報、反間諜和祕密警察工作的國家機構。 對中共政權而言，51歲的美國公民托馬斯‧威爾‧保肯二世（Thomas Weir Pauken II）的價值在於他可以隨時進出美國。 今年2月，保肯在華盛頓特
content:
【大紀元2026年10月18日訊】（英文大紀元記者Sean Tseng撰文／張紫珺編譯）一位美國記者曾經在中共官方媒體擔任專欄作家和編輯長達16年之久。在此期間，他有七年時間受僱於中共國家安全部（Ministry of State Security，簡稱MSS），該部門是中共負責對外情報、反間諜和祕密警察工作的國家機構。

對中共政權而言，51歲的美國公民托馬斯‧威爾‧保肯二世（Thomas Weir Pauken II）的價值在於他可以隨時進出美國。

今年2月，保肯在華盛頓特區的一家酒店被捕。9月1日，弗吉尼亞州亞歷山大市（Alexandria）的一名聯邦法官判處保肯兩年監禁。

「（保肯）利用了自己的美國公民身分，以及作為公民可以不受限制地進出美國的便利。」助理司法部長約翰‧艾森伯格（John A. Eisenberg）說道。

據美國司法部（Department of Justice，簡稱DOJ）稱，至少從2019年開始到2026年2月，保肯從一位他稱之為「凱西」（Cathy）的中共政府聯絡人那裡，至少領取了十萬美元的報酬。他的任務是從北京前往美國，與可能成為情報人員的人見面，向他們提供通訊設備，並傳遞北京想要了解的信息。

專家向《大紀元時報》透露，北京對美國的情報活動大多是通過已經居住在美國國內的人員進行的，他們執行的任務大多是合法的——牽線搭橋、舉辦活動、記錄參與集會者名單，或是查找個人信息。

這些活動在學生社團、同鄉會、競選籌款活動和大學論壇等各種場合展開——而這些恰恰是開放社會有意保持開放的機構。就保肯而言，他的任務是為他的中共聯絡人在美國司法部物色所謂的「新招募目標」（new recruitment targets）。

北京在美國開展了兩類並行的間諜活動。一類是瞄準美國政界人士、大學校園和國防企業；另一類是監控海外華人，追蹤他們的聚集活動會並向北京匯報。

## 遊走在法律底線以下

中國旅美異見人士陳破空告訴《大紀元時報》，為了完成這兩類間諜活動，北京主要依靠兩類人群：訓練有素的專業間諜和線人。

陳破空曾經參與組織1989年廣東省廣州市的民主抗議活動，曾兩次入獄。他在1996年流亡美國，目前是一位作家，並長期擔任自由亞洲電台（Radio Free Asia，總部位於華盛頓特區）和美國之音（Voice of America，簡稱VOA，總部位於華盛頓特區）的評論員。他在海外華人異見人士群體中已活躍了三十年。

[![Image 1: 這張照片拍攝於英國劍橋大學，日期不詳。照片中，居住在美國的政治評論員兼作家陳破空正在劍橋大學發表演講。陳破空曾因參與1989年中國民主運動而在中共監獄服刑多年。(Courtesy of Chen Pokong)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/14/id6103471-31932281_1803031209717371_4095902627051601920_o-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/14/id6103471-31932281_1803031209717371_4095902627051601920_o-ed.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

這張照片拍攝於英國劍橋大學，日期不詳。照片中，居住在美國的政治評論員兼作家陳破空正在劍橋大學發表演講。陳破空曾因參與1989年中國民主運動而在中共監獄服刑多年。(Courtesy of Chen Pokong)

中共政權大量運用了第二種策略（即利用線人進行間諜活動）——陳破空稱之為中共的「人海戰術」（human-wave tactic）。

「這些線人無處不在：在華人社區裡面、在民主運動的集會上、在美國各種學術會議當中，還有各種大學論壇裡面。」他說道。

「這些線人做的事情就是遊走在法律邊緣。他可以說他的行為是合法的。」

而保肯的性質介於兩者之間。他不算是受過專業訓練的特工，也並非遊走在法律的邊緣：他是一名被招募的特工——領取薪水、受聯絡人指揮、接受任務——而北京要他做的事情是招募更多的人手。

此外，他還向武漢一個想要獲取美國技術和美國司法部信息的組織出售報告，以及向一名可以幫助該組織「從事網絡間諜活動」（engage in cyber espionage）的專家出售報告。

檢方稱，保肯曾經慫恿一名川普政府官員與一名身在中國的女子聯繫，他認為該女子是中共的情報官員。美司法部表示，他承認試圖「滲透美國政治圈」（infiltrate U.S. political circles）以獲取機密信息。

保肯於今年6月認罪，承認在未通知司法部長的情況下，充當外國政府在美國的代理人。在法官萊昂妮‧布林克瑪（Leonie Brinkema）主持的量刑聽證會上，對於檢方查明的與其有關的行為事實，保肯沒有否認。

[![Image 2: 2026年9月23日，華盛頓特區，在中共黨魁習近平訪問前夕，華爾道夫酒店（Waldorf Astoria hotel）附近街道和人行道封閉。現場有人手持中國和美國國旗，站在酒店外巡邏的警察附近。(Oliver Contreras/AFP via Getty Images)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/14/id6103538-GettyImages-2296200045.jpg&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.theepochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/14/id6103538-GettyImages-2296200045.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

2026年9月23日，華盛頓特區，在中共黨魁習近平訪問前夕，華爾道夫酒店（Waldorf Astoria hotel）附近街道和人行道封閉。現場有人手持中國和美國國旗，站在酒店外巡邏的警察附近。(Oliver Contreras/AFP via Getty Images)

「我了解到很多祕密，我確實把這些祕密告訴了中國人。」他說道。他說的祕密，指的是他所分享的非公開信息，該信息並不構成國防機密。

「我原來以為我是在幫忙，但是現在我意識到，我可能會造成更大的破壞，甚至會引發戰爭。」

法官沒有對保肯提出違反《間諜法》（Espionage Act，1917）的指控。該法規定，向外國提供「與國防有關的信息」（information relating to the national defense）屬於違法行為，最高可判處死刑或終身監禁。

9月1日，保肯的律師查爾斯‧伯納姆（Charles Burnham）向《大紀元時報》表示：「正如政府今天在法庭上所確認的那樣，保肯先生沒有向中方提供任何機密信息。」

保肯認罪的罪名最高可判十年監禁。檢方要求判三年，他最終被判兩年監禁。

事實上，北京方面要求他做的事情，沒有一件需要使用暴力。而這一點，並不是他的個案的特殊之處。

1999年，中國軍旅作家喬良和前中共空軍大校王湘穗通過中共軍隊出版社出版了軍事理論書籍《超限戰》（Unrestricted Warfare, 1999）。他們在書中寫道，「戰爭與非戰爭、軍事與非軍事兩個世界之間的界限將被徹底打破。」

《大紀元時報》即將發表的獨家研究報告，專門揭示為何中共以這種方式來運作在美國的間諜活動。該報告題為「中共安全體系的結構：從中央名冊到一線行動單位」（The Structure of the CCP’s Security Apparatus: From Central Rosters to Front-Line Operational Units）。

報告的核心結論就是，中共並沒有將情報或安全工作集中於單一的集權機構。北京負責制定議程，並對所謂的威脅進行界定，而相關具體工作則分配給一線單位——省級和市級國安機關——以及普通民眾。

報告指出，在統一戰線、宗教和學校領域，中共的「社會控制並不總是以強制手段出現」。相反，它表現為聯絡、談心以及培養「代表性人物」（representative figures）——這與中共在美國的間諜活動案例所採用手法，屬於同一個套路。

這種分工也延伸到了中國境外。這些地方性的國安機構負責在入境口岸、大學、科研院所、在華運營的外國公司，以及從原籍國移居海外的僑民社區進行間諜活動。《大紀元時報》即將發表的報告指出，這些地方國安機構「有各自的起源、網絡和目標群體」。

而這一切間諜活動背後都有法律依據支持。中共在2017年頒布《國家情報法》（National Intelligence Law），要求中國公民和組織支持和配合國家情報工作。

而聯邦調查局（FBI）已經把這個間諜系統在美國實地運作的具體表現記錄了下來。

## 第一類間諜活動：培養特工接近目標

陳破空透露，在中共的「人海戰術」中，關鍵的要素是海外留學生。這些留學生被分配一些在活動中完成的小任務，例如建立人脈、錄製視頻和收集名片等等。

「回到中國後，他們可以把這些情報任務換成學分。」他說道。

他稱之為中國留學生的「作業」。

在近150頁的聯邦調查局（FBI）關於疑似中共特工方芳（Christine Fang）的記錄中，體現了這些情報的價值。這些記錄由白宮解密，並於8月17日發布。記錄顯示，FBI對這名加州舊金山灣區女子進行了長達四年的調查，FBI評估認為該女子與中共國家安全部（MSS）有可疑聯繫，並且她的父母都是情報官員。

方芳在美國某州立大學創辦了中國留學生的學生會，並將其發展到700多名成員。中共駐舊金山總領事館授予她「西海岸最佳學生會主席」的稱號。她曾經與舊金山市長共同舉辦盛大晚宴，並為當時年輕的聯邦眾議員埃里克‧斯沃韋爾（Eric Swalwell，民主黨/加州）籌款。

這些行為沒有一件是非法的。但根據方芳在檔案中的描述，在那幾年裡，中共曾經安排她分別與一位州長、兩位市長和一位國會議員單獨待在同一個房間裡。

曾任美國陸軍軍官和外交官的馬修‧布拉澤爾（Matthew Brazil）合著了《中共間諜活動：情報入門》（Chinese Communist Espionage: An Intelligence Primer，2019）一書。他告訴《大紀元時報》，外交使團有其正當理由去拉攏這類團體，「但這也為情報的發掘與評估提供了機會」。

「從方芳的行動來看，似乎是（對這些美國政要）進行長期培養，而不是招募作為情報人員和收集情報的來源。潛在的情報來源會先被識別並評估，然後才會被『接觸』並招募。」他說道。

當案件於當年5月結案時，FBI探員寫道，證據表明方芳違反了多項刑法，包括競選資金法、虛假陳述法和大量現金走私法，以及第951條（保肯正是根據該條被判刑）。調查人員沒有發現任何證據表明「方芳與國會議員或其辦公室之間存在利益交換」。

FBI拒絕就此案發表評論。

方芳間諜案就是中共整套間諜手法的典型例子。她所利用的每項資源，都是開放社會所自由提供的——無論是校園社團、領事榮譽、還是在籌款活動上的一個席位。她無需竊取任何東西，等到FBI弄清事情的來龍去脈時，她已經獲得了所有必要的資源。

## 然後提出要求

接近目標只是間諜活動的第一步。在準備工作完成之後，北京方面會提出什麼要求，則取決於誰在提出要求。

《大紀元時報》的專題報告發現，地方國安機構專攻哪一領域，「很大程度上取決於其所在地區」。有航空業的省份會想方設法獲得航空業相關的情報。而如果一個省份有很多移民並在加州建立了社區，自然會對加州感興趣。

江蘇省擁有航空航天基地。2013年，中國公民季超群（Ji Chaoqun）持學生簽證來到美國芝加哥，在伊利諾伊理工學院（Illinois Institute of Technology）攻讀電氣工程專業。作為中共國家安全部省級機構的江蘇省國家安全廳委託他收集八名在美國工作的中國公民的背景信息，以便日後可能成為招募對象。這些人都是工程師和科學家，其中幾人為美國國防承包商工作。

這一切都不需要闖入任何圈子。僅需一份學生簽證、一個研究生項目、八個目標人物的姓名——北京所需要的情報活動，任何人都可以執行。

而令季超群罪行暴露的是另外一件事。2016年，他通過一個針對具備特殊技能的外籍人士計劃，加入了美國陸軍預備役，並隱瞞自己與外國政府有聯繫的事實。季超群於2018年被捕，2022年因犯有非法從事代理人活動和向美國陸軍撒謊而被定罪。次年，他被判處八年有期徒刑。

在背後指揮季超群的中共官員叫徐炎鈞，他是江蘇省國安廳六處的副處長，也是在美國迄今為止唯一被定罪的在職中共情報官員。他的情報目標是位於俄亥俄州辛辛那提（Cincinnati）的通用電氣航空集團（GE Aviation）所擁有的複合材料發動機風扇模塊技術。美司法部稱，這項技術「全球尚無其它公司能夠複製」。。

徐炎鈞的手段與方芳如出一轍。他找到美國航空公司的工程師，邀請他們來中國講學，並向他們支付旅費和津貼。事發之後，由於無法在中國逮捕徐炎鈞，2018年，FBI以一位通用電氣工程師與他見面為誘餌，將他引到比利時。隨後，徐炎鈞被引渡回美國俄亥俄州，並於2022年11月因違反《經濟間諜法》（Economic Espionage Act，簡稱EEA，1996）被判處20年監禁。

## 第二類間諜活動：瞄準華人僑民

第一類間諜活動主要是向外操作，目的接觸外部人士以及獲取外部信息，而第二類間諜活動的運作方向則相反——目標向內，目的是控制海外的中國國民。在這項間諜活動中，國安部收集情報的工作通過中共領事館和中共公安部（在中國的警察部門）來執行。

在美國的中國異見人士群體在集會時會有簽到信息。陳破空介紹，如果這些團體已經被滲透，組織者就會複印簽到名冊，然後交給中共方面。

他說，同鄉會（以省為單位的華人社區聯誼會）「受到中共領事館和大使館的幕後操縱，中共向它們提供資金並頒發榮譽」。

5月13日，紐約布魯克林的一個聯邦陪審團裁定，來自紐約州布朗克斯（Bronx）的美國公民盧建旺（Lu Jianwang）犯有充當中共政府非法代理人和妨礙司法公正的罪行。

檢方稱，他協助中共在曼哈頓唐人街東百老匯的一棟建築內，設立了美國長樂公會。這是一個未經申報的中共警察局，其功能是監視海外的中國異見人士，並追蹤一名逃往美國的民主活動人士。盧建旺面臨最高30年的監禁。

「我們絕不允許外國派來的祕密『警察』騷擾美國民眾。」助理司法部長艾森伯格說道。艾森伯格也是宣布保肯判決的美國官員。

「很難說兩者之間有什麼界限。」他回答道，「線人和間諜之間——也就是中共非正規情報人員和中共正規情報人員之間——界限真的非常模糊。」

## 鉆美國法律的漏洞

而這條模糊的界限正是美國的檢察官們必須找到的；美國有兩項法律規定必須具備這條界限。

《美國法典》（United States Code）第18篇第951條是美國政府打擊祕密為外國政府工作的人的主要法律工具。保肯承認的罪名正是基於這條法律的規定。

1938年的《外國代理人登記法》（Foreign Agents Registration Act，簡稱FARA）的力度相對較弱。它要求為外國委託人工作的人員披露其身分，但在這一法律出台之後，大部分時期幾乎沒有被使用過：據美司法部統計，在截至2015年的49年裡，僅有七起相關刑事案件。

這兩項法規均未將「為外國政府工作」這一行為本身定為犯罪。根據第951條，為外國政府工作是合法的；違法行為的定義是為外國政府工作而未向美國司法部長申報。《外國代理人登記法》僅要求為外國政府工作的人進行公開登記。

在現實中，牽線搭橋、舉辦活動、記錄集會者名單——這些網絡日常運作的內容——都不受上述兩項法規的約束。即使某項法規確實適用，也需要證明該人員是在外國政府的指示或控制下行事，而這種關聯正是由眾多小角色組成的龐大網絡最擅長隱藏的。

中共勢力目前所利用的，正是美國法律的這一漏洞。

戴維‧基廷（David Keating）是美國言論自由研究所（Institute for Free Speech，簡稱IFS，總部位於華盛頓特區）負責人，該研究所基於美國憲法《第一修正案》（First Amendment），針對聯邦信息披露法和選舉法提起訴訟。去年，基廷曾經要求美國司法部縮小《外國代理人登記法》（FARA）的適用範圍。他當時針對的是法規本身，而不是任何具體的案例。

當被問及這些法規是否可能同時存在管得過於狹窄和管得過於寬泛的情況時，基廷告訴《大紀元時報》，這兩種情況都可能存在，而這正是由於法規措辭含糊不清造成的。他說，那些「可以說應該被涵蓋」（arguably should be covered）的行為，最終可能已經涵蓋了，也可能沒有涵蓋。

對於北京在美國境內向宗教團體施壓的案件，妮娜‧謝伊（Nina Shea）認為，背後存在著另一個問題。作為哈德遜研究所（Hudson Institute，總部位於華盛頓特區）的高級研究員，她曾七次擔任美國國際宗教自由事務專員。

「司法部正在調查其中一些案件，但只有極少數案件會進行調查並提起訴訟，更不用說上法庭了。」她向《大紀元時報》透露。

「即使他們提起訴訟，也只是較輕的指控——例如向聯邦調查局撒謊，或者未根據《外國代理人登記法》註冊為中方的外國代理人。」

兩人的言論指向相反的方向。謝伊抱怨的是，這類案件中真正被起訴的寥寥無幾；而基廷則認為，如果法律管得更為寬泛，反而會波及普通美國民眾。

## 間諜活動中斷但未停止

事實上，只要案件能提起訴訟，指控就會成立。徐炎鈞被判處20年監禁，季超群被判處8年有期徒刑。紐約布魯克林陪審團判定盧建旺罪名成立。方芳從未被起訴，但她的間諜身分已經被確認，並被禁止進入公共場所。

然而，這一切法律程序都未能從源頭上阻止中共在美國的間諜活動。

2024年11月27日，徐炎鈞和季超群與另一名中國公民一起被遣返回到中國；作為交換，北京釋放了被關押多年的三名美國人。

前美國陸軍軍官兼外交官巴西（Brazil，化名）認為，這次交換並不算是一種損失。

「2024年的這筆交易並非失敗，因為自冷戰之前，間諜交換就一直是常見的權衡之舉。」他說道。

北京方面對此早已做好盤算。

更引人思考的是這些間諜被指控的罪名：這些罪名鮮少是北京真正讓他們完成的任務，通常都是處於邊緣地帶的事務。季超群因在陸軍表格上作不實陳述而被定罪，徐炎鈞因泄露商業機密而非運營間諜網絡而被定罪，保肯則因在為北京工作七年後仍未向美國司法部長報告而被定罪。盧建旺被直接定罪，但他是容易抓獲的目標；2023年被起訴的44人據信目前身在中國境內，目前仍然逍遙法外。

與這些控罪相對的，是這些間諜活動帶給中共的成果。其中就包括：一位後來在聯邦眾議院情報委員會（House Intelligence Committee，簡稱HIC）任職的國會議員；來自美國航空公司工程師的資料；一份八人名單，其中幾人為美國國防承包商工作；一份異議人士集會的簽到名冊。

# 香港领导人在亚太经合组织会议后会见中国财政部长
香港行政长官李家港会见中国财政部长兰福安，讨论经济和金融发展。李显龙感谢兰率团出席在香港举行的亚太经合组织财长会议，并感谢国家对香港作为国际金融中心的信任。

李显龙欢迎并感谢兰率团来港主持2026年亚太经合组织财长会议。会上，李总对合作伙伴表示衷心感谢。

# Hong Kong leader meets China finance minister after APEC meeting

Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee met China's Finance Minister Lan Fo'an to discuss economic and financial development. Lee thanked Lan for leading a delegation to the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting in Hong Kong and expressed gratitude for the country's trust in the city as an international financ

Hong Kong's Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu met with China's Finance Minister Lan Fo'an to exchange views on the economic and financial development of the mainland and Hong Kong, according to a government statement issued on 21 October.

Lee welcomed and thanked Lan for leading a delegation to Hong Kong to chair the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Finance Ministers' Meeting. At the meeting, Lee expressed his sincere gratitude for the country's trust in and support for Hong Kong, as well as its high recognition of the city's status as an international financial centre.

Hong Kong actively leveraged the finance ministers' meeting as an international exchange platform to showcase its unique advantages and to deepen economic and trade exchanges and cooperation with APEC member economies, Lee said.

As the engine of global economic growth, the Asia-Pacific region shoulders greater responsibility amid multiple challenges facing world economic growth, he added. The city will continue to play its roles as a "super-connector" and a "super value-adder" to jointly promote regional economic cooperation, prosperity, and stability, Lee said.

Hong Kong will continue to advance the high-quality development of its international financial centre, deepen mutual market access with mainland financial markets, and serve the country's high-level financial opening-up, Lee added.

Also attending the meeting were Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong Wai-lun, and Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui Ching-yu.

title: 台北一周 - 台湾政治风向指标关键新北市，苏巧慧能否打破过去21年蓝营执政

content:
距离九合一选举剩下约6个星期，各区选战都已进入白热化的「选战模式」。受到台北市「洋流崛起」影响选情，过往让蓝营引以为豪的双北票仓，都传出失守危机。而新北市因身为全台最大票仓，被国民党视为「绝对不能输的重中之重」与2028年总统大选重返执政的关键基地。

距离九合一选举剩下约6个星期，各区选战都已进入白热化的「选战模式」。关键选区包括新北市、台北市、新竹县、彰化县及基隆市，其中又以「新北市为最关键一战」。美国史丹佛大学胡佛研究所政治学者祁凯立（Kharis Templeman）曾表示，新北市是观察台湾政治走向最重要的风向指标。

祁凯立分析，新北市人口超过400万，是台湾人口最多的直辖市，蓝绿实力相近，可视为双方实力正面对决，且全国性因素预料将在新北市选举结果中扮演重要角色。某种程度来说，无论谁拿下新北，都有理由称自己表现超出预期，将这次选举视为胜利。

**新北国民党21年执政遭挑战？**

从台北县到新北市，国民党已连续执政21年。自2005年周锡伟担任台北县长到2010年朱立伦选上新北市长。如今新北市长侯友宜两任任期届满，国民党由李四川接棒参选，民进党则由苏巧慧出马挑战，双方目前战况陷入胶着状态。

以《巨闻天下》民调结果来看，李四川从7月的50.85%，一路滑落到现在的45.74%，下滑了5.11个百分点。反观，苏巧慧则稳步爬升到45.18%，双方差距只剩0.56个百分点，进入肉搏拉锯战。以此走势来看，李四川一路从稳赢到跌破防线，被解读为是对国民党选情上一大警讯。

若以台北市信民两岸研究协会在13日公布最新的新北市长选情民调，苏巧慧获得43.1%支持度、李四川则获得30.0%，差距直接拉到13.1个百分点。民调专家戴立安以此民调数据分析，这是因为台北市民进党参选人沈伯洋的「洋流」外溢，直接拉抬了新北市长选情，洋流现在已经变成海啸。但也有专家表示，虽然民调受洋流效应影响产生震荡，但双方在得票率推估上仍可能在误差范围内，即所谓「沉默的蓝营选民」尚未表态。

**新北市长候选人苏巧慧与李四川**

民进党候选人苏巧慧自2016年起当选连任第9、10、11届新北市第五选举区立委，也是现任民进党立法院党团副干事长。国民党主席郑丽文曾以「出身民进党最大、最有力家族的公主」形容苏巧慧，因为她的爸爸正是前行政院长苏贞昌，所以自5岁起她就有跟着父亲上街拜票的经验。

副总统萧美琴曾表示，苏巧慧不仅在教育、社福、环卫及经济等领域做足了准备，更是大家心中温暖的「水獭妈妈」，集结了狗派跟猫派的温暖热情，与强大的创新行动力。

苏巧慧在早早确定目标后，就开始地方拜票、扫街、扫市场，并让她的民调得以快速跟上其竞选节奏。她将竞选主轴聚焦在年轻族群、地方创生、文化、AI等建设，以此力拼翻转新北市。但另一方面，来自父亲苏贞昌的政治包袱，可能让不喜欢苏贞昌的选民因此选择将票投给对手。

另一方面，国民党候选人李四川现年68岁，自2010年起担任过新北市副市长、台北市副市长、高雄市副市长、行政院秘书长、国民党秘书长等要职。 2022年，受台北市长蒋万安邀请出任台北市副市长。并在2026年2月，代表台北市政府与辉达正式签约后不久即卸任，投入新北市长选举。

李四川向来的强势区域为新北的瑞芳 、贡寮等海岸线行政区，以及人口稠密的新店、中永和等区。但部分评论表示，李四川的形象太老，难以吸引年轻人。且李四川越上新闻节目，整体就越失分。竞选节奏落后与年老形象成为他最主要的劣势。

两位候选人相较之下，李四川长期主打能做事的工程师、技术官僚形象，但在没有新政见牛肉与愿景支撑下，开始让年轻中产家庭、女性选民感到枯燥无味。相反地，苏巧慧主打实质育儿、教育与生活感牛肉，成功精准吸纳了浮动的票源。这可能是造成双方支持度逐渐拉平的原因之一。

**守住新北市对蓝营的意义**

国民党在这次九合一县市长选举中面临保住既有执政版图的压力，难度比表面上看起来更高，民进党则可能席次反而增加。这与国民党许多现任县市长因任期限制必须卸任、失去现任优势，赖清德总统施政满意度提升，以及经济蓬勃发展有利执政党等因素有关。

在这场难打得选战中，受到台北市「洋流崛起」影响选情，过往让蓝营引以为豪的双北票仓，都传出失守危机。而新北市因身为全台最大票仓，被国民党视为「绝对不能输的重中之重」与2028年总统大选重返执政的关键基地。

有台湾学者表示，新北市对国民党而言，有不能输的压力，若能稳住新北，不仅能为蓝营2028重返执政保留关键量能，也能验证台北市长蒋万安「万安旋风」的外溢效应。

《经济日报》报导，美国学者祁凯立对此分析，如果国民党在这次选举结果不如预期，可能会促成党内权力调整，反而可能为2028总统大选创造更有利位置。因此九合一选举结果未必能代表2028总统大选胜负。

# Taiwan a 'faithful partner': St. Vincent envoy at Independence Day fete

10/21/2026 08:50 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi (陳明祺), left, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' ambassador to Taiwan Kenton Chance.CNA photo Oct. 21, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 21 (CNA) The ambassador of St. Vincent and the Grenadines (SVG) to Taiwan on Wednesday called Taiwan a "faithful partner" that has helped his country develop and prosper, as the Caribbean nation marked the 47th anniversary of its independence at a reception in Taipei.

"Today, we pay tribute to our developmental partners, the countries, international agencies and organizations that have contributed and continue to contribute to our development over the last 47 years," Ambassador Kenton Chance said in his address.

"In this regard, I express particular gratitude to the Republic of China (Taiwan), which has been a faithful partner over the last 45 years," he said.

Chance also urged his compatriots to learn from Taiwan's success.

"My fellow Vincentians, Taiwanese today enjoy the fruits of the hard work of their forebears while building an even more resilient and prosperous country for the next generation," he said.

"I urge every Vincentian in Taiwan to take inspiration from our host and build sacrificially so the next generation can experience in St. Vincent and the Grenadines a level of development similar to what we enjoy now in Taiwan," he added.

Representing the Taiwanese government at the reception, Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi (陳明祺) wished the Caribbean ally a happy Independence Day.

Chen said 2026 also marks the 45th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

"Throughout these years, our two nations have developed a close friendship built on mutual trust, shared values, and meaningful cooperation," he said.

Looking ahead, Chen said Taiwan was committed to deepening its partnership with SVG, particularly in economic cooperation, tourism and agriculture.

"By working together in these areas, we hope to create new opportunities for our local businesses, support economic growth, and bring lasting benefits to both our peoples," Chen added.

SVG is one of 12 countries that maintain diplomatic relations with the Republic of China, Taiwan's official name. The two countries established diplomatic ties on Aug. 15, 1981.

(By Joseph Yeh)

title: Takaichi’s history remarks aim to smooth the path to a meeting with Xi, Taiwanese expert says
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that her Cabinet would uphold the position expressed in the Murayama Statement. A Taiwanese expert said the remark was a conciliatory sig
content:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that her Cabinet would uphold the position expressed in the Murayama Statement. A Taiwanese expert said the remark was a conciliatory signal to Beijing as Tokyo seeks a meeting between Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) in November.
**Murayama Statement**

Asked about her views on history at a House of Councillors Budget Committee meeting on Oct. 16, Takaichi [said](https://tchina.kyodonews.net/articles/-/14976?words=%E6%9D%91%E5%B1%B1%E8%AB%87%E8%A9%B1) that, as stated in the 70th-anniversary statement marking the end of World War II, the positions of successive Japanese Cabinets would remain unchanged under her administration.

She said this included the 1995 Murayama Statement, issued on Aug. 15 that year by then Prime Minister Tomiichi Murayama.

The statement was the first in which the Japanese government officially acknowledged that Japan’s wartime aggression and colonial rule caused great damage and suffering in Asian countries, and expressed deep remorse and heartfelt apology.

 Chinese President Xi Jinping meets Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Gyeongju, South Korea, on the afternoon of Oct. 31, 2025. (Ministry of Foreign Affairs PRC)

**A conciliatory signal?**
This year’s APEC summit will be held in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18–19. Whether Xi and Takaichi will meet during the summit has drawn attention.

Takaichi [confirmed](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/10/18/japan/politics/takaichi-china-apec-parliament/) plans to attend the China-hosted APEC leaders' summit pending Diet clearance, signaling a readiness to engage Beijing in person despite deeply strained bilateral ties.

Kuo

Yu~~-~~jen (郭育仁), director of the Institute of China and Asia-Pacific Studies at National Sun Yat-sen University, told TCN that Japan was working to arrange a meeting between the two leaders. Takaichi’s pledge to uphold the Murayama Statement ahead of APEC, he said, was a gesture of goodwill toward Beijing.
Given Beijing’s recent posture, a formal bilateral meeting remains improbable, Kuo said, suggesting that any encounter would likely be choreographed as a "chance meeting" in the corridors.

Should no interaction take place at all, he said, it would signal that already strained Tokyo-Beijing relations are continuing to deteriorate.

**A Taiwan contingency is a Japan contingency**

In November 2025, Takaichi told Japan’s House of Representatives that a Chinese armed assault on Taiwan—such as a naval blockade enforced with military force—could be deemed a "survival-threatening situation" under Japanese security laws. Such a determination, she noted, could legally permit the Self-Defense Forces to exercise limited collective self-defense, provided other legal requirements were met.

Beijing responded with retaliatory measures, cooling cultural exchanges, dampening outbound tourism to Japan, re-imposing a ban on Japanese seafood, and restricting exports of dual-use goods to Japanese military users and for military uses, including uses that contribute to Japan’s military capabilities. China’s dual-use control list covers roughly 1,100 items, including critical minerals such as rare earths, gallium, and germanium.

Kuo said Takaichi’s commitment to the Murayama Statement did not mean she was retracting her “Taiwan contingency, Japan contingency” remarks, adding that the two issues were unrelated.

Pointing to enduring structural rifts over history, the disputed Diaoyu (Senkaku) Islands, and cross-strait issues, Kuo noted that Takaichi previously stated in parliament that Tokyo refrains from commenting on Taiwan's status under international law because Japan has renounced sovereignty over the island.

Kuo said the remarks indirectly touched on the “undetermined status of Taiwan” theory, which Beijing opposes, but should not be conflated with Takaichi’s earlier comments about a Taiwan contingency.

 A China Coast Guard officer observes the Diaoyu Islands from aboard a patrol vessel. (CCG)

**Xi-Takaichi meeting could signal easing tensions**
Kuo said a meeting between Xi and Takaichi at APEC was unlikely, but that Beijing also had an interest in easing tensions with Tokyo amid the current international environment.

Kuo pointed out that,ahead of Japan’s year-end revisions to its National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program, the Japan Innovation Party has called for the blueprints to endorse nuclear-powered submarines and create an exception to Tokyo's Three Non-Nuclear Principles to permit US nuclear-armed assets entry during contingencies.

Pointing out that the APEC summit coincides with coalition-level preparations to deliver defense recommendations to Takaichi, Kuo noted that Tokyo could deploy flexible terminology like "consider" in the revised security documents to retain strategic room for maneuver.

While such defense debates risk antagonizing Beijing, they could paradoxically create openings for renewed bilateral dialogue, Kuo argued. Tokyo’s public discourse on nuclear-powered submarines and potential exemptions to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles may function as a calculated form of strategic signaling toward China, he added.

Beyond the defense document updates, Kuo noted, Takaichi has set her sights on a major constitutional overhaul next year. The four-point reform agenda targets enshrining the legal status of the Self-Defense Forces in pacifist Article 9, creating executive emergency authorities during national crises, ending merged House of Councillors constituencies to ensure representation for each prefecture, and improving educational access.

Kuo said China would not want Japan to revise Article 9 and might therefore seek to coordinate with Tokyo on the matter.

**Japan-Taiwan security cooperation**

Regardless of whether Tokyo and Beijing break the ice on the sidelines of APEC, the direct military threat China poses to Japan remains fundamentally unaltered, Kuo said.

Looking ahead, he predicted that Japan’s updated security documents, due by year-end, will define its stance on security cooperation with Taiwan with unprecedented clarity.

Even if Japan-China relations ease temporarily, Kuo said, Takaichi is unlikely to change her policy toward Taiwan and remains strongly inclined to advance security cooperation with the island.

 In April 2025, Japanese lawmaker Sanae Takaichi led a delegation to visit Taiwan and posed for a photo with Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍). (MOFA Facebook)

**Taiwan should proceed cautiously**
Kuo said a substantive improvement in Japan-China relations would be difficult under Takaichi’s administration.

Since November last year, he said, China has restricted group travel to Japan and rare-earth supplies, sought to court Japanese opposition parties and factions outside the mainstream of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, and criticized Takaichi in international forums, putting pressure on her.

Despite Takaichi’s push to deepen economic, technological, and defense alignment with Taiwan, Kuo noted she remains constrained at home by pushback from career diplomats, business interests, opposition parties, and rival ruling-party factions.

Takaichi remains exceedingly unlikely to walk back her statements regarding a Taiwan contingency, Kuo noted. Given the resulting pressure from Beijing and domestic critics, cultivating a close, steadfast rapport with US President Donald Trump has become paramount to underwriting her security agenda, Kuo added.

Kuo urged Taipei to recognize the practical constraints shaping Japan’s cross-strait policy, noting that bilateral cooperation has traditionally advanced most effectively out of the public eye.

Taiwan should respect Tokyo’s appetite for discretion rather than pressing for high-profile diplomatic milestones, allowing practical partnerships to develop steadily beneath the political radar, Kuo added.

title: South Africa’s digital ID system and green book phase-out
summary: _“South Africa is actually building the next evolution of that kind of digital identity system... what we are doing is we are now credentialising your identity in a verifiable format, where at the moment the_[_Estonian solution_](https://ww
content:
_“South Africa is actually building the next evolution of that kind of digital identity system... what we are doing is we are now credentialising your identity in a verifiable format, where at the moment the_[_Estonian solution_](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-05-28-digital-dispatch-from-estonia-the-egovernance-capital-of-the-world/)_is card-based ... what we are doing is now made in a purely digital format that’s on your smartphone.”_

That was the explanation Lohan Spies, founder of DIDx, gave when Daily Maverick asked his views on the cooperation between Estonia and South Africa in this digital public infrastructure (DPI) journey.

You can trust him because DIDx is, by its own admission in the bio the company’s PR sent over ahead of our meeting in Techno Park, “a technology-based business that builds Africa’s trusted digital identity and payments infrastructure”.

Spies, a cybersecurity veteran who was building with blockchain before it was cool, founded the company in 2019 and established it as the continent’s most experienced builder of decentralised identity infrastructure.

He also shares Communications Minister Solly Malatsi’s sentiment that Estonia is “a reference point for a lot of DPI development that is happening, and there’s nothing wrong with observing best practice and how it can be useful for our context”.

Spies independently confirmed the minister’s claims that what we are building in South Africa is “not just a cut and paste … because the environments are different, and societal digital skills proficiency is also different”.

Someone [owes the Estonian ambassador an apology](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-23-estonian-echoes-sas-digital-public-infrastructure-looks-like-it-was-made-in-estonia/).

### **Show, don’t tell**

South Africa is undergoing a comprehensive digital migration designed to overhaul how civil registration, national security and public service delivery function. It’s anchored by the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) strategy for 2025-2030, with the primary objective of transitioning from an inefficient, paper-heavy legacy system into a digital-first organisation under the banner of “Home Affairs @ home”.

This transformation leverages the DPI infrastructure of a secure digital identity framework, an automated risk engine, data-exchange channels and mobile credentials to grant every South African secure identity authentication from smartphone devices or partner facilities.

According to Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber, “digital IDs enable instant, paperless processing for banking, work visas and business registrations through an automated risk engine, eliminating months of administrative delays”.

That DHA Strategic Plan reveals that attracting highly skilled workers and streamlining access to work visas can significantly boost economic output; bringing in 11,000 skilled workers annually adds 1.2% to annual GDP growth, while a 10% increase in tourism (through a digitised travel visa system) adds 0.6% to GDP.

And before we start marching (and marching), a digitally authenticated population register linked to the automated biometric identification system prevents illicit entries, fraudulent citizenship acquisition and internal collusion.

When demonstrating the live working prototype using his personal record on the population register, Schreiber emphasised that digital credentials would restore transparency and dignity.

He also confirmed that “on the 31st of March 2028 the Green ID book will officially cease to be recognised as a valid form of identification in terms of section 251B of the Identification Act”.

### **All the pieces clicking together**

Addressing GovTech on behalf of the Presidency’s Digital Services Unit within Operation Vulindlela, Kule Duma detailed the foundational mechanics of South Africa’s Digital Transformation Roadmap.

> “The experience of someone going to a government office is often layered by bureaucracy... They often must borrow money as a first stop, or they must use the very grants that we pay them ... jump on two or three taxis ... get into that long line and at the end they’re told you don’t have the sufficient documentation... We know that we can bring digital services to the tip of people’s fingers.”

He also articulated the central solution: “How should one person experience this one government and one government service ... if I provide government my information once, you shouldn’t have to ask me for that information ... that is the way that we drive it through the data exchange.”

Kule Duma on stage at GovTech 2026. (Photo: Lindsey Schutters)

Spies explained the details as best he understands them – DIDx is doing work in an SA Revenue Service skunkworks project, but his experience of these systems bridges the gap.erv

“DHA will be an issuer, and DHA will issue me with my verifiable credential in [mDoc format](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/digital-identities-getting-know-verifiable-digital-credential-0),” he says. “Once I then issue that credential to the holder, which is me, the citizen, that then lives in my mobile device, and on the mobile device we make use of the secure enclave on the device. So we make use of what the OEM manufacturer provides us ... to protect the private keys.”

It’s simple, actually, and Schreiber’s demo, erm … demonstrated it perfectly. “In that demo, the reality is they actually move the data by Bluetooth phone to phone,” Spies points out.

“So there’s no third party involved in that at all ... the security there is literally in proximity. It’s directly Bluetooth phone to phone ... you can be completely offline and I can share my credentials.”

### **Goodbye, green mamba**

The paper-based green ID book lacks modern cryptographic security and embedded biometrics. It is easily forged, altered, or duplicated by criminal syndicates, making it the primary vehicle for identity theft and impersonation.

Green ID books also cannot support automated online authentication, remote Know-Your-Customer checks for banks, or digital wallet credentials required for e-commerce and integrated public services.

The solutions being built like Schreiber’s Home Affairs @ home and the Presidency’s MyMzansi app propose a world where citizens can request, renew or authenticate civic identity products (IDs, birth/marriage certificates, passports) online using facial recognition on a mobile phone or computer, with physical cards delivered directly to their doorstep.

The green South African ID book is being phased out in favour of a digital ID system. (Photo: trying2 [adult.com](http://adult.com/) / Wikipedia)

By transferring routine transactions to digital self-service channels, we no longer lose full working days or pay transport costs standing in the queue at Home Affairs offices.

And all that is built on the foundation of a digital ID that anchors the experience with state platforms, including tax compliance with the SA Revenue Service, social grant distribution through Sassa, healthcare records and digital payment systems.

And the future is being built by South Africans. **DM**

針對上述案件，吳崢在民進黨中執會後記者會表示，相信民眾看到這件事情都會非常震驚，此事的本質已近乎恐怖主義的跨國鎮壓，且這位演員不是公職人員、從政者，只是一位在台灣享受言論自由的台灣人民。

吳崢指出，中國竟然連台灣人在台灣的言論也要管、甚至買凶進行這種極度殘暴的行為，相信所有台灣人民絕對不能接受，這已嚴重踩到台灣的國安、治安以及民主法治的紅線。

吳崢說，中國對台灣不論是介選、認知作戰，到現在直接買凶攻擊，意圖使民眾的人身安全受到損傷，這都凸顯中共對台灣干預及介入的力道越來越加強、殘暴。

吳崢認為，台灣不分黨派、支持台灣自由民主的政治工作者，都應齊聲、同聲譴責中共這種令人髮指的暴行，也拜託民眾參與選舉活動、行使自由民主的權利時，一定要多加留意，保護自己的人身安全，行政團隊也會盡全力做好相關因應與應變。

民進黨中國部於臉書撰文，嚴厲譴責中共當局毫不遮掩的流氓行徑，並正告北京當局，立即停止各項跨國鎮壓與對台灣人民威脅的惡劣行徑，台灣人民的生命安全與言論自由，絕不容許任何境外勢力任意侵犯。

此外，陸劇「逐玉」男主角張凌赫申請來台被拒，中國國台辦發言人張晗稱，大陸演藝人員赴台開展文化交流，是「兩岸民眾樂見並期盼的民間往來，有利於增進兩岸民眾相互了解」。民進黨政府拒不同意有關大陸演藝人員赴台交流，這有損兩岸文化交流，應摒棄政治操弄，取消不合理限制。

吳崢說，陸委會已清楚說明此事。出入境管理本來就是國家主權的象徵，例如他10幾年前參加完學運，跟青年夥伴申請港簽時也是直接被拒絕，這都是各國會有的管理作為。

吳崢指出，國台辦希望台灣行政團隊重視台灣粉絲心願，看來國台辦現在也感受到「民主是個好東西」，中國人民在網路上也表達希望中國民主化等心願，值得國台辦參考。

title: US Grapples With China-Linked Critical Minerals Shortfall Left Unresolved By Trump-Xi Summit
summary: WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals e
content:
WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals export restrictions that have roiled Pentagon and commercial supply chains alike.

Trump and Xi agreed to extend a trade truce -- set to expire on November 10 -- by two months. But the extension doesn’t address Washington’s core concerns about inadequate minerals exports from China.

During testimony in July before the Senate Finance Committee, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that China’s mineral exports are “not as much as we would want. It’s not at the pace we would want.”

#### SEE ALSO:

[Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict](https://www.rferl.org/a/trump-xi-summit-iran-war-china-hormuz-nuclear-trade/33757431.html "SEE ALSO: Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict")

China dominates global production and refining of critical minerals and rare earth permanent magnets, which retain their magnetic properties indefinitely without the need for external power. Rare earth permanent magnets are essential for the functionality of everything from electrical vehicle motors and wind turbines to fighter jets and missile guidance systems.

The International Energy Agency (IEA), an autonomous intergovernmental organization based in Paris, estimates that China is the top refiner for 19 out of 20 key strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent.

China has an even tighter grip on permanent magnets with a 94 percent global market share, according to the IEA.

Beijing has weaponized its critical minerals dominance to counter US sanctions on its semiconductor sector and the Trump administration’s tariffs. It has calibrated the export controls to inflict maximum pressure on Pentagon supply chains while avoiding large-scale disruption to consumer industries, which would risk escalation with Washington that China’s ruling Communist Party (CCP) does not want.

Overall, China exported 512 metric tons of rare-earth permanent magnets to the US in August, down 21 percent from July and 13 percent from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data.

Heading into the summit, Xi sought to leverage China’s strategic metals dominance to secure a lasting trade truce with the United States, says Tomasz Nadrowski, portfolio manager at the New York-based Amvest Terraden Critical Minerals Fund.

“China has this spigot that it can turn on and off -- which determines the flow of critical minerals to the US and other countries,” he told RFE/RL in an interview.

“Extending the trade truce two years would have given this tool additional value,” further locking in US dependency on China’s critical mineral supply chains.

The Trump administration was concerned that with a two-year truce, “everyone [both commercial and defense manufacturers] would relax and think, 'We don’t need to build any new capacity,” he says.

#### SEE ALSO:

[China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy](https://www.rferl.org/a/china-central-asia-wang-yi-diplomacy-minerals-mining-kyrgyzstan-debt/33597375.html "SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy")

“The US cannot afford to accept strategic chokepoint dependencies for inputs that are essential to our defense industrial base and foundational industries like automotive,” Mahnaz Khan, vice president of policy for critical supply chains at the Silverado Policy Accelerator in Washington, said in an interview.

The two-month truce agreed to by Trump and Xi “buys the United States time, but it doesn’t eliminate the underlying vulnerability,” she said

## **Partnering With Central Asia**

As it works to reduce critical minerals dependence on China, the Trump administration has cast a wide net. In an August [**fact sheet**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/08/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-announces-billions-in-new-deals-and-investments-to-power-american-mining/), the White House said it has signed or approved more than 160 mineral deals since January 2025, totaling about $40 billion.

While the administration prioritizes domestic minerals production, in some cases, overseas projects are more feasible. This holds true for tungsten, which the United States has not produced at home since 2015. Tungsten is a crucial input for military-grade steel, aerospace components, munitions, and ground vehicle armor. Given its high density, the metal is used for stabilization and control in missiles and aircraft.

Tungsten’s importance for defense led the Trump administration to throw its support behind a $1.1 billion project in Kazakhstan. Under an agreement signed in November 2025 between US-based Cove Capital (now known as the Cove Kaz Capital Group) and the state-run Kazakh mining company Tau-Ken Samruk, the two parties will jointly develop one of the world’s largest tungsten resources.

“Kazakhstan made a conscious political choice to make an award to a US company, though rumor has it that China was also bidding for the same project,” Akbota Karibayeva Meyer, a research fellow at the Caspian Policy Center in Washington, told RFE/RL. The decision exemplifies Kazakhstan’s multi-vector foreign policy, which aims to preserve strategic autonomy by balancing ties with major powers, she explains.

#### SEE ALSO:

[US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise](https://www.rferl.org/a/us-georgia-black-sea-iran-trump-trade/33727854.html "SEE ALSO: US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise ")

Drilling, feasibility studies, and site preparation began after the agreement’s formal closing. Yet full commercial production is several years away.

“Are these projects in Kazakhstan viable? Sure, they’re viable. The economics are very hard to pencil out without a subsidy, though,” Ian Lange, a professor at the Colorado School of Mines and deputy director of its Critical Materials Innovation Hub, said in an interview.

“Ideally, I might want to do something [in terms of a mining investment] that limits the government’s expenditure and provides for some competition,” he says.

The Trump administration is also working with Uzbekistan to source critical minerals.

In February, the US commodities firm Traxys signed a $1 billion deal with the Uzbek government focused on the exploration and extraction of tungsten, molybdenum, and copper. This agreement aligns with a separate critical minerals pact reached between the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Uzbekistan.

Elsewhere in Central Asia, the potential for cooperation with the US exists. Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan both have major reserves of antimony, a critical mineral used as a flame retardant, an alloying agent for lead, and a compound in semiconductors.

During a September visit to Bishkek, US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor and US Senator Steve Daines, chairman of the Senate Central Asia Caucus, discussed mining cooperation with Kyrgyz officials.

#### SEE ALSO:

[China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy](https://www.rferl.org/a/china-central-asia-wang-yi-diplomacy-minerals-mining-kyrgyzstan-debt/33597375.html "SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy")

During their trip, they also met with the presidents of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikstan.

While the US continues to make progress sourcing critical minerals from Central Asia, “it is important to recognize the limiting factor of geography,” Karibayeva Meyer says.

Given its proximity to Central Asia, “it is much easier for China to be involved in the region.”

## **Short And Long-Term Challenges**

In the short term, the US faces a key hurdle in its critical minerals diversification push: from January 1, 2027, the Pentagon will prohibit the use of certain metals sourced from the “foreign adversary countries” of China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran.

The ban, outlined in [**Executive Order 14415**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/07/securing-americas-defense-supply-chains-and-ensuring-domestic-acquisition-of-critical-materials/), sharply narrows the possibility of receiving waivers for the use of rare-earth magnets, tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum from those four nations. Defense firms can no longer be granted a waiver based on cost or convenience reasons. To receive one, they must show that compliant materials are completely unavailable despite exhaustive efforts to source them.

The Aerospace Industries Association (AIA), a Washington-based trade association, said in a [**recent report**](https://www.aia-aerospace.org/publications/strengthening-critical-minerals-supply-chains/) that some of its member companies expect to achieve compliance for certain applications by January 1. Others may need until 2028 or later, given the paucity of compliant aerospace-grade material for several covered materials.

AIA recommends that the Trump administration align compliance requirements with supply chain readiness and preserve flexible waiver authorities.

Lange of the Colorado School of Mines says that the administration may offer defense firms some additional leeway.

In the longer term, analysts say that the United States must focus greater effort on critical minerals processing. Decades of outsourcing production to China have resulted in high regulatory costs, a shortage of specialized metallurgical expertise and a dearth of commercial-scale downstream facilities.

**“**I do see processing as the top, most enduring impediment to large-scale diversification away from China,” Cory Combs, head of critical mineral and supply chain research at the consultancy Trivium China, told RFE/RL.

“Mining is generally much less technologically complex. Processing is where the most critical know-how bottlenecks lie. China's own experience, with decades spent building its processing capabilities, reflects the challenge,” he says.

He further notes that the US lacks strong demand signals in the parts of the production chain between processed minerals and end uses, which limits the scale of offtake agreements necessary to properly fund processing expansions.

Given long project lead times, permitting bottlenecks and capital constraints, analysts expect that Washington will need more than a decade to develop a midstream critical minerals supply chain not dependent on China.

In the meantime, Beijing will aim to exploit that continued dependency to deter the US from imposing further curbs on its development of advanced technologies integral to semiconductors and artificial intelligence.

So far, it has been successful.

Earlier this year, the Trump administration delayed adding more than 100 Chinese firms to the Commerce Department Entity List -- a trade and export blacklist -- because of concern over how Beijing might further throttle rare earth shipments.

China’s continuing dominance of critical minerals could also constrain Washington’s ability to intervene in a Taiwan Strait crisis.

A [**Heritage Foundation report**](https://www.heritage.org/tidalwave/chapters/chapter-6-assessing-the-us-indo-pacific-munitions-system)published in January warns that if China fully weaponizes its export restrictions at the onset of a war, the US could deplete existing stockpiles of minerals needed to produce new advanced munitions in under 90 days.

title: 康乃尔大学轮奸案：Jane Doe 称校长质疑她提出的指控
summary: 图像来源，Reuters 图像加注文字，康乃尔大学的教职员在上周的教务委员会会议上就学校处理性侵案件的方式进行了辩论。 * * Author, 纳尔丁·萨阿德（Nardine Saad） * Author, 普拉蒂克莎·吉尔迪亚尔（Pratiksha Ghildial） * Published 2 小时前 * 阅读时间: 3 分钟 一名康奈尔大学前学生声称，自己在一所兄弟会会所（fraternity house）遭多人轮奸。她表示校长的反应令她感到“得不到支持，也不被相信”。
content:
图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，康乃尔大学的教职员在上周的教务委员会会议上就学校处理性侵案件的方式进行了辩论。

*       *   Author, 纳尔丁·萨阿德（Nardine Saad）

    *   Author, 普拉蒂克莎·吉尔迪亚尔（Pratiksha Ghildial）

*   Published 2 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

一名康奈尔大学前学生声称，自己在一所兄弟会会所（fraternity house）遭多人轮奸。她表示校长的反应令她感到“得不到支持，也不被相信”。

这名女学生以 Jane Doe （女性无名氏）名义发函，指控校长米高·科特利科夫（Michael Kotlikoff）曾质问她，为何事发数星期后才报案。

这所位于纽约州北部的常春藤联盟（Ivy League）院校表示，该前学生对校长反应的描述“并不正确”。

Jane Doe 把信件寄给校内教职员。本月，教职员将就科特利科夫的表现举行罕见的投票。Jane Doe 上月入禀法院提出诉讼，指控自己在2024年10月参加 Chi Phi 兄弟会派对时遭多名男子强奸。

视频加注文字，全美各地“我是 Jane Doe”抗议活动呼吁停止性暴力（英文影片）

Jane Doe 指控七名前兄弟会成员。BBC的美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）联络他们时，七人全部否认有不当行为。目前没有任何人因此被刑事起诉。

Jane Doe 曾向校园警察报案，当地检察官当时决定不提出起诉，但案件其后已重新展开调查。

康奈尔大学回应 Jane Doe 最初提出的指控时表示，校方已展开内部调查，并进行民权调查。

BBC 取得一封日期为10月14日、共两页的信件。Jane Doe 在信中告诉教务委员会（faculty senate），在她举报强奸事件后，透过他人得知科特利科夫的反应。她表示，校长“最初的反应”大致是：“她为甚么等了这么久才举报事件？”

Jane Doe 于11月8日向校园警察报案，距离她参加兄弟会派对约三星期后。

她指出，科特利科夫曾与她所属姊妹会（sorority）的时任主席交谈，当时亦有其他职员在场。其中至少一人似乎对这名大学校长提出的问题“感到不安”。

Jane Doe 在信中写道：“这削弱了我对校方行政团队的信心。我原本希望、亦期望这所曾是我的梦想学校，能够以理解、敏感和公平的态度看待我的经历，但这件事令我对校方能否做到这一点失去信心。”

她表示，自己写这封信，是希望教职员在10月28日就是否通过对科特利科夫领导层的不信任动议投票前，能够“作出知情的选择”。

大学证实已收到 Jane Doe 律师寄来的信件。

但康奈尔大学发言人向 BBC 表示：“信件提及，科特利科夫校长在2025年1月的一次会议上提出的问题，其相关描述来自他人转述。而根据一份有文件记录、由亲历者提供的第一手说法，这个描述并不正确。”

视频加注文字，“我感到非常震惊”——大学生们对康乃尔大学强暴案调查的反应（英文影片）

发言人表示，科特利科夫就涉嫌强奸事件延迟被举报一事提出的问题，“是针对当时在场的旁观者，而不是 Jane Doe”。发言人指出，尽管2024年10月事件发生后，社交媒体上一直有相关讨论，但旁观者并没有使用康奈尔大学的匿名举报专线。

发言人说：“他质疑的并不是 Jane Doe 报案一事。”

科特利科夫领导这所位于伊萨卡（Ithaca）的学府已有26年。上星期三（14日），他在教务委员会上接受了一连串尖锐提问。

BBC 取得的会议录音显示，教职员对科特利科夫处理案件的方式表示“深感不安”，并指他缺乏“情感上的反应”。

科特利科夫则列举校方因应 Jane Doe 指控而推行的改革，包括禁止举办兄弟会派对。

他说：“对于2024年10月在康奈尔大学发生的事件，我们所有人都感到极度难过。”

康奈尔大学教务委员会是校内的管治机构，由教授及其他学术人员组成。委员会已安排于10月28日就科特利科夫的领导表现进行不信任投票。

会议录音显示，教职员指出校园内的性不当行为是一个系统性问题，需要“从制度层面予以重视”。

支持提出不信任动议的劳工史教授保罗·奥尔蒂斯（Prof Paul Ortiz）表示，学生曾告诉教职员，他们“天黑后走到图书馆都感到不安全”。

他指控康奈尔大学把强奸事件当成“更像是一个‘公关问题’，而不是一宗令人发指的罪行”来处理。

# 美国制裁前谷歌工程师丁林葳创办的公司和奇绩创坛四个主体 中国商务部说坚决反对

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月21日 08:52

美国国务院10月19日根据《保护美国知识产权法》，以涉嫌窃取美国人的商业秘密为由，制裁与中国公民、前谷歌软件工程师丁林葳有关联的五家实体：丁林葳2023年在中国创办的上海至算科技有限公司，以及奇绩创坛北京投资管理有限责任公司、北京奇绩创坛一期和二期创业投资中心、北京奇绩创坛致远企业管理中心。受影响的是这五家实体和与这五家实体往来的美国人：美国财政部外国资产控制办公室同一天把这五家实体列入非SDN菜单式制裁清单，措施包括冻结这些实体的全部财产和财产权益，除进口货物外禁止与这些实体的一切交易，并另发通用许可证，允许结束涉及这些被冻结实体的交易。

国务院说，这次制裁是在司法部和联邦调查局调查丁林葳之后作出的；美国联邦陪审团今年1月29日裁定丁林葳犯有七项盗窃商业秘密罪，他被裁定窃取了数千页包含谷歌超级智能相关技术商业秘密的机密信息，为自己和设在中国的科技公司牟利。按指控，丁林葳在2023年12月辞职前不到两个星期，把2000多页商业秘密转到个人云端账户；至算科技自称能开发加快机器学习运算的软件平台，包括用超级计算芯片训练大型超级智能模型。奇绩创坛的前身是创业孵化器Y Combinator 2018年开设、由前微软和百度高管陆奇主持的中国业务；Y Combinator 2019年11月关闭中国业务后，陆奇把团队独立出来，成立了奇绩创坛。

丁林葳案和奇绩创坛的几个时间点

1.   2018年 Y Combinator开设中国业务，由陆奇主持
2.   2019年11月 Y Combinator关闭中国业务，陆奇把团队独立出来，成立奇绩创坛
3.   2023年 丁林葳在中国创办上海至算科技有限公司
4.   2023年12月 按指控，丁林葳辞职前不到两个星期，把2000多页商业秘密转到个人云端账户
5.   2026年1月29日 美国联邦陪审团裁定丁林葳犯有七项盗窃商业秘密罪
6.   2026年10月19日 美国国务院制裁与丁林葳有关联的五家实体
7.   2026年10月20日 中国商务部回应说坚决反对，敦促美方纠正

数据：美国国务院、美国司法部和中国商务部的说法，据媒体报道

中国商务部新闻发言人10月20日回应说，美方炒作所谓“窃取商业秘密”问题，污名化中国企业并实施制裁，严重损害中国企业合法权益，中方坚决反对；发言人说，中国人工智能企业的快速发展得益

summary: 香港 香港卫生署突击搜查四家美容店，检获超过100瓶疑似毒药和70瓶未经注册的产品，其中包括20瓶声称含有人体组织的Elravie Re2O。一名38岁女子被捕。官员警告该产品缺乏安全数据和 vio [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 21 日04:41 HKT · 2 分钟读 卫生署突击搜查四家美容服务场所
content:
香港
香港卫生署突击搜查四家美容店，检获超过100瓶疑似毒药和70瓶未经注册的产品，其中包括20瓶声称含有人体组织的Elravie Re2O。一名38岁女子被捕。官方警告该产品缺乏安全数据和vio

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 21 日 04:41 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

卫生署10月21日宣布，突击搜查尖沙咀、旺角、荃湾及元朗四间美容服务场所，检获超过100瓶怀疑第1部注射用毒药及超过70瓶怀疑未经注册注射用药剂制品。

查获的物品中有 20 瓶名为 Elravie Re2O 的产品，用韩文包装，声称含有人体组织。一名38岁女子在旺角处所与警方联合行动中被捕，涉嫌非法管有第1部毒药及未经注册药剂制品，以及涉嫌非法商业买卖人体器官。
卫生署规管事务总监冯英医生表示，该产品根据《人体器官移植条例》被列为“受规管产品”，而根据《药剂业及毒药条例》被列为“药剂制品”。卫生署已收到有关受管制产品的豁免申请并正在处理，但尚未获得豁免。尚未收到该产品作为药品的注册申请。

冯医生表示，该产品缺乏临床安全数据，对公众健康构成潜在风险，卫生署已致函所有医生和私营医疗机构，提醒他们遵守法例。由人体组织制造的产品属于《人体器官移植条例》下的受规管产品，并须在销售前获得卫生署署长批准的豁免。

违反《人体器官移植条例》的罪犯，首次定罪可处罚款港币 50,000 元及监禁三个月，再定罪则可处罚款港币 100,000 元及监禁一年。根据《药剂业及毒药条例》，非法供应或管有未经注册药剂制品或第1部毒药，每次犯罪最高可被罚款港币100,000元及监禁两年。
卫生署已将其他涉嫌销售非豁免受管制产品的案件移交警方。 2023年至2026年9月，药物办公室共处理108宗涉及售卖或管有未经注册药剂制品的定罪案件，最重刑罚为监禁10个月，最高罚款为港币242,000元。

冯医生提醒市民，注射手术属于医疗程序，只应由注册医生或牙医进行，市民应核实医生的资格，不要因为打针被宣传为美容疗法而认为注射没有风险。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Hong Kong's Department of Health raided four beauty premises, seizing over 100 vials of suspected poisons and 70 vials of unregistered products, including 20 vials of Elravie Re2O claiming to contain human tissue. A 38-year-old woman was arrested. Officials warn the product lacks safety data and vio

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

21 Oct 2026 at 04:41 HKT · 2 min read

The Department of Health (DH) has raided four beauty service premises in Tsim Sha Tsui, Mong Kok, Tsuen Wan and Yuen Long, seizing over 100 vials of suspected Part 1 poisons for injection and more than 70 vials of suspected unregistered pharmaceutical products for injection, the agency announced on 21 October.

Among the seized items were 20 vials of a product called Elravie Re2O, packaged in Korean and claiming to contain human tissue. A 38-year-old woman was arrested during a joint operation with police at the Mong Kok premises on suspicion of unlawful possession of Part 1 poisons and unregistered pharmaceutical products, and suspected unlawful commercial dealing in human organs.

Dr Fung Ying, Controller for Regulatory Affairs at the DH, said the product is classified as a "regulated product" under the Human Organ Transplant Ordinance and as a "pharmaceutical product" under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance. The DH received an exemption application for the regulated product and is processing it, but no exemption has been granted. No registration application has been received for the product as a pharmaceutical product.

Dr Fung said the product lacks clinical safety data and poses potential public health risks, and that the DH has written to all doctors and private healthcare institutions reminding them to comply with the law. Products manufactured from human tissue are regulated products under the Human Organ Transplant Ordinance and require an exemption approved by the Director of Health before sale.

Offenders under the Human Organ Transplant Ordinance face a fine of HK$50,000 and three months' jail on first conviction, and HK$100,000 and one year's jail on subsequent conviction. Under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance, unlawful supply or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products or Part 1 poisons carries a maximum fine of HK$100,000 and two years' imprisonment per offence.

The DH has referred other cases involving alleged sale of non-exempted regulated products to police. From 2023 to September 2026, its Drug Office handled 108 convicted cases involving sale or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products, with the heaviest sentence at 10 months' jail and the highest fine at HK$242,000.

Dr Fung reminded the public that injection procedures are medical procedures and should only be performed by registered medical practitioners or dentists, and that people should verify a doctor's qualifications and not assume injections are risk-free because they are marketed as cosmetic treatments.

title: Steven Gruzd met alleged killers at Airbnb, court hears
summary: Almost seven months after the murder of senior researcher [Steven Gruzd](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-03-30-steven-gruzds-murder-highlights-express-kidnapping-spike-as-suspects-appear-in-court/), court details indicate he me
content:
Almost seven months after the murder of senior researcher [Steven Gruzd](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-03-30-steven-gruzds-murder-highlights-express-kidnapping-spike-as-suspects-appear-in-court/), court details indicate he met his assailants at an Airbnb in Corlett Gardens, Johannesburg, which they had booked and paid for, and where the murder allegedly took place.

Gruzd (53) was the head of the African Governance and Diplomacy Programme at the South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA). He was reported missing on Friday, 27 March, after he had left to attend a meeting in Corlett Gardens.

His body was found the following day at George Goch Hostel in Jeppestown, 20km away. A postmortem determined the cause of death to be blunt force trauma to the neck.

Five men were arrested on the day Gruzd’s body was found. Thabiso Ngcongco, Nkosenhle Zuma, Siyanda Mzolo, Buhle Zuma, and Nsikelelo Njali are facing charges of robbery with aggravating circumstances, kidnapping, murder, and defeating the ends of justice. They have all pleaded not guilty.

The George Goch Hostel, where the body of Steven Gruzd was found. (Photo: OJ Koloti / Gallo Images)

On Friday, 16 October, at the Johannesburg Central Magistrates’ Court, Lieutenant Colonel Johan Potgieter testified that the suspects’ fingerprints were found at the murder scene and inside a white Toyota Corolla driven by the assailants.

The police also found bloodstained linen from the murder scene and a rope with Gruzd’s DNA in the car. CCTV evidence showed the suspects and Gruzd entering the premises separately.

The case has been investigated as a suspected “express kidnapping”. This refers to a crime in which victims are held against their will while being forced by their assailants to withdraw cash from multiple ATMs and send cash transfers to other accounts.

These incidents are [the main driver](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-03-30-steven-gruzds-murder-highlights-express-kidnapping-spike-as-suspects-appear-in-court/?dm_source=blocks-horizontal&dm_medium=card-link&dm_campaign=inform&dm_position=4) of kidnappings in Gauteng, which records the highest kidnapping cases nationally.

Steven Gruzd speaking at the African Peer Review Mechanism. (Photo: X / @APRMorg)

The circumstances behind the death revealed in police evidence and through a Daily Maverick investigation point to an alarming trend in express kidnappings, about which LGBT+ activists have been raising the alarm since 2023.

The SA Police Service did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

### Possible links to online gangs

The police have not officially established how the accused and Gruzd knew each other, and they do not appear to have had an established relationship.

A Johannesburg resident, who requested anonymity, told Daily Maverick that he had matched with Gruzd on Grindr, a dating app for men who have sex with men. He confirmed that Gruzd, whom he also knew outside of the app, was “very active” on the site and regularly confided in him.

This detail, along with the circumstances of his murder, points to the possible involvement of criminal syndicates that create fake accounts on Grindr to lure men who have sex with men to secluded locations for robbery and extortion.

Associates of Gruzd have described him as a “devoted family man” to his wife and children.Daily Maverick was not able to reach his family for comment.

### ‘Grindr gangs’ documented since 2023

The online targeting of men who have sex with men is often linked to “Grindr gangs”. However, the term describes the tactic rather than a single, interconnected syndicate. Such gangs have been documented [in Nelson Mandela Bay](https://iol.co.za/news/2025-09-15-beaten-robbed-and-dumped-gay-men-lured-on-grindr-in-new-wave-of-attacks/), [Durban](https://www.mambaonline.com/2026/07/23/four-men-jailed-for-grindr-gang-kidnappings-and-robberies-in-ballito-umhlanga-and-durban-north/)and [Cape Town](https://iol.co.za/capeargus/news/2023-03-15-concern-over-grindr-gang-luring-sa-victims-on-hook-up-app-to-rob-assault-them/).

In 2023, seven men targeted a Wits University student on Grindr before [kidnapping and torturing](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-09-22-wits-kidnapping-police-probe-dozens-of-similar-cases/) him, demanding a R30,000 ransom from his family. Police rescued the student from Denver Men’s Hostel after arresting one of the captors while he attempted to withdraw the ransom money.

At the time, SAPS spokesperson Athlenda Mathe stated that the suspects were linked to [at least 85 similar cases](https://x.com/AthlendaM/status/1704764064017068135?s=48&t=PJpBansSH7jGLH5lIBJspQ).

This year, at least two similar incidents in Gauteng were reported. In early March, [Mamba Online](https://www.mambaonline.com/2026/03/02/community-alert-grindr-gang-attack-reported-in-randburg-johannesburg/) reported that a 43-year-old man was ambushed in a guesthouse by five men after he had agreed to meet a Grindr match.

His assailants forced him to hand over his phone, transferred money out of his bank account, tied him up, and threatened to publish explicit photos of him on social media if he “did anything stupid”.

In April, veteran emergency services worker [Braam Kruger](https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2026-05-22-pretoria-guesthouse-murder-three-suspects-from-kzn-granted-bail/)was murdered after being lured to a guesthouse in Brooklyn, Pretoria, by a [Grindr match](https://www.mambaonline.com/2026/05/25/fears-pretoria-guest-house-murder-may-be-linked-to-grindr-gang-criminals/). After he arrived, he was ambushed by three men, robbed and murdered.

Braam Kruger. (Source: Facebook)

The Johannesburg resident who knew Gruzd told Daily Maverick that he knew of at least one other incident where a man in a relationship with a woman went to meet a Grindr match only to be ambushed at gunpoint.

Details of such attacks are widely shared through informal community whisper networks, prompting some men to carry firearms for protection during initial in-person meetups with people they match with on the app.

He added that Grindr automatically erases message history for both users when one account blocks another – a feature that can further complicate criminal investigations.

Grindr had not responded to Daily Maverick’s questions by the time of publication.

The "Grindr" app logo is seen amongst other dating apps on a mobile phone screen. (Photo by Leon Neal/Getty Images)

### Cases underreported due to stigma

Sibonelo Ncanana-Trower, the co-chair of the National Task Team on Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Gender Expression, and Sex Characteristics Matters, confirmed a rise in “Grindr gang” incidents, particularly in Gauteng and Cape Town. He noted, however, that the true scale of the problem is probably underreported due to stigma and fear of being outed.

“Our significant concern is that the reported cases likely represent only a fraction of what is actually occurring. Many individuals are extremely fearful of opening cases with the police due to the risk of further harm, secondary victimisation, or being outed, especially in contexts where stigma and discrimination remain pervasive,” he said.

Mike Bolhuis. (Photo: mikebolhuis.co.za.)

### Sextortion on the increase

Private investigator Mike Bolhuis said he had observed a marked increase in sextortion cases across various dating platforms in recent months. In cases handled by his team, offenders routinely set up fraudulent, anonymous profiles to engage and exploit potential victims.

Perpetrators either coerce victims into sending explicit photos to use for blackmail, or lure them to private locations where they are ambushed, held captive, and extorted for money. In physical attacks, the criminals also take explicit photos of the victims, threatening to post them online if they contact the police – and frequently reselling them on the black market.

Bolhuis urged those who use dating sites to verify the identity of the person they have matched with before meeting in person by asking for full names and contact information.

“Because it’s a social media platform, you go through all the necessary other available platforms to find [their profiles]. The moment the person says he’s from overseas, it's a red flag,” he warned.

“When they start asking for money, it’s a red flag. If they don’t want to do a video call, it’s a problem. If they say, ‘Yeah, but I’m in the bath now, I don’t have any clothes,’ and you say, ‘I’ll hold on, put some clothes on.’ You know they come with stories,” he said. **DM**

title: Examining State-Level Legislation on Transnational Repression in the United States
summary: Transnational repression has become an increasingly visible public policy issue in the United States, and worldwide, over the past decade. The gruesome 2018 [murder](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-45812399) and dismemberment of Saudi
content:
Transnational repression has become an increasingly visible public policy issue in the United States, and worldwide, over the past decade. The gruesome 2018 [murder](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-45812399) and dismemberment of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi in the Saudi Consulate in Istanbul, the 2023 [assassination](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/08/murder-canada-sikh-activist-hardeep-singh-nijjar-indian-criminal-gang-leader-charged) of Canadian Sikh activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar outside of a British Columbia temple, and the 2025 [rendition](https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/case/one-year-after-his-arrest-human-rights-defender-hugues-comlan-sosoukpe-remains-custody) of Beninese journalist [Comlan Hugues Sossoukpè](https://cpj.org/data/people/comlan-hugues-sossoukpe/) from Côte d’Ivoire highlight the extent to which governments have brazenly targeted their nationals across borders.

Initially, the policy response in the United States occurred entirely at the federal level. But over the past several years, U.S. states have begun to consider legislation on the issue. Not all of this legislation has been adopted, and the U.S. state-level response is clearly in an early phase. As U.S. states continue to respond to transnational repression, it is important that state legislators – and ultimately, members of Congress – understand what the states have done and what can be learned from their various approaches.

One of the challenges of countering transnational repression is that it has not yet been defined in U.S. federal law. The democracy and rights organization [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/report/transnational-repression), which has played a leading role in drawing attention to the issue and in gathering data on it, defines transnational repression as “governments reaching across [national] borders to silence dissent among diaspora and exile communities.” (One of us, Grady, is a research analyst at Freedom House.) Perpetrator governments employ a range of tactics – including assassinations, illegal deportations, abductions, digital threats**,**and coercion-by-proxy – to intimidate and harass those who pose a perceived threat to the regime. Transnational repression can also involve the abuse by authoritarian regimes of legitimate international legal cooperation mechanisms such as [Interpol’s notice system](https://newlinesinstitute.org/intl-law-peace/how-the-abuse-of-interpol-contributes-to-transnational-repression/), [mutual legal assistance frameworks](https://www.ohchr.org/en/statements-and-speeches/2026/09/joint-statement-united-nations-human-rights-experts-transnational) and [counterterrorism financing structures](https://carnegieendowment.org/russia-eurasia/politika/2025/11/russia-eu-banking-exploits).

## **The Federal Response**

The federal response to transnational repression in the United States has been [varied](https://newlinesinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/FINAL_TNR-US_policy-report-nlisap.pdf). Numerous congressional committees have held hearings — including multiple hearings by the U.S. Helsinki Commission and most recently, and relevantly, the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC) June 4, 2026, [hearing](https://www.cecc.gov/events/hearings/prcs-threats-americans-transnational-repression-state-level-responses) on “The PRC’s Threats to Americans: Transnational Repression & State-Level Responses.” Federal law enforcement has regularly brought cases against perpetrators, and U.S. congressional offices have introduced several bills on transnational repression, including the [Transnational Repression Policy Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/2525/text) (TRPA). Yet, that bipartisan and bicameral legislation, which would codify a formal definition of the phenomenon into law and mandate the development of a government strategy to blunt the threat, has struggled to move on the Hill, given other legislative priorities.

U.S. administrations have also evaded the intent of the most significant U.S. legislation, Section 6503 of the 2022 National Defense Authorization Act, entitled “Transnational Repression Accountability and Prevention” or “[TRAP](https://www.congress.gov/117/plaws/publ81/PLAW-117publ81.pdf).” The provisions directed the Attorney General and Secretary of State to provide biannual reports to Congress on authoritarian governments’ misuse of Interpol’s systems, support reforms to prevent such abuse, and develop a coordinated U.S. response to this form of transnational repression. While the required [initial report](https://www.state.gov/transnational-repression-accountability-and-prevention-trap-act-reports) was submitted in August 2022, the TRAP provisions have not produced the sustained reporting, coordinated implementation, or broader accountability that Congress envisioned. The result is that, while the U.S. federal government has done more than any other government to raise awareness about transnational repression, its response has been neither unified nor consistent.

Indeed, the United States and other democracies continue to [facilitate](https://freedomhouse.org/report/special-report/2026/collaboration-and-resistance-tracking-transnational-repression-2025) transnational repression via their immigration and extradition systems by detaining and deporting dissidents. Part of the challenge is that, precisely because of the widespread participation of democracies in international legal cooperation, it is all too easy for perpetrator governments to abuse these systems to seek the return of exiled activists and dissidents. While those mechanisms require greater transparency and stronger safeguards against abuse, receiving countries must also ensure that they do not detain, extradite, or deport individuals based solely on uncorroborated allegations or requests from governments with a documented history of abusing these systems for political purposes.

By the same token, a great deal of transnational repression occurs outside of immigration enforcement, in the everyday lives of those targeted. Adhering to due process standards when adjudicating claims for asylum, while essential, will not protect individuals from surveillance, harassment, coercion, or intimidation by foreign regimes or their agents inside the United States. These are acts that can be addressed at the state level. Indeed, given the federal structure of the United States, leaving every offense to the federal government to criminalize is neither sensible nor safe. U.S. states, in addition to serving as legislative laboratories, can play a constructive role in responding to the challenge of transnational repression.

## **State Legislative History and Legal Mechanisms**

In recent years, state legislatures have increasingly taken steps to address foreign interference. In general, legislative initiatives have been broad, treating transnational repression, alongside land sales and [foreign lobbying campaigns](https://www.akingump.com/en/insights/alerts/state-level-foreign-influence-laws-begin-taking-effect), as increasingly serious national security concerns. These broad approaches have prompted some concerns about the potential for overreach. At a June hearing of the U.S House of Representatives Select Committee on China, the president of Asian Americans Advancing Justice, John C. Yang, [cautioned](https://www.congress.gov/119/meeting/house/119385/witnesses/HHRG-119-ZS00-Wstate-YangJ-20260625.pdf) that efforts to address foreign interference must avoid repeating historical instances of national security concerns leading to ethnicity-based suspicion rather than evidence-based enforcement.

Since the beginning of 2025, seven states have adopted laws that explicitly mention transnational repression and enact measures to respond to the phenomenon. While these laws vary to some extent in scope and approach, they reflect growing state-level attention to the problem.

In May 2025, Texas became the first state to pass legislation to counter transnational repression. [Senate Bill 1349](https://legiscan.com/TX/text/SB1349/id/3235301), signed into law by Governor Greg Abbott on May 24, 2025, and effective on September 1, 2025, criminalizes actions committed by a foreign government or terrorist organization, or an agent working on behalf of these entities, when the acts interfere with Texas residents’ protected conduct under the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution or in some way coerce a Texas resident to either work for a foreign principal or to [leave the United States](https://safeguarddefenders.com/en/blog/new-report-chasing-fox-hunt). The law also makes it illegal to enforce another country’s laws in the state. The sentencing enhancement for serving a foreign principal can be applied to pre-existing offenses in the Texas penal code, including assault, stalking, and human trafficking. The law also requires the Texas Department of Public Safety to create a training program for Texas law enforcement on common tactics and on the primary perpetrators of transnational repression, and requires the Department, in collaboration with the Governor’s office, to prepare a study on the issue.

While the law identifies how transnational repression infringes on the rights of affected individuals, it takes an overly expansive view of the perpetrators by including terrorist organizations. Unlike terrorist offenses, which usually attack state institutions or the public at large, government-directed campaigns are targeted against particular private individuals who, as individuals, have the rights the law seeks to protect. Moreover, the act incorrectly implies that terrorist organizations stably control territory and are recognized foreign principals.

Soon after Texas passed its law in 2025, Nebraska adopted the [_Crush Transnational Repression in Nebraska_](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/FloorDocs/109/PDF/Slip/LB644.pdf)[_Act_](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/FloorDocs/109/PDF/Slip/LB644.pdf). It defines transnational repression as actions committed by a foreign government or terrorist organization, or an agent working on behalf of these entities, “with the intention of harassing, intimidating, censoring, or otherwise extending such principal’s ability to influence, control, or impose such principal’s preferences on the behavior of individuals outside of the principal’s territory or jurisdiction.” Similarly to the Texas measure, the Nebraska law introduces a criminal sentencing enhancement for covered offenses — including first-, second- and third-degree assault, stalking, and violation of a harassment protection order, among others — that interfere with Nebraskans’ protected conduct under the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution or that seek to force a Nebraska resident to work for a foreign principal or leave the United States.

In addition to these increased penalties, the act calls on Nebraska State Patrol to create training on cross-border repression tactics and key perpetrators, to establish a website with a multilingual reporting mechanism for targeted individuals, and to prepare a report for the legislature. Certainly, training and multilingual reporting tools are helpful. However, the legislation’s repeated reference to the term “foreign adversary” may increase the likelihood that the implementation process will only focus on governments like China and Iran and overlook transnational repression linked to U.S. allies such as [Saudi Arabia](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2019/06/khashoggi-killing-un-human-rights-expert-says-saudi-arabia-responsible) and [India](https://apnews.com/article/india-nikhil-gupta-pannun-sikh-murder-b1c6a424dc2bfc4d8606d08ba70b00c6).
