title: Tshwane needs better freight rail to become SA’s automotive capital
summary: There was a blue, oval-shaped void on the show floor at SA Auto Week 2026 in Durban this week. Ford Motor Company Africa’s president, Neale Hill, was on the speakers’ list, but it had no representation as a brand with a stand. Into this vac
content:
There was a blue, oval-shaped void on the show floor at SA Auto Week 2026 in Durban this week. Ford Motor Company Africa’s president, Neale Hill, was on the speakers’ list, but it had no representation as a brand with a stand.

Into this vacuum stepped Chery, latest tenant of the Nissan factory in Rosslyn, Pretoria, and its neighbour in the not-so-special automotive economic zone, BMW.

The Eastern Cape can say what it wants, but Gauteng hosts 200 automotive component firms alongside major assembly plants, and generates 34.4% of South Africa’s total GDP. And Pretoria serves as the country’s central hub for automotive research, development and technical skills, making a powerful case for it serving as the strategic inland platform for vehicle assembly and export into broader African markets.

Tony Liu, chief executive of Chery SA, says that as a new investor coming to the country, the company is in it for the long run. “We are here in South Africa for the people and are also becoming a South African citizen. So, we are part of the economy, part of this country’s economic development.”

But there are barriers that all businesses and even citizens fully understand, and Liu knows he will have to grapple with them. “Infrastructure-cost competitiveness, including water and electricity – those are basic things. Logistics cost – that is also going to be adding a lot of weight onto our competitiveness across Africa and even globally,” he tells Daily Maverick.

BMW’s Rosslyn plant exports most of its production volume. Operating far inland from coastal export ports creates structural logistics vulnerabilities that require reliable rail infrastructure and stable municipal grid connections.

“It’s the wrong place, to be honest, because we export 96% of our volume… So that’s always been an issue, and our biggest challenges have been logistics,” admits Peter van Binsbergen, chairperson and chief executive of BMW Group SA.

### The Transnet curse

One of the benefits of moving into Rosslyn is that a railway line runs by it, but this has not always been the benefit it should have been.

“We’ve had a lot of logistics challenges in the time when Transnet was shaky,” says Van Binsbergen. “Post-Covid, when railway lines and power cables were being stolen, we had a lot of problems getting our cars and our parts in and out of Rosslyn. So we even brought in containers via Mozambique and things like that.

“We have a rail line that comes right to our siding at the vehicle distribution centre, but that rail line has just been notoriously unstable.”

Chery SA chief executive Tony Liu. (Photo: Supplied / Chery South Africa)

So, Daily Maverick was not surprised to spot both Van Binsbergen and Liu in conversation with Transnet group CEO Michelle Phillips on day two of the conference.

“We managed to clear up ... as the motor industry meeting with Transnet that we want to actually put more on rail instead of on trucks,” the BMW chief disclosed. “Trucks are not our wish… But you need to balance your line so that it’s full going down to the port and full coming back. Having Chery in Rosslyn might, or will, give us a bit more muscle to balance that line a bit better.”

### Special zone, special treatment

One Pretoria carmaker that also has a railway line running right by it, Ford, was actually promised improved logistics when it sank R15-billion into Silverton.

“There has been progress in the broader rail reform process, including the rail access framework and onboarding of private operators, as well as some progress at ports,” Ford wrote in reply to questions. “However, rail is one part of an interconnected logistics value chain, and the entire ecosystem needs to operate in unison.

“For Ford, the key issue is how this translates into reliable, commercially viable services that support automotive manufacturing and exports.

“This requires a rail system that runs on time, has suitable rolling stock, and provides dependable connections between manufacturing hubs and ports so that incoming goods and export vehicles reach their destinations on schedule, and support our wider business operations.

Neale Hill, president of Ford Motor Company in Africa, at a function on 10 April 2024 when the Nelson Mandela Foundation recognised the company as a Legacy Champion, the highest tier of donors to the foundation. (Photo: Supplied)

“Access agreements and reform milestones are important, but the real measure will be dependable operational services across the logistics chain.”

Ford’s castle is in the heart of the Tshwane Automotive Special Economic Zone (Tasez), an empire that spans 162.6ha in Silverton and holds pride of place as Africa’s first automotive city. It is backed by direct funding and a multi-
tiered government partnership between the De­­partment of Trade, Industry and Com­petition, the Gauteng provincial gov­­ernment and the City of Tshwane.

As part of the privilege of re­­ceiving Cyril Rama­phosa’s blessing during his 2019 presidential campaign, the Tasez has been integrated into a VIP energy grid to protect tenants against municipal power interruptions, alongside dedicated rail sidings connecting Rosslyn and Silverton factories straight to export ports.

### Break in the chain

Transnet’s CEO has actively engaged with automotive leaders during industry forums to build collaboration channels between the state-owned logistics provider and primary vehicle manufacturers.

“We will talk to the automotive industry about how best we can support them going forward, both on port and rail, and engage with them on collaboration initiatives and how they can support us to make sure that we do what is required for the industry,” Phillips told Daily Maverick after her conversation with Liu.

Transnet group CEO Michelle Phillips at the Africa Rail Expo that was held at the Sandton Convention Centre on 7 July 2026 in Johannesburg. (File photo: Fani Mahuntsi / Gallo Images)

“We are in this business because we know that it’s difficult, actually, and that there are problems to be solved. I think in the logistics space, if you don’t have a problem, then you have a problem... Look, we are trying hard together with the teams to support the industry as much as we can.”

To be fair to Transnet, it is on the right track to reform in two important ways. First, manufacturers acknowledge a marked improvement in Transnet’s willingness to communicate openly, resolving misunderstandings regarding rail usage versus road freighting.

And second, Phillips’s engagement with Rosslyn manufacturers on bi-directional corridor efficiency addresses line balancing – using inbound trains for imported components or vehicles and outbound trains for export vehicles – and has seemingly set clear objectives.

However, there is still an execution gap. Although leadership dialogue is welcomed, manufacturer evaluations – particularly from Ford – still show that reform milestones, access frameworks and private sector onboarding must rapidly translate into on-time rail schedules, sufficient rolling stock and seamless port handling to protect manufacturing competitiveness.

Van Binsbergen reveals a possible policy direction that could salvage the ailing industry. “If we really want to get economies of scale, we’ve got to actually agree that [we need to] specialise in South Africa … in wiring harnesses, car glass, tyres,” he suggests.

“And then we have to be able to talk to each other without breaking competition law to say, ‘Okay guys, these are the topics we’re going to focus on. We’re going to give enough ­volume to the producer so they can get their economies of scale in place and we can develop like pools of competence.’ ”

There must be something in the water on the west side of Tshwane because Liu was singing a similar tune of collaboration and united industrial action. Now, if only that message can spread. **DM**

Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the city now hosts more than 1,400 fintech enterprises, including eight digital banks, four virtual insurers and 12 licensed virtual-asset trading platforms. Speaking at a press conference for the upcoming Hong Kong Fintech Week, Chan said the city's success in the field was not accidental, but the result of sustained policy vision, robust regulatory guidance and a firm commitment to implementation.

The Fintech Week, to be held from 2 to 6 November under the theme “Fintech Hub: Connecting the World, Building the Future”, follows the recent conclusion of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) finance ministers' meeting in Hong Kong, where digital infrastructure financing was a core topic.陈茂波表示，是次活动契合香港第一个五年规划和未来发展的施政报告蓝图。
陈表示，政府和香港金融管理局已完成对香港固定收益市场使用分布式账本技术（DLT）的初步审查。他们已发布澄清，确认使用 DLT 维护的债券持有人名册可被视为满足《公司条例》（第 622 章）规定的记录保存要求。

截至去年底，香港银行托管的数字资产超过140亿港元，代币化存款达到290亿港元。政府上个月还完成了第四次数字绿色债券发行，筹集了约200亿港元，创下了全球数字债券发行规模的新纪录。陈说，这也是世界上第一个将代币化港元存款纳入结算流程的数字债券。

证券及期货事务监察委员会将完善其监管框架，以促进以黄金和其他实物资产为支持的代币化产品在持牌平台上的发行和交易。香港交易及结算所将于明年与指定银行合作推出代币化仓单融资试点，并正在开发基于区块链的多资产代币化平台，其中将包括来自伦敦金属交易所认可仓库的商品仓单。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Hong Kong now hosts over 1,400 fintech companies, including eight digital banks and four virtual insurers. He highlighted progress in digital asset regulation, tokenised bonds and a forthcoming blockchain platform for warehouse receipts.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

23 Oct 2026 at 13:22 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the city now hosts more than 1,400 fintech enterprises, including eight digital banks, four virtual insurers and 12 licensed virtual-asset trading platforms. Speaking at a press conference for the upcoming Hong Kong Fintech Week, Chan said the city's success in the field was not accidental, but the result of sustained policy vision, robust regulatory guidance and a firm commitment to implementation.

The Fintech Week, to be held from 2 to 6 November under the theme “Fintech Hub: Connecting the World, Building the Future”, follows the recent conclusion of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) finance ministers' meeting in Hong Kong, where digital infrastructure financing was a core topic. Chan noted that the event aligns with Hong Kong's first five-year plan and the Policy Address blueprint for future development.

Chan said the government and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority had completed an initial review of the use of distributed ledger technology (DLT) in the city's fixed-income market. They had issued clarifications confirming that a register of debenture holders maintained using DLT could be treated as meeting record-keeping requirements under the Companies Ordinance (Chapter 622).

As of the end of last year, digital assets held in custody by Hong Kong banks exceeded 14 billion Hong Kong dollars, while tokenised deposits reached 29 billion Hong Kong dollars. The government also completed its fourth digital green bond issuance last month, raising about 20 billion Hong Kong dollars and setting a new global record for the size of a digital bond issuance. It was also the world's first digital bond to integrate tokenised Hong Kong dollar deposits into the settlement process, Chan said.

The Securities and Futures Commission will refine its regulatory framework to facilitate the issuance and trading of tokenised products backed by gold and other physical assets on licensed platforms. The Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing will launch a pilot for tokenised warehouse receipt financing next year in cooperation with designated banks, and is developing a blockchain-based multi-asset tokenisation platform that will include commodity warehouse receipts from London Metal Exchange-accredited warehouses.

# Strong earthquake strikes China’s remote Tibet region

At least 16 people have died and dozens more have been injured after a major earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale shook China’s remote Tibet region on Thursday, state media said. Hundreds of houses collapsed in the tremor.

Issued on: 22/10/2026 - 23:09 Modified: 22/10/2026 - 23:30

 1 min Reading time

Share

 By:

 The earthquake measured 7.0 on the Richter scale. © Science Photo Library via Reuter/ Illustration picture

At least 16 people were killed and 32 more injured when a strong 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck [China](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/china/)’s remote [Tibet](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/tibet/) region, state news agency Xinhua said, citing local authorities.

More than 300 houses collapsed in the earthquake, which struck Thursday at 10:33pm (1433 GMT). Officials were still evaluating the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, Xinhua said.

Read more[Scores killed in powerful earthquake in Tibet](https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20250107-earthquake-tiibet-shigatse)

The quake’s epicentre was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.

It struck at a shallow depth of 10 kilometres.

A level-II earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, Xinhua said.

The epicentre was located in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua.

Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.

Earthquakes in China are relatively common.

In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in [an earthquake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county](https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20250107-earthquake-tiibet-shigatse).

content:
华盛顿 —

台湾政府星期三(10月21日)对北京当局企图以暴力威胁，侵害台湾人民的人身安全及言论自由的做法发出严厉谴责。台湾检方当天起诉五名被告，指控他们受中国大陆人士委托，策划驾车冲撞曾于去年12月在社交媒体发布讽刺中国领导人习近平段子的台湾相声演员黄逸豪。台湾外交部也呼吁民主伙伴正视中国跨国镇压，共同捍卫民主自由与人权。

新北地方检察署说，检调查出大陆地区人士“K”涉嫌以新台币45万元为报酬，委托郑姓、游姓、黄姓、范姓及廖姓等五名被告搜集特定人士的个人资料，预谋驾车冲撞使其受伤住院，以阻止其参加原定演出。检方侦查终结，依重伤害未遂、违反《个人资料保护法》等罪嫌提起公诉，具体求刑2年7个月至5年6个月。

黄逸豪去年12月在社交媒体贴出讽刺中国领导人习近平的段子，上个月在自家住处附近遭车辆撞伤，经检调人员侦查后发现是涉案人受中国人士指使，意图制造假车祸让他无法上台演出。

新北地检署说，“本案系中共涉嫌透过跨境镇压手段，指挥我国不法分子以极端暴力手段打压政治立场相左声音之严重事件。被告等人甘为境外敌对势力效劳，意图在我国社会制造寒蝉效应，严重挑衅我国民主法治底线，恶性极重。”

**台湾外交部、陆委会发表声明谴责**

台湾外交部和陆委会同日发表声明，同声谴责中国此一“跨国镇压”暴力行为。

外交部说，言论自由是民主社会不可侵犯的基石，“任何人都不该因发表评论而遭受暴力报复”，中国涉嫌收买在地人士意图使艺文工作者无法登台，“是恶劣的政治噤声行径”，外交部呼吁国际社会共同正视中国跨国镇压的威胁，拒绝威权整体利用民主社会的开放与自由，从事恐吓、渗透及暴力迫害。

陆委会说，中共不但在其境内无法容忍不同意见，也不容许中国以外的地方有人提出政治批评，“更可耻的是，以跨国镇压手法伤害台湾网民众，企图钳制台湾的言论自由，严重挑战台湾的民主法治秩序”，台湾必将依法究责，追缉到底。

**国际人权组织：台湾缺乏界定跨国镇压的法律工具**

总部在巴黎的国际人权组织“第19条”(Article 19)亚洲项目专员刘以正在接受美国之音采访时说，台湾政府对跨国镇压已有一定认识,也有相应的应对机制。他举例说,日裔媒体人矢板明夫在台湾遭香港人士攻击后，执法人员能在机场迅速逮捕涉案者。

不过，刘以正说，对于涉及政治意图的案件,台湾仍缺乏合适的法律工具。他说：“我们目前没有一个好的法律工具来定义跨国镇压。因为如果只是A打了B，两个人都没有任何政治意图，它就只是一个伤害罪，可是今天他具有某种特别政治意图，就需要要以不同形式去处理，它的背后可能有国家级的行动者。”

刘以正认为，民主国家需要提高对跨国镇压的理解，让其执法单位理解这种行为才能提前作出防范措施。

“因为很多单位其实不知道中国这样的做法，他们需要人权团体去倡议，可是很多时候这样的倡议都是在有人受害之后才发生，所以提前围堵，增加大家对跨国镇压的了解，然后准备好合适的法律工具，”他说，跨国镇压与欧洲目前非常注意的FIMI (foreign information manipulation and interference，外国信息操纵与干预)有重叠之处，大家应该携手合作，共同思考如何有效应对中国的新形态威胁。

“因为越来越多这种混合型威胁行为难以单一放在某一个法律概念框架下，像欧洲人会讲FIMI，它与跨国镇压又有一些交集的地方，所以它们是两个有交集的象限概念群，所以到底要怎么样好好的来描述中国可能对所有人造成的混合型威胁，这件事情是我们组织下一个想要探讨的东西。我们现在想要看到就是其实我们大家需要更多的串联，来把这些不同的框架一起放进来，不然的话，我们都会用一人处理一个小的框架，那永远没有办法对抗我们的对手，”刘以正说。

**美国近期案件与北京回应**

美国司法部月初才起诉居住在加州尔湾的女子张婉莹，指控她涉嫌在美国境内充当中国政府未登记代理人。检方指控她曾按照中国政府官员的指示，在美国对台湾总统赖清德的儿子进行秘密监视，这起案件也再度引发外界对中国政府在美国开展跨国监视活动的关注。

台湾方面表示，赖清德的家人遭到监视显示，所谓的跨国镇压已经影响到台湾民众及其家属。中国国台办发言人陈斌华则表示，坚决反对民进党政府“勾连外部势力”信口雌黄，操弄‘反中抗中’，挑起两岸对立。

**美国智库学者：非国家行为者如何接受指令值得关注**

全球台湾研究中心(GTI)研究员本·桑度(Ben Sando)在接受美国之音采访时说，在涉及中国在全世界影响力的行为方面，无论是间谍、窃取商业秘密或恐吓异议人士等，人们会见到许多非国家行为者参与各种活动，以赖清德的例子来说，它涉及的是一个政治人物的儿子可能被恫吓，他认为这些涉案者的背景值得仔细观察。

全球台湾研究中心(Global Taiwan Institute, GTI)研究员本·桑度(Ben Sando)接受美国之音采访时说，在涉及中国全球影响力的行为方面，无论是间谍活动、窃取商业机密还是恐吓异议人士，常有许多非国家行为者参与其中。以赖清德之子的案例而言，涉及的是一名政治人物的儿子可能受到恫吓，他认为这些涉案者的背景值得仔细观察。

桑度说:“有意思的是去看这些不同行为者如何从中国政府接收指令。我非常好奇的是，是否有人事先采取这些行为来作为向中国政府建立可信度或名声的方式。人们都知道，中国有非常复杂的系统--统战系统--来奖赏这种忠诚。”

他说，只要能执行北京当局的指令或作出有利它的行为，即便人不住在中国都有可能因此得到奖赏。

“即便你不是住在北京或与中国高级领导人有关系，即便你只是住在香港、福建或甚至是海外，中国都有办法能奖赏你，像是恫吓政治人物的子女都可能得到小小的奖赏，”桑度说，这种奖赏或许是拍完一张照片后回到中国，就有可能被邀请去与某人合做生意，或是从地方政府得到好处真的赚到一些钱。

“中国尤其将经济武器化，以此来奖赏忠诚，”他说。

## Uganda: Police Break Silence On Murder of Rwandan Dissident Beheaded in Mpigi

Robert Kabera.

19 October 2026

[Nile Post (Kampala)](https://nilepost.co.ug/ "Visit Nile Post (Kampala)")

By Kenneth Kazibwe

Police have launched investigations into the murder of a Rwandan dissident whose headless body was discovered in Mpigi District, with the victim's missing head yet to be recovered.

Sgt Maj Robert Kabera, 50, a former Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) soldier who was critical of President Paul Kagame's leadership, was found dead on Saturday morning, October 17, in Luwala Village, Kammengo Sub-county.

Police spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke told journalists on Monday that officers had registered a murder case after the discovery of the body.

"We acknowledge that we registered murder of male adult averagely 50 years whose head was cut off and up to now it hasn't yet been recovered. We recovered the body minus the head. He was identified as Robert Kabera by his relatives," Rusoke said.

He said police received the report on Saturday, although investigators believe the killing could have occurred either during the night of October 16 or in the early hours of October 17.

According to Rusoke, local residents discovered the remains and alerted police. Kabera's relatives had also become concerned after he failed to communicate as he usually did.

"The remains were discovered by locals who informed police. Incidentally relatives were concerned about their person who usually wouldn't take long to communicate," he said.

Police officers who visited the scene found the headless body, which was subsequently taken to Mulago City Mortuary as part of the investigation.

Rusoke said investigators were examining the circumstances surrounding the killing and other details that could help establish what happened.

"We are investigating that murder and any other details relevant to the murder or any circumstances surrounding his life," he said.

Kabera reportedly fled Rwanda for Uganda around 2020 after raising concerns that his life was in danger.

His killing comes against the backdrop of his reported criticism of the Rwandan leadership. However, police have not publicly established a motive for the murder or indicated whether his political views were connected to his death.

Investigations are ongoing, with the recovery of his missing head among the outstanding details in the case.

title: Taiwan, U.S. still lack 'hellscape' to thwart China invasion: U.S. official - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 美国官员：台湾和美国仍缺乏阻止中国入侵的“地狱景观” - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月20日电 美国国会委员会主席周二表示，台湾和美国尚未建立起帮助台湾军队抵御中国潜在入侵所需的“地狱图景”，鉴于当前“危险”的地缘政治局势，他们应该以“紧迫感”来完成这项任务。美中经济与安全审查委员会主席兰德尔·施赖弗在台北的一个论坛上发表讲话时表示，即使在 2027 年 8 月 1 日（该日期）几年后，美国仍将面临弹药和其他关键能力短缺的问题。
content:
中新社台北10月20日电 美国国会委员会主席周二表示，台湾和美国尚未建立起帮助台湾军队抵御中国潜在入侵所需的“地狱图景”，鉴于当前“危险”的地缘政治局势，他们应该以“紧迫感”来完成这项任务。

美中经济与安全审查委员会主席兰德尔·施赖弗在台北的一个论坛上发表讲话时表示，即使在2027年8月1日之后的几年内，美国仍将继续面临弹药和其他关键能力的短缺。据报道，中国国家主席习近平已在该日指示中国人民解放军做好武力占领台湾的准备。

施里弗引用了美国和伊朗之间持续不断的冲突，称亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰在中东延长部署后松了一口气，造成了“航母缺口”。

他说，在此背景下，如果朝鲜和俄罗斯与中国协调，加剧紧张局势，美军将不得不做出回应，从而进一步耗尽资源，并使当前时期“尤其危险”。

施里弗指出，现代战争并不是谁拥有最先进的人工智能或反无人机能力的竞赛，而是谁能够以最快的速度扩展这些技术并将其整合到能够解释战争不断演变的性质的作战概念中的竞赛。
他引用了美国印太司令部司令塞缪尔·帕帕罗上将提出的一个类比，帕帕罗在 2024 年的一次采访中表示，他希望在台湾发生突发事件时，让解放军“将台湾海峡变成无人的地狱”，为美国的反应赢得时间。

“但请记住，地狱景观非常令人向往，”施赖弗说。 “我们还没有把它建成。”

他说：“我们不仅需要考虑建造东西，还需要考虑运营概念，并带着某种紧迫感这样做。”

施里弗认为，持续不断的冲突表明，关于防御和进攻相对优势的长期争论出现了转折点。

在谈到俄罗斯与乌克兰的战争时，他说，“我们看到乌克兰通过不输而获胜。”

“坦率地说，我们看到伊朗做得很好，至少没有失去政权和一些关键能力，”他补充道。

为了加强无人机能力，台湾立法院批准了2400亿新台币（73.6亿美元）的特别预算，而内阁则提议通过补充预算额外增加1457亿新台币的国防开支。其中，新台币 559 亿元专门用于无人系统，包括无人机。

与此同时，2026财年美国国防授权法案指示美国国防部寻求与台湾建立一项联合计划，为双方武装部队开发和部署无人系统和反无人系统能力，包括通过共同开发和共同生产。

（林肖恩）
结局/ASG

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 20 (CNA) Taiwan and the United States have yet to build the "hellscape" needed to help Taiwanese forces hold out against a potential Chinese invasion, and they should approach the task with a "sense of urgency" given the current "dangerous" geopolitical situation, a U.S. congressional commission chair said Tuesday.

Speaking at a forum in Taipei, Randall Schriver, chair of the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, said the United States would continue to face shortages of munitions and other key capabilities even a couple of years after Aug. 1, 2027, the date by which Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) has reportedly directed the People's Liberation Army (PLA) to be ready to take Taiwan by force.

Schriver cited the ongoing conflict involving the United States and Iran, saying it had created an "aircraft carrier gap" after the USS Abraham Lincoln was relieved following an extended deployment in the Middle East.

Against this backdrop, if North Korea and Russia were to coordinate with China to escalate tensions, U.S. forces would have to respond, further stretching their resources and making the current period "particularly dangerous," he said.

Schriver noted that modern warfare is a race not over who possesses the most advanced artificial intelligence or counter-drone capabilities, but over who can scale those technologies the fastest and integrate them into operational concepts that account for the evolving nature of warfare.

He cited an analogy offered by U.S. Indo-Pacific Command chief Adm. Samuel Paparo, who said in a 2024 interview that he wanted to "turn the Taiwan Strait into an unmanned hellscape" for the PLA in a Taiwan contingency to buy time for a U.S. response.

"But remember, hellscape is very aspirational," Schriver said. "We haven't built it out."

"We need to think about not only building things but the operational concepts and doing so with some sense of urgency," he said.

Schriver argued that ongoing conflicts suggest a turning point in the longstanding debate over the relative advantages of defense and offense.

Referring to the Russia-Ukraine war, he said, "We're seeing Ukraine win by not losing."

"Frankly, we're seeing Iran do quite well without losing at least the regime and some of its key capabilities," he added.

To strengthen its drone capabilities, Taiwan's Legislative Yuan has approved a special budget of NT$240 billion (US$7.36 billion), while the Cabinet has proposed an additional NT$145.7 billion in defense spending through a supplementary budget. Of the latter amount, NT$55.9 billion is earmarked for uncrewed systems, including drones.

Meanwhile, the fiscal 2026 U.S. National Defense Authorization Act directs the U.S. Department of Defense to seek to establish a joint program with Taiwan to develop and field uncrewed systems and counter-uncrewed systems capabilities, including through co-development and co-production, for both sides' armed forces.

(By Sean Lin)

Enditem/ASG

title: Liberia: IMF Urges African Govts to Shield Vulnerable Citizens From Economic Shocks
summary: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has urged African governments to strengthen measures to protect vulnerable citizens from economic shocks, warning that global uncertainties, energy supply disruptions and declining foreign aid could pla
content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has urged African governments to strengthen measures to protect vulnerable citizens from economic shocks, warning that global uncertainties, energy supply disruptions and declining foreign aid could place additional pressure on households and economies across the continent.

Speaking during the IMF's annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Zeine Zeidane, Director of the IMF's African Department, emphasized the need for governments to balance economic stability with targeted social protection, particularly as countries confront rising external pressures and uncertain global economic conditions.

Zeidane said economic reforms implemented in several African countries have helped strengthen macroeconomic stability, citing subsidy and exchange rate reforms in Ethiopia and Nigeria, as well as structural reforms in South Africa.

However, he cautioned that the resilience demonstrated by African economies should not be mistaken for immunity to further shocks.

According to him, countries have adapted to changes in global energy supplies through rerouting shipments, drawing down inventories and adjusting business operations. Nevertheless, he warned that renewed disruptions to energy supplies and other external developments could undermine these efforts.

The impact of global economic pressures also varies across countries. Some commodity-exporting economies have benefited from higher prices for oil, copper and gold, while countries with less resource-intensive economies are experiencing slower growth and widening external deficits.

Zeidane also highlighted the continued decline in bilateral aid, which the IMF projects will fall by another 12 percent this year following a steep reduction in the previous year. The decline could further constrain governments' ability to finance development programs and provide essential services.

He identified renewed energy supply disruptions, increased global risk aversion, a strong El Niño weather pattern, and continuing conflict and insecurity as potential risks to Africa's economic outlook.

Against this backdrop, the IMF official urged governments to prioritize targeted assistance for vulnerable households rather than adopt broad and costly interventions that could place additional pressure on public finances.

He pointed to measures such as school feeding programs and temporary price relief as possible ways to support households facing rising living costs. Such interventions, he stressed, should be transparently financed, carefully targeted, capped and time-bound to ensure that assistance reaches those who need it most without undermining fiscal stability.

The IMF also called on governments to protect essential public services and productive investment while pursuing policies that safeguard economic stability.

For commodity-exporting countries benefiting from higher prices, the Fund emphasized the importance of saving part of the additional revenue and using available resources to repay expensive debt. This would help governments build financial buffers against future shocks rather than commit temporary windfalls to permanent spending.

Countries facing high import bills, meanwhile, may need to continue fiscal adjustment while protecting critical services and investments necessary for long-term development.

Zeidane further underscored the importance of exchange rate flexibility in countries whose monetary frameworks allow it, alongside stronger debt transparency and improved public debt management.

Beyond immediate economic challenges, the IMF urged African governments to pursue structural reforms capable of generating sustainable growth, attracting investment and creating employment opportunities.

Priority areas include improving electricity supply, expanding digital connectivity, strengthening workforce skills and establishing a more predictable business environment for businesses and investors.

The Fund said these reforms could help African economies close productivity gaps, improve competitiveness and strengthen their ability to withstand future external shocks.

content:
和埃斯库罗斯、索福克洛斯相比，欧里庇得斯的戏剧更具现代性。这就是说他的戏剧主题，价值判断更容易让现代人理解。他的戏剧主人公面对的问题和解决问题的方式也更易让我们产生共鸣。欧里庇得斯剧作的一个显著特点是让女性占上舞台中央。

问：在希腊，女性的地位一直是个问题。

答：是的。这让许多历史学家不解。因为在号称文明典范的雅典，妇女却缺少应有的权利。首先，妇女几乎没有政治权利。她们不能参与城邦政治，不能投票，担任公职。那种直接民主，如市场公民集会，辩论竟然没有女性参与。其次，妇女也没有经济权利，没有独立的财产权。家庭财产的拥有者是男性家长。再次，女性的社交活动受到严格限制，不许可单独外出，妇女上街必须结伴而行。未婚少女更要在成年亲属陪伴下才能与外人见面，因为男性相信只有这样才能保证处女贞洁。第四，妇女几乎没有受教育的机会，她们大多只能在家庭中受教育，一些男性公开嘲笑妇女，甚至修昔底德这样的睿智之人也说过“妇女端庄的名声是在家里的”这种贬低女性的话。在古希腊，妇女天然合理的位置是在家中侍奉丈夫，生儿育女。所以古希腊有家政学，它专门传授主持家政的知识。但是，希腊男性需要丰富多彩的社交生活，而这种生活不可能没有女性参与。结果就出现一种奇怪的现象，一些杰出的，让人艳羡的女性是以妓女之名出现的。比如伯里克利最爱的女人，连苏格拉底都称为老师的阿斯帕西亚就被人称为妓女。其实她创办修辞学校，给青年女子传授知识，帮助伯里克利规划雅典建设，赞助悲剧诗人，她是一位聪慧睿智，特立独行的杰出女性。我们甚至可以猜测，希腊社会中女性应有的地位和她们实际受到的忽视激发了欧里庇得斯的创作灵感。所以希腊学大家基托说：“如果戏剧家们从未描绘过这些被压抑的生灵，这些和他们一起生活的人们，并将这些生动的形象从荷马的诗中带到舞台上，这实在是难以置信的。”

问：希腊悲剧中不缺让人惊叹的女性形象。

答：确实。 但在塑造可歌可泣的女性形象方面，欧里庇得斯绝对首屈一指。在欧里庇得斯现存的18部剧作中，有半数以上以女性为主角。他对女性的欲望，理智，疯狂，犹疑，决断，各种情感与行为方式，对女性在希腊社会中的爱恨情仇都做了深入骨髓的刻画。法国著名的希腊悲剧的研究家德·罗米依女士指出：“把现代性这个概念用在古代作家欧里庇得斯身上有两重含义。首先，较之他的同代人和前人，欧里庇得斯是现代人。在埃斯库罗斯和索福克洛斯之后，欧里庇得斯进行了创新和探索，还引发热议。可以说欧里庇得斯是他所处时代的现代人。另一方面，在好些特质上，欧里庇得斯又与我们的时代联系在一起。事实上，我们当今的作家就借鉴并强化了他的多种倾向。这些倾向在欧里庇得斯的时代令人愕然，因此欧里庇得斯还是绝对意义上的现代人。”这段话引导我们从两个方向上欣赏和思考欧里庇得斯的剧作。哪怕在当代的意义上，我们也可以说欧里庇得斯是位女权主义者，甚至是有些过分的女权主义者。在《美狄亚》一剧中，他甚至安排犯下双重杀人罪的美迪亚乘龙车升空，逃脱报复。当然，欧里庇得斯生活的雅典已经发生了巨大的变化。索福克洛斯的创作期多是在雅典黄金时代，社会氛围总体上是积极乐观向上的。可欧里庇得斯的创作活动却是在波罗奔尼撒战争的阴影之下。正如德·罗米依指出的：“他没有经历希波战争的辉煌时代，给他留下深刻印记的是波罗奔尼撒战争，一场希腊人之间的战争。这战争在爆发前就显示出会旷日持久，劳民伤财的种种迹象。而在长达27年生灵涂炭的角逐之后，雅典帝国被摧毁了。他笔下人物挣扎于其中的混乱无序可能很大程度要归因于这种幻灭的气氛。”

问：欧里庇得斯比索福克洛斯年轻，可他们去世的时间似乎差不多。

答：关于欧里庇得斯的生平，可靠的资料很少。有记载说当索福克洛斯听到欧里庇得斯去世的消息后，曾让歌队全体着黑衣，不带花冠。可我们知道索福克洛斯死于公元前406年，可见他们是相继去世的。但确切的是欧里庇得斯去世前已经离开了雅典，他是在马其顿去世的。我们根据仅存不多的一点资料介绍一下欧里庇得斯的生平。首先，他的出生年月就不确切，传说希波战争中希腊联军取得撒拉米海战大捷，在庆祝大会上，16岁的索福克洛斯曾头戴花冠，领唱胜利凯歌。欧里庇得斯就出生在战役发生的当天。但是人们发现了一块石碑，上面记载欧里庇得斯出生于公元前485年与484年之间的冬天。据罗念生先生的判断，这块石碑上的记载较为可靠。他的父亲是拥有土地的贵族，所以他少年时同一般贵族青年一样，学习过角斗术。他还学习过绘画，比较特殊的一点是他收集许多书藉的手抄本，是第一位有藏书的剧作家。这恐怕和他与当时雅典的哲人圈子交往密切有关。他与普罗塔哥拉、阿纳克萨格拉、苏格拉底是好朋友，经常参加哲人们的讨论。伯罗奔尼撒战争以雅典的失败结束。欧里庇得斯身边的朋友也渐渐凋零。他离开雅典去了马其顿。马其顿国王阿尔克拉俄斯是他的崇拜者，而且雅好文艺。欧里庇得斯就生活在他的王宫中，最后终老于此。时间大约在公元前406年。这与索福克洛斯去世几乎同时。如果索福克洛斯让他的歌队向欧里庇得斯致哀的记载是真实的，那么他也是随后而逝。但这些资料很可疑，因为有记载，索福克洛斯也不是在雅典去世。雅典曾派人去马其顿，想接回欧里庇得斯的遗骨，但未成功。不过倒是有雅典人为他树立了纪念碑，碑文是：“全希腊世界是欧里庇得斯的纪念碑，诗人的遗骨在客死之地马其顿永埋，诗人的故乡本是雅典，希腊的希腊，这里万人称赞他，赞赏他的诗才。”

问：这碑文倒是写的不错。

答：是的。欧里庇得斯配得上这个赞誉。我们读他的作品确实能感到那种现代感。古代神话传说中的人物在他笔下成为一个个有血有肉的现实人物。就如同我们身边所见的人。索福克洛斯当年说，他自己写人应该是怎样的，而欧里庇得斯写人就是怎样的。这句评语极为精准。我们把欧里庇得斯笔下人物的活动及遭遇梳理一下，你会发现一个社会所面对的各种情况，战争的正义与非正义，民主制度的运作，男女关系中平等与压迫的冲突，贫富差距，宗教与世俗，英雄与常人等等，都表现在他的戏剧中。诗人也借人物的行为表达自己的价值观。以我个人的阅读经验，欧里庇得斯的剧耐读而且发人深醒。有趣的是他的戏剧题材常被后来的戏剧大家拿来重写。高乃依就重写《美狄亚》拉辛依据《希波吕托斯》的剧情重新创作了《费德尔》，德国作曲家格鲁克的杰出歌剧《伊菲格涅在陶里德》就是以欧里庇得斯的同名悲剧为脚本。总之，欧里庇得斯对人类精神宝库贡献良多。

# Putin and Chinese Premier Li Qiang reaffirm strategic ties ahead of APEC summit

3 hours ago

Photo: Xinhua

Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Wednesday, highlighting that relations between Moscow and Beijing continue to develop successfully and dynamically amid an evolving global landscape. The high-level talks also come as the Kremlin floats the prospect of a potential three-way meeting involving Putin, US President Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping during the upcoming APEC summit in China.

Premier Li stated during the meeting that close strategic coordination between China and Russia represents an invaluable stabilizing force in an increasingly turbulent international environment. He noted that Beijing is ready to enhance strategic communication, deepen mutual political trust, and expand comprehensive, mutually beneficial cooperation to foster greater well-being for both populations.

Addressing international governance, Li warned that unilateralism and hegemonism remain prevalent worldwide, urging both countries to strengthen coordination on major global issues. He emphasized the need for close collaboration within multilateral frameworks such as the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and BRICS, aiming to rally broader support across the Global South to safeguard shared interests and uphold international fairness and justice.

According to a Chinese readout of the discussion, Putin affirmed that China-Russia relations are founded on mutual respect, equality, and reciprocity, remaining resilient against third-party interference and global fluctuations. Describing China as Russia's closest and most dependable partner, Putin expressed Moscow's intent to deepen practical cooperation in energy, agriculture, aerospace, civil nuclear power, information technology, artificial intelligence, and transportation. The Russian leader also pledged support for China’s hosting of this year’s APEC gathering and its upcoming chairmanship of the BRICS grouping next year.

title: China says COP31 should focus on tariffs against its clean tech
zh_title: 中国称COP31应重点讨论对其清洁技术征收关税
summary: 中国 中国敦促下个月在土耳其举行的COP31峰会解决其所谓的全球气候行动的新问题：对其清洁技术征收关税。李高副部长批评单边主义和保护主义，并表示北京将对袭击事件作出坚决回应。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 21 日香港时间 14:45 · 2 分钟阅读中国已致电下个月在土耳其举行的 COP31 峰会将重点讨论所谓的新问题
content:
中国
中国敦促下个月在土耳其举行的第三十一届联合国气候变化框架公约(COP31)峰会解决其所谓的全球气候行动的新问题：对其清洁技术征收关税。李高副部长批评单边主义和保护主义，并表示北京将对袭击事件作出坚决回应。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 21 日 14:45 香港时间 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

中国呼吁下个月在土耳其举行的 COP31 峰会重点讨论全球气候行动的一个新问题：针对其清洁技术的关税。

生态环境部副部长李高周三在新闻发布会上表示，将于下个月在安塔利亚举行的第31届缔约方大会（COP）应讨论发展中国家的气候融资等问题，以及单边主义和保护主义的“新问题”，这是对美国和欧盟贸易政策的常见间接批评。

他说：“我们认为，这次会议应深入讨论发达国家减排不足、资金支持不足的老问题，以及单边主义和保护主义破坏全球集体努力的新问题。”
中国是迄今为止世界上最大的减排所需太阳能电池板、风力涡轮机、电池和电动汽车生产国。然而，对于担心对其当地产业产生竞争影响的国家来说，这项技术越来越被视为威胁，而不是机遇。

美国对中国太阳能和电动汽车征收高额关税，欧盟对汽车也采取了同样的做法，对一些太阳能零部件实施了限制，并正在调查中国一家大型风电公司的不公平贸易行为。

李说，在地缘政治冲突“加剧”的背景下，会议应讨论绿色技术的自由流动，并补充说，中国将对针对绿色技术的抹黑或攻击给予“坚决回应”。

李说，会议的其他优先事项应包括在 2024 年承诺每年为发展中国家提供 3000 亿美元气候融资的路线图。当被问及中国是否支持土耳其推动全球电气化协议时，李表示，这一目标符合中国政策，但没有明确支持这一推动。 “我们建议主席继续充分听取各方意见，寻求最大公约数，争取最广泛支持，”他说。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编
负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
China
China urges next month's COP31 summit in Turkey to address what it calls a new problem for global climate action: tariffs on its clean technology. Vice minister Li Gao criticised unilateralism and protectionism, and said Beijing would give a firm response to attacks.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

21 Oct 2026 at 14:45 HKT · 2 min read

China has called on the COP31 summit in Turkey next month to focus on what it described as a new problem for global climate action: tariffs against its clean technology.

The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP) meeting, which begins in Antalya next month, should address issues such as climate finance for the developing world as well as the “new problem” of unilateralism and protectionism, a common indirect criticism of US and EU trade policy, Li Gao, vice minister of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, told a press conference on Wednesday.

“We believe the conference should discuss in depth the old problems of developed countries’ insufficient emission reductions and insufficient financial support, as well as the new problem of unilateralism and protectionism undermining global collective efforts,” he said.

China is by far the world’s largest producer of solar panels, wind turbines, batteries and electric cars needed to cut emissions. However, that technology is increasingly seen as a threat, rather than an opportunity, for countries concerned about the competitive impact on their local industries.

The United States has imposed steep tariffs on Chinese solar and electric cars, while the European Union has done the same for autos, imposed restrictions on some solar components and is investigating a major Chinese wind company for unfair trade.

Against a backdrop of “intensifying” geopolitical conflicts, the conference should discuss the free flow of green technology, said Li, who added that China would give a “firm response” to smears or attacks against it.

Other priorities for the conference should include a roadmap for a pledge made in 2024 to marshal US$300 billion of climate finance a year for the developing world, Li said. Asked whether China supported Turkey’s push for a global agreement on electrification, Li said the objective was in line with Chinese policy but stopped short of explicitly supporting the push. “We suggest the presidency continue to listen fully to views from all sides, seek the greatest common denominator, and work to win the broadest possible support,” he said.

# Taiwan semiconductor electricity use hits record high in Sept.

10/21/2026 03:15 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Taipei, Oct. 21 (CNA) Electricity consumption by Taiwan's semiconductor industry topped 4.5 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) for the first time in September, a record high driven by stronger-than-expected demand for artificial intelligence (AI), the Taiwan Research Institute (TRI) said Wednesday.

As AI technologies develop rapidly and demand for computing power grows, global demand for cutting-edge chips, advanced packaging and high-performance chips continues to rise, pushing up the industry's electricity consumption, the TRI said in a statement.

Nationwide, electricity consumption by high-voltage and extra-high-voltage industrial users rose 1.76 percent year on year in September, while consumption by manufacturers rose 1.96 percent, the TRI said.

Electricity consumption in the semiconductor industry rose 11.55 percent year on year in September, returning to double-digit growth. The economic monitoring indicator for the power industry remained at "red," signaling robust activity, for the 18th consecutive month, the institute said.

Strong production in the high-tech sector has gradually spurred investment demand in other industries, boosting exports, production and corporate investment and supporting rapid economic growth, the TRI said. It estimated Taiwan's economic growth in September at 12.6 percent.

The TRI estimated that the semiconductor industry's annual electricity consumption will exceed 50 billion kWh this year, as AI-related business opportunities expand from high-end chips to servers, equipment, materials and key components, benefiting investment and production across the supply chain.

The chemical materials and textile industries continued to show "blue" monitoring readings, signaling contraction, though for different reasons. The chemical materials industry remained under pressure from global petrochemical overcapacity and a slow recovery in demand, while the textile industry faced weak international end-market demand and price competition, which continued to weigh on orders and production.

(By Pan Tzu-yu and Sean Lin)

title: Gold, ancient store of wealth, is finally gaining digital traction
summary: The digital gold market, worth about $50-billion today, is set for liftoff and could tap a swelling vein of demand to reach $700-billion, according to a new report by the World Gold Council (WGC) and Boston Consulting Group. Digital gold pr
content:
The digital gold market, worth about $50-billion today, is set for liftoff and could tap a swelling vein of demand to reach $700-billion, according to a new report by the World Gold Council (WGC) and Boston Consulting Group.

Digital gold provides exposure to the precious metal through digital platforms, eliminating the cumbersome logistics and settlement headaches associated with physical gold.

“As trading and record-keeping has moved onto electronic systems and markets have become more connected, investors have begun to expect gold to behave like other modern assets,” says the WGC.

Traction is building on this front, bringing one of humanity’s oldest stores of wealth into the digital age.

### Token gesture

“Momentum is already building as financial markets undergo a broader digital transformation, bringing tokenised investment products increasingly into the mainstream,” says the WGC.

“Tokenised gold, one segment of the digital gold market alongside vaulted digital gold, has grown fivefold in value since late 2024 to around $6-billion. Cumulative spot trading volumes in tokenised gold exceeded $90-billion in the first quarter of 2026, more than in the whole of 2025.”

This is still small potatoes. The current gold market is worth about $30-trillion at current prices and is focused on jewellery, bars, coins, gold-backed ETFs, OTC5 and central bank reserves. The physical investment gold market is worth about $13-trillion.

The report sees digital gold growing to about $165-billion in the next five years, a figure that could reach $275-billion over the same timeframe if various barriers are removed.

Source: World Gold Council.

“What holds investors back is not a lack of interest but four key barriers: trust, access, utility and cost. Trust is the swing factor. Investors point to stronger consumer protections, transparent proof of backing, accessible redemption and clearer regulation as the conditions most likely to increase confidence in digital gold,” the WGC says.

Access, meanwhile, is hampered by a lack of platforms outside of big Asian markets.

> “Where digital gold is embedded in mainstream channels such as super-apps, payment platforms and banking apps, as seen in India, China and Indonesia, penetration is up to seven times higher than in markets where such distribution does not yet exist.”

The potential for a $700-billion market stems from “latent demand” – a pool of untapped investors who would rather do things in the digital space because this is the 21st century.

“Among today’s digital gold investors, 52% held no gold before their first digital purchase, of which 92% have since bought other forms of gold,” says the report.

Gold has been a red-hot commodity over the past few years and while it is off its historic peaks of almost $5,600 an ounce scaled in January this year, its price remains elevated at more than $4,000 an ounce.

### Performance enhancing

A range of factors explain this performance, including geopolitical uncertainty – which enhances the precious metal’s safe-haven status – and central bank purchases, notably in emerging markets as the greenback loses some of its lustre as the world’s reserve currency.

The digital gold market itself is unlikely to move the dial much on this front but is seen as an entry point into the wider bullion market, especially for younger investors who are obviously more wired than their older counterparts.

Source: World Gold Council.

“Around 65% of latent demand comes from people who have not yet invested in gold. Among those who already hold gold in other forms, more than half would fund a digital gold investment with money not currently allocated to the asset.

“Rather than cannibalising demand for bars, coins or gold-backed ETFs, digital gold is thus likely to attract new investors, and new money,” the report says. **DM**

# Taiwan’s Tech Diplomacy Has a Labor Problem

Migrant worker recruitment debt threatens the island’s access to Western markets and its ties with Southeast Asia.

By **Ethan Chiu**

October 20, 2026

[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Ftaiwans-tech-diplomacy-has-a-labor-problem%2F&title=Taiwan%E2%80%99s+Tech+Diplomacy+Has+a+Labor+Problem "Share on LinkedIn")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Ftaiwans-tech-diplomacy-has-a-labor-problem%2F "Share on Facebook")[](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Taiwan%E2%80%99s+Tech+Diplomacy+Has+a+Labor+Problem%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Ftaiwans-tech-diplomacy-has-a-labor-problem%2F "Share on Bluesky")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Taiwan%E2%80%99s+Tech+Diplomacy+Has+a+Labor+Problem&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Ftaiwans-tech-diplomacy-has-a-labor-problem%2F "Share on X")

Foreign migrant workers often gather in the square in front of Taipei Station during their day off. Photo taken Sep. 24, 2023.

Credit: [Shutterstock](https://www.shutterstock.com/image-photo/taiwan-taipei-square-front-station-often-2400609447?trackingId=3c2bdff3-e00f-4467-8a4b-b1fba853fb26&listId=searchResults)

Ad

In an investigation [published](https://transparentem.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Debt-Before-Day-One.pdf) this October, three migrant workers at a Garmin factory in Taiwan said recruiters had forced them to sign documents falsely denying the mandatory fees they had paid to get jobs. Two reported that the recruiters threatened to retaliate and deport them if they disclosed the charges. These workers were making products for a U.S.-based electronics company.

The nonprofit Transparentem interviewed 24 workers at seven manufacturers operating in Taiwan and documented recruitment fees totaling $6,400 each. Compal, the laptop maker, and Garmin claimed they had long prohibited worker-paid fees. But they only reimbursed current migrant workers [after](https://transparentem.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Debt-Before-Day-One.pdf) investigators contacted them, and excluded former workers from compensation. Despite corporate promises, these exploitative charges continued.

These findings expose a blind spot in Taiwan’s economic diplomacy. Taipei and Washington should stop treating their technology partnership and Taiwan’s Southeast Asian labor relationships separately. Recruitment abuse threatens Taiwan’s Western market access and regional goodwill. Fair recruitment is just as integral to supply chain security as factory investment.

A framework for reform already exists. The February 2026 Taiwan-U.S. trade agreement [compels](https://ustr.gov/sites/default/files/files/Press/Releases/2026/AIT-TECRO%20ART%20sanitized.pdf) Taiwan to prohibit worker-paid recruitment fees and related costs in manufacturing and fishing within three years of entry into force. Yet on October 6, Premier Cho Jung-tai [said](https://money.udn.com/money/story/7307/9797651) unresolved U.S. trade measures were delaying ratification in Taiwan’s legislature. Tariff negotiations cannot excuse delaying recruitment reform.

Taiwan’s Labor Ministry [counted](https://statdb.mol.gov.tw/html/mon/c12040.htm) more than 910,000 migrant workers at the end of August, including approximately 100,000 lacking valid work permits. Among permit holders, 515,000 worked in manufacturing, with 127,000 of those in the electronics industry. These numbers reveal just how critical migrant labor is to Taiwan’s technology sector.

Rather than stopping at a recruitment fee, the brokerage system often continually exploits workers. Agencies abroad initially charge workers to secure jobs in Taiwan, and Taiwanese brokers then skim recurring service [fees](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=N0090028) off worker bank accounts that they control. Taiwan also [restricts](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=N0090001) migrant workers from changing employment, requiring extensive paperwork and official authorization. Debt and restricted mobility thus reinforce each other.

My fieldwork has revealed what is at stake. In May 2024, I interviewed a Filipino worker at a Hsinchu semiconductor supplier. The worker described 12-hour night shifts, six days a week, and a broker who deducted fees from her wages. Only Catholic missionaries and more experienced migrants offered the worker reliable support.

While debt alone does not establish forced labor, the International Labor Organization (ILO) [recognizes](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@ed_norm/@declaration/documents/publication/wcms_203832.pdf) debt bondage as an indicator of it. For a worker still repaying heavy recruitment fee loans, the cost of reporting abuse could be exceptionally high. Losing their job could not only force them to default on the loan that secured it, but also threaten their family’s very livelihood. Such fear of whistleblowing also makes buyers and regulators less aware of actual factory conditions.

The commercial consequences are stark. In September 2025, U.S. Customs and Border Protection [detained](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/3f42019) imported Giant bicycles and related products manufactured in Taiwan over forced labor concerns. Giant subsequently expanded recruitment fee reimbursements. By September 2026, companies comprising over 80 percent of Taiwan’s bicycle exports had [joined](https://english.cw.com.tw/article/article.action?id=5032) an industry human rights initiative. Customer access restrictions accelerated reform.

Ad

Electronics manufacturers should take notice. The European Union will automatically [block](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/forced-labour-regulation/what-forced-labour-regulation-and-how-does-it-work_en) products made with forced labor by Decembe

title: HKJC Charities Trust shares healthy ageing work at WHO meeting
zh_title: 香港赛马会慈善信托基金于世界卫生组织会议分享健康老龄化工作
summary: 香港 香港赛马会慈善信托基金在世卫组织技术会议上介绍了近三十年的健康老龄化举措，重点介绍了 60 多个项目，耗资 40 亿港元。该信托基金概述了解决健康不平等问题并采取以客户为中心的方法的计划。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 20 日 17:41 HKT · 2 分钟阅读《香港报》赛马会慈善信托基金分享了其近三十年的工作成果
content:
香港
香港赛马会慈善信托基金在世界卫生组织技术会议上介绍了近三十年的健康老龄化举措，重点介绍了超过 60 个项目，资助金额达 40 亿港元。该信托基金概述了解决健康不平等问题并采取以客户为中心的方法的计划。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 20 日 17:41 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

随着人口持续老龄化，香港赛马会慈善信托基金在周二的世界卫生组织技术会议上分享了其近三十年来在健康老龄化方面的工作。

该信托表示，自20世纪90年代末以来，已支持超过60个与健康老龄化相关的项目，获批资金近40亿港元。这些举措涵盖痴呆症护理、心理健康、慢性病和药物管理、行动支持和老年科技，旨在帮助老年人保持健康、活跃并与社区保持联系。

此次会议与世界卫生组织西太平洋区域委员会第 77 届会议同时举行，政府代表、专家和合作伙伴组织齐聚一堂，讨论支持社区健康和独立老龄化的方法。
赛马会健康和老年人慈善机构负责人陈伊梅尔达以“从承诺到行动：通过伙伴关系、创新和投资促进西太平洋地区的健康老龄化”为主题，与地区领导人和专家一起讨论加强卫生系统和对老年人的社区支持。与会者还分享了不同司法管辖区的经验，并探讨了区域学习、技术交流和未来合作的机会。

该信托基金还重点介绍了与香港中文大学的合作，包括赛马会社区电子健康社区关怀项目和赛马会乐龄城市项目。

展望未来，陈表示信托基金将继续支持健康老龄化举措，重点关注解决健康不平等问题。她表示，该信托基金还将采取以客户为中心的方法，帮助社区合作伙伴支持老年人的功能能力并减轻疾病负担。

她说：“我们期待分享中国香港的经验，向朋友和同事学习，并加强与世界卫生组织和区域利益相关者的伙伴关系，以推动卫生系统转型，实现健康老龄化。”
赛马会表示，它通过税收贡献、慈善捐赠和就业产生社会和经济价值的模式支持健康老龄化和其他社区举措。香港赛马会成立于1884年，是一个赛马和娱乐组织，也是香港最大的慈善捐助机构之一。马会表示，2025/26 年度向社会回馈 393 亿港元，其中包括向香港特区政府作出的税项及奖券基金捐款 307 亿港元，以及经批准的慈善捐款 86 亿港元。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust presented nearly three decades of healthy ageing initiatives at a WHO technical meeting, highlighting over 60 projects with HK$4 billion in funding. The Trust outlined plans to address health inequalities and adopt a client-centred approach.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

20 Oct 2026 at 17:41 HKT · 2 min read

The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust shared its nearly three decades of work on healthy ageing at a World Health Organization technical meeting on Tuesday, as populations continue to age.

The Trust said it has supported more than 60 projects related to healthy ageing since the late 1990s, with nearly HK$4 billion in approved funding. The initiatives cover dementia care, mental well-being, chronic disease and medication management, mobility support and gerontechnology, with the aim of helping older adults remain healthy, active and connected to their communities.

The meeting was held alongside the 77th session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific and brought together government representatives, experts and partner organisations to discuss ways to support healthy and independent ageing in communities.

Under the theme "From Commitment to Action: Advancing Healthy Ageing in the Western Pacific through Partnership, Innovation and Investment," Imelda Chan, the Jockey Club's head of charities for health and older adults, joined regional leaders and experts to discuss strengthening health systems and community-based support for older people. Participants also shared experiences from different jurisdictions and explored opportunities for regional learning, technical exchange and future collaboration.

The Trust also highlighted its work with the Chinese University of Hong Kong, including the Jockey Club Community eHealth Community Care Project and the Jockey Club Age-friendly City Project.

Looking ahead, Chan said the Trust would continue supporting healthy ageing initiatives with a focus on addressing health inequalities. She said the Trust would also adopt a client-centred approach to help community partners support older adults' functional ability and reduce disease burdens.

"We look forward to sharing Hong Kong, China's experience, learning from friends and colleagues, and strengthening partnerships with the WHO and regional stakeholders to advance health-system transformation for healthy ageing," she said.

The Jockey Club said it supports healthy ageing and other community initiatives through a model that generates social and economic value through tax contributions, charitable donations and employment. Founded in 1884, the Hong Kong Jockey Club is a horse-racing and entertainment organisation and one of the city's largest charitable donors. The Club said it returned HK$39.3 billion to the community in 2025/26, including HK$30.7 billion in taxes and Lotteries Fund contributions to the HKSAR Government and HK$8.6 billion in approved charitable donations.

title: Taiwan coastguard wards off 16 mainland ships as Beijing turns up the pressure
zh_title: 北京加大施压 台湾海警拦截16艘大陆船只
summary: 台湾海岸警卫队表示，一天之内，16艘中国大陆船只驶入台湾自行定义的限制水域，并通过协调一致的多管齐下行动将其拦截，专家表示，这表明北京海上压力策略的转变。据海巡署称，这些船只包括 12 艘海岸警卫队和科考船，以及四艘渔船，周日在花莲以东、屏东以南、高雄西南部以及台湾控制的东沙群岛周围海域同时作业。 “CGA自始至终监控海事局势
content:
台湾海岸警卫队表示，一天之内，16艘中国大陆船只驶入台湾自行定义的限制水域，并通过协调一致的多管齐下行动将其拦截，专家表示，这表明北京海上压力策略的转变。

据海巡署称，这些船只包括 12 艘海岸警卫队和科考船，以及四艘渔船，周日在花莲以东、屏东以南、高雄西南部以及台湾控制的东沙群岛周围海域同时作业。

中国海警在周日的一份声明中表示，“中国海警在整个行动过程中监视了海上局势，并立即派遣海警船只前往前沿阵地，对大陆船只进行严密监视，并发布警告命令其离开。”

该机构将这些活动描述为“[混合战争](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3220645/chinese-general-calls-military-prepare-hybrid-modern-warfare?module=inline&pgtype=article)”，旨在扩大北京的管辖权主张。

它指责北京“名义上执法，实际上扩大权力”，以营造其对该海域行使管辖权的印象。

此次行动正值安全专家越来越担心北京越来越多地利用海岸警卫队、海上执法船和科考船在台湾周边施加压力，而不是主要依靠中国人民解放军。
02:55

台湾结束年度军演，包括为解放军海上封锁做准备

桃园国防大学解放军事务教授马振坤表示，北京今年的重点已逐渐从海军主导的灰色地带行动转向通过海岸警卫队、海上巡逻和研究船维护管辖权。

马云说：“对于北京来说，此类措施比传统的军事灰色地带行动能产生更具体的成果。”

他将这一做法描述为“离岛夺周边海域”的战略——逐步挤压台湾及其离岛周边海域，但又不引发彻底的军事冲突。

马英九表示，这种做法在南海已经很明显，而且在台湾以东的海域以及金门、马祖、东沙和台湾控制的南沙群岛太平岛周围的海域也越来越多地出现。金门又名金门。

他的评估大体呼应了国际战略研究所 10 月 8 日的分析，该研究所称，自 6 月以来，北京加强了台湾东部的执法、海上监视、渔业和研究活动。

这家总部位于伦敦的智库将中国大陆行为体的扩散描述为北京灰色地带战略的重大发展，可能旨在在台湾周围建立一个涉及军事和民事机构的更复杂的海洋治理体系。
活动的增加也引发了人们的疑问：台湾是否能够在不造成自身海岸警卫队资源紧张的情况下可持续地对船只做出反应。

美国退役海军四星上将、美国太平洋司令部前司令丹尼斯·布莱尔上周在台北举行的海上安全会议上发表视频讲话时表示，台湾不应自动跟踪每艘大陆船只或飞机。

相反，台北应该根据威胁程度分配有限的资源，保留运营能力

【原文 English Original】
Taiwan’s coastguard said it warded off 16 mainland Chinese vessels in one day after they sailed into the island’s self-defined restricted waters in a coordinated, multi-pronged operation that experts say points to a shift in Beijing’s maritime pressure tactics.

The vessels – 12 coastguard and research ships, as well as four fishing boats – operated simultaneously on Sunday in waters east of Hualien, south of Pingtung, southwest of Kaohsiung and around the Taiwan-controlled Dongsha Islands, according to the Coast Guard Administration (CGA).

“The CGA monitored the maritime situation throughout the operation and immediately dispatched coastguard vessels to forward positions, where they closely monitored the mainland vessels and broadcast warnings ordering them to leave,” it said in a statement on Sunday.

The agency described the activities as “[hybrid warfare](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3220645/chinese-general-calls-military-prepare-hybrid-modern-warfare?module=inline&pgtype=article)” intended to expand Beijing’s jurisdictional claims.

It accused Beijing of pursuing “law enforcement in name, expansion of authority in reality” to create the impression that it exercised jurisdiction over the waters.

The operation comes amid growing concern among security experts that Beijing is increasingly using coastguard, maritime law enforcement and research vessels to apply pressure around Taiwan, rather than relying predominantly on the People’s Liberation Army.

02:55

Taiwan concludes annual war games, including preparing for PLA sea blockade

Ma Chen-kun, a professor of PLA affairs at National Defence University in Taoyuan, said Beijing’s focus had gradually shifted this year from navy-led grey-zone operations towards asserting jurisdiction through coastguard, maritime patrol and research vessels.

“For Beijing, such measures produce more concrete results than conventional military grey-zone operations,” Ma said.

He described the approach as a strategy of “leaving the islands but taking away the surrounding seas” – gradually squeezing the waters around Taiwan and its outlying islands without provoking an outright military conflict.

Ma said the approach, already evident in the South China Sea, was increasingly being seen in waters east of Taiwan as well as around Quemoy, Matsu, Dongsha and the Taiwan-controlled Taiping Island in the South China Sea’s Spratly archipelago. Quemoy is also known as Kinmen.

His assessment broadly echoes an October 8 analysis by the International Institute for Strategic Studies, which said Beijing had stepped up law enforcement, maritime surveillance, fisheries and research activities east of Taiwan since June.

The London-based think tank described the proliferation of mainland Chinese actors as a significant development in Beijing’s grey-zone strategy, potentially aimed at establishing a more complex system of maritime governance around Taiwan involving military and civilian agencies.

The increased activity has also raised questions over whether Taiwan can sustainably respond vessel-for-vessel without straining its own coastguard resources.

Dennis Blair, a retired US Navy four-star admiral and former commander of the US Pacific Command, said in a video address to a maritime security conference in Taipei last week that Taiwan should not automatically shadow every mainland ship or aircraft.

Taipei should instead allocate its limited resources according to the level of threat, retain operational flexibility and strengthen maritime surveillance, law enforcement and self-defence capabilities, he said.

02:04

Philippines accuses China of firing a water cannon at its vessels for a second day

Taipei has increasingly looked to learn from the Philippines and its policy of “active transparency”, under which Manila has publicised confrontations with mainland Chinese vessels in the South China Sea.

Taiwan’s coastguard plans to send a vessel carrying about 100 officers and students to the Philippines next October, its first such visit in 53 years. Taipei also [donated](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3368788/why-taiwans-coastguard-vessel-transfer-philippines-has-sparked-double-outcry?module=inline&pgtype=article) a retired patrol vessel to Manila last month.

Taiwan’s National Security Council deputy secretary general Lii Wen has called for greater technological and maritime law enforcement cooperation between the two in areas including maritime domain awareness, unmanned systems and less-lethal weapons.

Sunday’s operation was the latest in a series of encounters this month. Taiwan’s coastguard said it had driven mainland coastguard vessels away from waters around Dongsha on 11 occasions this year, involving 14 vessel appearances before the latest operation.

Since the start of this month, it has warded off 29 mainland coastguard, research, survey and fishing vessel appearances, including 16 from Sunday.

In a more serious incident on October 1, a Taiwanese coastguard vessel [used a water cannon](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3369634/taiwan-coastguard-uses-water-cannons-warn-mainland-chinese-fishing-vessel?module=inline&pgtype=article) to drive away a mainland fishing boat that refused to leave restricted waters near the Dongsha Islands, prompting a strong protest from Beijing.

09:58

Will Batanes become the next South China Sea flashpoint?

For Ma, the broader significance lies in Beijing’s apparent effort to turn repeated peacetime activity into assertions of jurisdiction – pressure that remains below the threshold of armed conflict but could gradually reshape practices in waters surrounding Taiwan.

Blair warned that the threshold would change sharply if Beijing escalated pressure by intercepting or boarding commercial vessels, forcing them to change course or imposing an effective blockade.

Such actions, he said, would move beyond grey-zone coercion and amount to acts of war.

Beijing regards Taiwan as part of China to be reunited by force if necessary. Most countries, including the US, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, but Washington is opposed to any attempt to take the self-ruled island by force and is committed to supplying it with weapons.

title: Moving Manufacturing From China To Mexico
summary: ### Moving Manufacturing From China to Mexico: The Complete Guide When China's COVID-zero lockdowns and its aggression toward Taiwan started spooking foreign companies in 2022, the [international manufacturing lawyers](https://harris-sliwos
content:
### Moving Manufacturing From China to Mexico: The Complete Guide

When China's COVID-zero lockdowns and its aggression toward Taiwan started spooking foreign companies in 2022, the [international manufacturing lawyers](https://harris-sliwoski.com/practice-areas/international-manufacturing-law/) at my firm began getting a steady stream of calls and emails from companies looking to leave China. Most wanted to know about Mexico, and some of the companies calling us were themselves Chinese or Taiwanese. The tariff wars since then have given companies more reasons to look south. Mexico makes sense for many of them. But companies that go into Mexico expecting to find China with a shorter shipping route are in for an expensive education.

Starting in 2022, my good friend Andrew Hupert and I wrote a long series of posts for this blog on what leaving China for Mexico actually involves. Nobody was better suited to write about this than Andrew. I first met him in Shanghai in 2003, and over the following two decades I came to rely deeply on his practical business wisdom, especially about China. When my firm stepped up its China practice, he was one of my go-to people on all things China. He was a business school professor who taught negotiation around the world, and he spent more than 20 years in Asia, living and working in Shanghai, Taipei, Hong Kong, and Saigon. Though he had tied his career to China, he, like me, was an early believer in a post-China manufacturing world. He moved to Thailand and then Vietnam, and when Mexico began emerging as a leading replacement for China manufacturing, he moved to Monterrey and then Oaxaca, and became fluent in Spanish. He spent his last years there helping companies, especially companies leaving China, set up and run operations in Mexico. Few people had spent as much time thinking about how the two countries compared, and fewer still had Andrew's willingness to say exactly what he thought.

Andrew died of a heart attack in Oaxaca in October 2024, at 61. I wrote about him and our friendship in [Remembering Andrew Hupert](https://harris-sliwoski.com/chinalawblog/remembering-andrew-hupert-international-business-guru/). This guide brings our Mexico work together in one place and updates it for 2026. Most of the business and cultural observations are Andrew's, drawn from his years running and advising operations in both countries. The legal and trade analysis is mine, informed by my firm's [affiliated lawyers in Mexico City](https://harris-sliwoski.com/location/mexico-city/) and the United States, and by many of the conclusions Andrew and I reached together over the years. Andrew is no longer here to update his words, so I have done that as best I can. Where events have proved us right or wrong, I say so. When I quote him, the words are his as he wrote them. I want readers to understand where his observations came from and why I continue to think they matter.

### Why Companies Are Leaving China

In early 2023, Andrew and I wrote that running a supply chain entirely through China had become a bet against the house, the kind that ends with the gambler up a ton at midnight and borrowing bus fare home by morning. The trade numbers seemed to argue otherwise. U.S.-China trade had hit a record $690 billion in 2022, and plenty of companies took that as vindication of their decision to stay. Multinationals were reading the situation differently. Their supply chain planners, the Lean Production and Six Sigma people who treat unnecessary risk as a sin, were piling into Mexico, as Unilever's $400 million commitment to a new plant in Nuevo León showed that same month. When a Chinese surveillance balloon was shot down over the United States that February, we predicted that cooler heads would not prevail. Washington, we said, would keep changing the economics of China supply chains by every means available, and Beijing would answer each new U.S. restriction with its own. We saw little reason to expect either government to put the interests of companies caught in the middle ahead of its own political priorities.

We put governments at the top of the list of likely supply chain shocks and said the damage would most likely come through mistakes, meaning bad regulations written and enforced for non-economic goals. Would governments knowingly hurt their own economies for a good soundbite? "Yes. Of course they would. We expected U.S. customs to demand ever more detailed proof that your goods were not made with forced labor in Xinjiang. Complying would trap your China staff in a catch-22, because trying to trace the origin of your materials could get them "invited to tea" by the authorities. We also expected Beijing to retaliate, since, as we put it, "Beijing will not apologize; it will reply." China has a long record of using trade to punish countries that anger it, including Japan, Norway, Canada, South Korea, Australia, and Lithuania. And we warned that after the disruptions of 2021 and 2022, no owner or fiduciary could credibly claim a China supply chain disruption was impossible to foresee. Many of our clients already had China exit and evacuation plans, and we told readers they should too. That advice was based on what we were already seeing companies struggle with, long before the current tariff battles. See [Doing Business with China and Your Reputation Risks](https://harris-sliwoski.com/chinalawblog/doing-business-with-china-and-your-reputation-risks/) and [Repeat After Me: Trade Relations Between the United States and China Will Only Get Worse](https://harris-sliwoski.com/chinalawblog/repeat-after-me-trade-relations-between-the-united-states-and-china-will-only-get-worse/).

Tariffs and trade restrictions have since vindicated much of what we wrote. In 2023, Mexico overtook China as the top source of U.S. goods imports, at $475.6 billion to China's $427.2 billion, with China's total down 20 percent from 2022. Real U.S. imports from China fell 28 percent in 2025 alone, and by year-end the average U.S. tariff on Chinese goods was near 50 percent, up from 21 percent when the second Trump administration took office. Beijing retaliated most effectively with rare earth export controls. It suspended its expanded October 2025 controls for one year, until November 10, 2026, but its April 2025 controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths remain in force. The forced-labor scrutiny we predicted has also become a basis for tariffs. In July 2026, the U.S. Trade Representative imposed tariffs on goods from 60 economies, China and Mexico among them, after finding that they had failed to impose and effectively enforce bans on imports made with forced labor. Our biggest mistake was assuming North American trade would remain politically protected. We underestimated just how willing Washington would be to make life difficult for companies manufacturing in Mexico, a subject I discuss below.

Companies that left China early told us their decisions had paid off. In that same 2023 series, Andrew and I passed along what clients who had moved their manufacturing elsewhere were saying. One said he slept better, both because he worried less about his supply chain and because he felt better about no longer supporting such a brutal regime. Another had left before COVID, which let it avoid the China tariffs, underprice its competitors, and take a good chunk of market share while those competitors scrambled to catch up. Others said they were hiring people who chose them because they had nothing to do with China. Still others had customers choosing them because their products did not come from China, whether to reduce supply chain risk or reputational risk. These were business owners explaining what had happened to their companies, and their experiences were far more persuasive than another consultant's presentation about geopolitical risk. We also said the most unforgivable sin foreign companies committed in China was going there without an exit strategy. I still believe that, and I would build an exit strategy into any Mexico plan from the start as well.

**Which Manufacturing Risks Can You Actually Control?**

One of the most important differences between manufacturing in China and Mexico is how much control you have over the risks your business faces. Every country has problems. Factories lose power, employees leave, suppliers fail, and shipments get delayed. You can reduce many of these risks by investigating your suppliers, choosing your location carefully, and making sure you have alternative sources of supply. You can never eliminate every manufacturing risk, but there is a great deal you can do to keep ordinary business problems from becoming disasters.

Many of Mexico's biggest manufacturing risks fall into that category. Security is a serious concern, but you can investigate specific locations and arrange safer transportation. Labor laws are demanding, but you can hire Mexican employment lawyers and structure your operation to comply with them. Infrastructure varies considerably, but you can check whether a proposed site has reliable power and water before committing to it. None of these precautions guarantees that your operation will run smoothly. They do, however, give you meaningful ways to reduce your exposure.

China presents some risks that no amount of good management can bring under your control. You can investigate your suppliers and trace your materials, but you cannot eliminate the possibility that U.S. Customs will detain your goods over forced-labor concerns. You cannot prevent Beijing from imposing export restrictions or Washington from raising tariffs. You can prepare for a crisis involving Taiwan, but you cannot prevent one. A company can do everything right inside its Chinese factory and still find its business badly damaged by a political decision made thousands of miles away. That is what makes these risks especially troubling. The company has very little ability to influence the decisions that create them.

Mexico has political risks of its own, as the 2026 USMCA review and the latest tariffs demonstrate. A Mexican manufacturer cannot control what Washington decides about North American trade any more than a Chinese manufacturer can control U.S. policy toward China. I would never suggest otherwise. But when comparing countries, I would pay particular attention to which risks you can realistically manage and which ones can overwhelm your business regardless of how carefully you operate. That distinction is one of the strongest reasons many companies have decided they would rather manufacture in Mexico.

**Who Can Still Stay in China**

Andrew's test turned on what you make and who buys it. Several kinds of companies can probably stay in China: those that provide services to Chinese B2B markets, produce for sale in China and Asia, or specialize in multinational supply chains. Companies that depend on an end-to-end global presence, such as hotels, travel companies, and financial services firms, can also stay, as can those big enough to run separate supply chains for separate markets. Companies that need materials, components, technology, or processes available only in China are a maybe. Their position keeps deteriorating, and nobody should want to be the last international manufacturer in China. A company running a low-cost strategy built on small runs of pre-sold products, less-than-container-load shipping, probably cannot stay. The important question is whether your own business falls into one of the categories that still makes economic sense there.

### Is Mexico Right for Your Company?

Andrew's starting point, from the first post of our series, was that comparing China and Mexico is not comparing apples to apples. The same product may leave the factory gate in both countries, but setting up and running operations in them involves very different systems. title: Vivian Kong urges elite sports upgrade to boost Hong Kong's soft power
zh_title: 江若珩促精英体育升级提升香港软实力
summary: 香港立法会议员、前奥运击剑运动员江文慧呼吁优化精英体育训练体系，称运动员是香港软实力的最佳广告。在立法会辩论之前，她概述了四个目标，包括人才管道、体育科学、大湾区合作和国际合作 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编2026 年 10 月 19 日，香港时间 17:35 · 阅读 2 分钟 优化精英运动训练体系，提升香港运动能力
content:
香港
立法会议员、前奥运击剑运动员江文慧呼吁优化精英体育训练体系，称运动员是香港软实力的最佳广告。在立法会辩论之前，她概述了四个目标，包括人才管道、体育科学、大湾区合作和国际合作。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 19 日 17:35 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

运动员出身的立法会议员江文慧表示，优化的精英体育训练体系将增强香港运动员的竞争优势，并成为香港在全球舞台上最强大的软实力展示。

继香港在第 20 届亚运会历史性地夺得 54 枚奖牌之后，她在周三立法会就一项改善精英体育训练和支持系统的动议进行辩论之前发表了上述言论。这位前奥运会击剑金牌得主在接受《旗帜报》姊妹刊物《星岛日报》的采访时，表达了对运动员发展和机构支持持续进步的强烈支持。

“运动员为这座城市参赛，实际上是这座城市培养体育人才和软实力的最好广告，”她说。孔解释说，运动员在国际舞台上的表现直接提升香港的国际形象，增强居民的归属感和自豪感。
她为精英体育训练提出了四个目标，包括培养顶尖运动员以提升香港在世界体育界的地位，以及展示香港的人才培养实力。她补充说，精英运动员可以激励年轻人从事体育运动，推动大众参与并建立社会凝聚力和自豪感。

香港表示，以精英体育为支柱，香港可以推动社区体育、保持重大国际赛事的枢纽地位、提高专业水平、打造体育产业、改善运动员退役后的道路并创造可持续的人才循环。

在谈到资源分配时，她指出，精英体育资金传统上侧重于通过主要投资于最有可能获得主要国际奖牌的运动员和学科来实现回报最大化。她敦促当局全面推广这一方法，同时推进人才输送、体育科学研究、场馆基础设施、大湾区合作和全球体育影响力。

孔特别强调早期人才发掘和双轨教育途径，平衡严格的训练与学术研究，确保全职运动生涯仍然是年轻人才的可行且安全的选择。为了实现训练方案的现代化，她建议更深入地整合运动科学，包括生物力学分析、生理跟踪、量身定制的营养计划和心理咨询。
她还呼吁政府申办重大国际赛事，实行国内设施与海外训练营相结合的混合训练模式。她建议与大湾区城市探索建立训练基地，创造更多比赛和交流机会，并敦促政府争取国际体育机构在香港设立地区总部或办事处，培养本地担任委员和裁判的人才，让香港在比赛规则上有更多发言权。

Hong Kong
Lawmaker and former Olympic fencer Vivian Kong Man-wai has called for an optimised elite sports training system, saying athletes are Hong Kong's best advertisement for soft power. Ahead of a Legco debate, she outlined four goals including talent pipelines, sports science, GBA cooperation and interna

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 17:35 HKT · 2 min read

An optimised elite sports training system would sharpen Hong Kong athletes' competitive edge and serve as the city's strongest soft-power showcase on the global stage, athlete-turned-lawmaker Vivian Kong Man-wai has said.

Her remarks came ahead of a Legislative Council debate on Wednesday on a motion to improve elite sports training and support systems, following Hong Kong's historic 54-medal haul at the 20th Asian Games. In an interview with Sing Tao Daily, the sister publication of The Standard, the former Olympic fencing gold medallist expressed strong backing for sustained advancements in athlete development and institutional support.

"Athletes competing for the city are, in fact, the best advertisement for its ability to nurture sports talent and for its soft power," she said. Kong explained that athletes' performances on the international stage directly raise Hong Kong's global profile and strengthen residents' sense of belonging and pride.

She laid out four goals for elite sports training, including producing top athletes to lift Hong Kong's standing in world sports and showcasing its talent-nurturing strength. Elite athletes, she added, can inspire young people to take up sports, drive mass participation and build social cohesion and pride.

With elite sports as the anchor, Kong said Hong Kong can promote community sports, remain a hub for major international events, raise professionalism and build sports as an industry, improving athletes' post-retirement pathways and creating a sustainable talent cycle.

Addressing resource allocation, she noted that elite sports funding has traditionally focused on maximising returns by investing primarily in competitors and disciplines with the highest probability of securing major international medals. She urged authorities to expand this approach comprehensively by advancing talent pipelines, sports science research, venue infrastructure, Greater Bay Area cooperation and global sporting influence in tandem.

Kong placed special emphasis on early talent scouting and dual-track educational pathways that balance rigorous training with academic study, ensuring full-time athletic careers remain a viable and secure choice for young talent. To modernise training regimens, she recommended deeper integration of sports science, including biomechanical analysis, physiological tracking, tailored nutritional planning and psychological counselling.

She also called on the government to pursue bids for major international competitions and implement a hybrid training model combining domestic facilities with overseas training camps. She recommended exploring training bases with Greater Bay Area cities to create more competition and exchange opportunities, and urged the government to court international sports bodies into opening regional headquarters or offices in Hong Kong to nurture local talent as committee members and referees, giving the city more say over competition rules, resources and major-event bids.
