title: Hong Kong press group urges authorities to scrap new rules tightening media access to land records
zh_title: 香港新闻团体敦促当局废除收紧媒体查阅土地记录的新规定
summary: 香港一个新闻团体敦促政府废除收紧媒体查阅香港土地记录的新规定，并警告称，这些安排将“加剧信息不对称”并损害信息自由。香港土地注册处的网上搜寻服务。照片：屏幕截图。香港记者协会（HKJA）周三呼吁当局搁置可能限制媒体获取土地记录的土地登记法规修正案，土地记录是一个对房地产作为经济支柱的城市新闻报道至关重要的公共数据库。记协也促请立法会
content:
香港一个新闻团体敦促政府废除收紧媒体查阅香港土地记录的新规定，并警告称，这些安排将“加剧信息不对称”并损害信息自由。香港土地注册处的网上搜寻服务。照片：屏幕截图。香港记者协会（HKJA）周三呼吁当局搁置可能限制媒体获取土地记录的土地登记法规修正案，土地记录是一个对房地产作为经济支柱的城市新闻报道至关重要的公共数据库。记协还敦促立法会“慎重考虑”修正案，并敦促当局制定“操作标准”，以保障信息自由流通。香港记协在提交给立法会的一份意见书中表示：“香港长期以来一直坚持自由市场原则，应该为其市场透明度感到自豪，而不是反其道而行之。”根据发展局的声明，法规修正案已于上周在宪报公布，并将于明年生效。目前，对谁可以访问土地记录没有限制，搜索者也不需要提供支持文件。公众只需声明遵守该市的隐私法即可搜索记录。
新规则规定，搜索只能用于被视为访问记录合法的九个目的，包括学术和市场研究。尽管“公共利益”被列为有效理由，但新闻报道并不在九个指定目的之列。然而，任何申请都将由土地注册处处长根据具体情况进行审查。发展局在向立法会提交的文件中表示，此举旨在加强私隐保障。该局表示：“[这些变化]旨在在保护个人数据隐私的需要与保留[土地记录]的作用和目的的重要性之间取得平衡……以确保其透明度和效率。”新闻自由担忧 但记协辩称，没有证据表明之前的安排威胁到隐私。记协表示：“这一说法不足以支持加强搜查，当局不应允许任何有关保护隐私的提及凌驾于公众的知情权之上。”它还认为，新规定将削弱公众和媒体监督房地产市场的能力。香港记者协会。资料图片：HKFP。
记协表示：“根据新规定，土地记录将继续为有商业利益的人进行交易提供便利，而公众或无直接利害关系者若想监督房产所有权和公平交易，则必须首先获得特别批准。这势必严重阻碍利用公共信息打破既得利益。”记协列出了18起利用土地记录进行调查的新闻报道，作为报道的例子，称在收紧的土地查册制度下“无法进行”。香港记者协会主席郑秀玲表示，新规定将“消除”大多数日常房地产报道，并使对潜在土地滥用行为的新闻调查“不可能”。 “新安排的目的是方便那些有商业或既得利益的人进行房产交易，而没有直接利害关系的公众则可以进行房产交易。”

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong press group has urged the government to scrap new rules tightening media access to the city’s land records, warning that the arrangements will “exacerbate information asymmetry” and harm freedom of information. Hong Kong Land Registry’s online search services. Photo: Screenshot. The Hong Kong Journalists Association (HKJA) called on authorities on Wednesday to shelve amendments to land registration regulations that could restrict media access to land records – a public database vital for news reporting in a city where property is a pillar of the economy. The HKJA also urged the Legislative Council (LegCo) to give the amendments “careful consideration” and to press the authorities to set “operational standards” to protect the free flow of information. “Hong Kong has long upheld free-market principles and should take pride in its market transparency rather than move in the opposite direction,” the HKJA said in a submission to LegCo. ‘Strike a balance’ Amendments to the regulations were gazetted last week and will come into effect next year, according to a Development Bureau statement. Currently, there are no restrictions on who may access the land records and searchers do not need to provide supporting documents. Members of the public only need to declare compliance with the city’s privacy laws to search for records. The new rules state that searches can only be conducted for nine purposes deemed legitimate for accessing records, including academic and market research. News reporting is not among the nine specified purposes, although “public interest” is listed as a valid ground. However, any application will be vetted by the Land Registrar on a case-by-case basis. The Development Bureau said in a document submitted to LegCo that the move was intended to strengthen privacy protection. “[The changes] aim to strike a balance between the need to protect personal data privacy and the importance of preserving the role and purpose of the [land records]… to ensure its transparency and efficiency,” the bureau said. Press freedom concerns But the HKJA argued that there was no evidence that the previous arrangements had threatened privacy. “That assertion is not sufficient to support the tightening of searches, and the authorities should not allow a single reference to the protection of privacy to override the public’s right to know,” the HKJA said. It also argued that the new rules will weaken the public’s and the media’s ability to monitor the property market. Hong Kong Journalists Association. File photo: HKFP. “Under the new rules, land records will continue to facilitate transactions for those with commercial interests, while members of the public or parties with no direct interest who wish to monitor property ownership and fair dealing will first have to obtain special approval,” the HKJA said. “This is bound to seriously impede the use of public information to break down entrenched interests,” it added. The HKJA listed 18 investigative news reports that used the land records as examples of reporting that it said “could not be carried out” under the tightened land search system. Selina Cheng, HKJA chair, said that the new rules would “wipe out” most daily property reporting and make journalistic investigations into potential land misuse “impossible.” “What the new arrangement will do is allow convenience to those with commercial or vested interests to conduct property transactions, while members of the public with no direct interest but wishing to monitor how property is used or abused, including the media, must instead jump through extra hoops,” she told HKFP. “The new arrangement will exacerbate information asymmetry between big developers or property owners, and those less resourceful,” she added. Selina Cheng at the Eastern Magistrates’ Court on March 9, 2026. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Hong Kong’s news media have long relied on access to land records and other public registries for investigative reporting. The HKJA noted, however, that access to this information has been restricted in recent years. See also: Hong Kong press group criticises new curbs on media access to vehicle registry, gov’t says accusation ‘false’ In 2024, the government introduced new rules on media access to vehicle records. The move came after a veteran journalist was convicted, and later cleared by the city’s highest court , of making a false statement when accessing the vehicle registry for reporting purposes related to the 2019 protests and unrest. “[O]f 17 applications made by the media for vehicle registration particulars for journalistic purposes, only one was partially approved, and […] only after considerable delay,” the journalists’ group said. The HKJA launched a legal challenge against the government’s restrictions on media access to the vehicle registry in 2024, but the bid was dismissed by the High Court earlier this year.

## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AI[Subscribe](https://news.google.com/subscriptions)

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds signaled he’s open to hitting Chinese electric vehicles with tariffs to win enhanced access to European markets, but would make the call based on UK needs not demands from the EU.

The British government is under political pressure to align with Brussels on imposing tariffs on subsidized car imports from China in exchange for access to the EU-wide procurement model, Made in Europe. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has repeatedly demanded access to the program and making progress on a deal in that area is his key British priority ahead of the UK-EU summit next month.

# ASIAN PARA GAMES/Lin Tzu-yu defends Asian Para Games table tennis title in all-Taiwan final

Taiwanese table tennis player Lin Tzu-yu. Photo courtesy of the Ministry of Sports

Taipei, Oct. 20 (CNA) Taiwan's Lin Tzu-yu (林姿妤) won her second consecutive Asian Para Games women's singles table tennis gold Tuesday, defeating compatriot Tian Shiau-wen (田曉雯) in the class 10 final.

Lin prevailed 11-4, 11-7, 11-2 in just 13 minutes at the Aichi-Nagoya Games in Japan, completing a gold-silver sweep for Taiwan. She also defeated Tian in the final at the previous Games in Hangzhou, China, in 2023.

The longtime doubles partners had secured Taiwan's top two podium places by winning their semifinals earlier Tuesday. Before the final, Tian said she enjoyed the opportunity to face her partner and hoped both would perform at their best.

At the Hangzhou Games, Lin won two gold medals in the women's singles and mixed doubles, as well as a silver in the women's doubles alongside Tian.

(By Li Chien-chung and Chao Yen-hsiang)

美国海军最近因过于关注中东而忽视亚太而受到一些批评。 [美国海军陆战队也不能这样说](https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/10/05/us-marine-corps-anti-ship-weaponry-to-see-exercise-action-on-remote-japan-island-near-taiwan/ “https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/10/05/us-marine-corps-anti-ship-weaponry-to-see-exercise-action-on-remote-japan-island-near-taiwan/”），该战略于 2019 年公布了一项新战略，依靠分散的海军陆战队部队在[群岛]使用无人机和反舰导弹战争]（https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/05/15/us-marines-practice-seizing-remote-islands-in-philippine-exercise/“https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/05/15/us-marines-practice-seizing-remote-islands-in-philippine-exercise/”）以破坏中国的海上扩张。可以说，随着海军陆战队正在美国矛尖发展新能力，美国海军陆战队战略吸引中国国防专家的大量关注也就不足为奇了。本文总结了最近的几项中文评估。
北京对美国海军陆战队新战略的密切关注在一年前就变得清晰起来，当时《环球时报》发表了一篇不同寻常的[社论](https://opinion.huanqiu.com/article/4NlWSpjvMa6“https://opinion.huanqiu.com/article/4NlWSpjvMa6”)，谴责华盛顿在中国附近部署反舰导弹的新决定。本文认为，美国新战略旨在纠正美国海军优先考虑“公海控制”而非“封闭水域近距离交战”的做法，并得出结论认为，华盛顿“控制海上咽喉要道的努力[旨在]限制对手在海上行动的自由……[并]带来新的风险……”。

2025 年初，海军杂志《现代舰船》发表了对美国海军陆战队新战略的更详细研究。中国的这份评估相当震惊地指出，美国海军陆战队正在试验能够发射隐形远程反舰导弹反舰巡航导弹的无人水面舰艇，这些部队也可以充当前沿侦察兵，为美军远程火力确定目标。尽管如此，这一分析仍然凸显了美国海军陆战队战略的一些弱点，包括相关传感器和无人机的射程限制，甚至将美国海军陆战队的防空能力描述为“不稳定”。该杂志的另一项研究早些时候曾引起人们对新战略引发的物流困境的关注。
另一本中国海军附属杂志《舰载武器》对 2026 年中国的分析对海军陆战队的新做法提出了更为尖锐的批评，指出海军陆战队濒海团（MLR）的创建“实际上代表了美国海军陆战队为军事干预中国统一而进行的战役准备”。这项研究一开始就指出，许多美国智库对该战略提出了质疑，认为没有海上和空中控制的前沿基地可能“站不住脚”。

这项分析承认，新的

【原文 English Original】
#### [Opinion](https://defensenews.com/opinion)

By Lyle Goldstein

Oct 20, 2026, 09:09 AM

U.S. Marines prepare for a counter-landing live fire exercise during the annual US-Philippines joint military "Balikatan" exercise in Rizal, Palawan, Philippines, on April 28, 2025. (Jam Sta Rosa / AFP via Getty Images)

The U.S. Navy has taken some heat recently for focusing too heavily on the Middle East and neglecting the Asia-Pacific. The same cannot be [said of the U.S. Marine Corps](https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/10/05/us-marine-corps-anti-ship-weaponry-to-see-exercise-action-on-remote-japan-island-near-taiwan/ "https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/10/05/us-marine-corps-anti-ship-weaponry-to-see-exercise-action-on-remote-japan-island-near-taiwan/"), which unveiled a new strategy in 2019 relying on dispersed groups of Marines to wield drones and anti-ship missiles in [archipelagic warfare](https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/05/15/us-marines-practice-seizing-remote-islands-in-philippine-exercise/ "https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2026/05/15/us-marines-practice-seizing-remote-islands-in-philippine-exercise/") in order to unhinge Chinese maritime expansion. As the Marines are developing new capabilities at the pointy end of the American spear, so to speak, it’s not surprising that USMC strategy is attracting lots of attention from Chinese defense experts. This article summarizes several recent Chinese-language assessments.

The close attention that Beijing is paying to the new USMC strategy became clear about a year ago when the Global Times [环球时报] published an unusual [editorial](https://opinion.huanqiu.com/article/4NlWSpjvMa6 "https://opinion.huanqiu.com/article/4NlWSpjvMa6") decrying Washington’s new determination to deploy anti-ship missiles proximate to China. Arguing that the new American strategy aims to correct a U.S. Navy prioritization for “open ocean control” rather than “close-quarters engagement in confined waters,” this article concludes that Washington’s effort to “control maritime chokepoints [aims to] curtail the freedom of rivals to operate at sea … [and] introduces new risks … .”

A much more detailed study of the new USMC strategy appeared in early 2025 in the naval magazine Modern Ships [现代舰船]. This Chinese assessment noted with considerable alarm that the USMC was experimenting with unmanned surface vessels capable of firing the stealthy LRASM anti-ship cruise missile and that these units could alternatively serve as forward scouts, fixing targets for long-range U.S. military fires. Still, this analysis underlines some weaknesses of the USMC strategy, including the range limitations of related sensors and drones, and even characterized the air-defense capabilities of the USMC as “precarious.” Another study in this same magazine had earlier drawn attention to the logistics quandaries raised by the new strategy.

A 2026 Chinese analysis in another Chinese navy-affiliated magazine, Shipborne Weapons [舰载武器], offers a sharper critique of the Marines’ new approach, noting that the creation of the Marine Littoral Regiments (MLR) “actually represents campaign preparation by the USMC to militarily intervene in China’s unification.” At the outset, this study notes that many American think tanks raised doubts about the strategy, suggesting that forward bases without sea and air control could prove “untenable.”

There is a recognition in this analysis that the new mobile missile launchers that are being deployed by the USMC are small, light, and thus “not easily discovered by … surveillance.” In the end, this study concludes that the USMC strategy is vulnerable because the “U.S has no way to quickly establish air superiority. This could take weeks or months and would entail massive losses.”

Among the most remarkable pieces written by Chinese experts on the new USMC direction is one that was [published](https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cmsi-translations/76/ "https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cmsi-translations/76/") in translation recently by the China institute at U.S. Naval War College (NWC). That translation deserves extra attention due to the fact that it was written by senior active-duty Chinese Navy officers and also because it was published originally in a sensitive internal circulation Chinese military journal too.

Though this piece does not touch directly on the sensitive Taiwan issue, and it also explicitly notes the USMC strategy aims at deterrence of Beijing, it nevertheless explains that the new USMC deployments amount to “continuous penetration and encroachment into our near seas” and argues that China must “establish effective countermeasures.” Notably, this high-level rendering links the USMC strategy to China’s improving submarine force in significant detail, observing that forward deployed Marine forces could deploy “hydro-acoustic arrays and other assets to establish barrier zones and monitoring areas to track Chinese submarine operations.” Similar arguments are made that U.S. deployments could degrade Chinese air defenses by employing drone swarms “to overwhelm our radar tracking capacity.”

The Chinese Navy authors caution against applying resource-intensive assets to defeat such American asymmetric tactics. However, the conclusion of the article is rather disturbing since it argues that China must counter this posture by deploying a Chinese “proactive offensive posture, aggressively expand[ing] our operational reach, [and] project[ing] forces forward.” Elaborating, they counsel: “We must maintain and normalize forward-deployed forces, extend[ing] undersea combat capabilities as far forward as feasible.”

This conclusion and other aspects of these Chinese-language analyses raise some rather uncomfortable questions for U.S. defense planners. The final translation done by NWC strongly hints that the Chinese Navy may be adopting a more aggressive approach as a direct reaction to the forward lean in American strategy. This seems to be a very clear manifestation of the so-called ‘security dilemma,’ wherein two powers’ defensive measures develop into a dangerous escalatory spiral. Moreover, there is a clear recognition by Chinese strategists that forward USMC elements could be vulnerable due to logistics challenges and lack of proper air and missile defenses. It would not be the first time that the USMC was deployed [haphazardly](https://www.usmcu.edu/Outreach/Marine-Corps-University-Press/MCH/Marine-Corps-History-Winter-2025-26/Remembering-Chosin/ "https://www.usmcu.edu/Outreach/Marine-Corps-University-Press/MCH/Marine-Corps-History-Winter-2025-26/Remembering-Chosin/") in East Asia at the cost of many American lives.

Understanding these dynamics, American leaders should recalibrate and opt to rely less on forward defense. Alternatively, the USMC should aim to embrace the strategic depth of the Pacific and its myriad island archipelagos (e.g. the Philippines) in a less costly, less risky, more sustainable, and clearly defensive strategy.

_Lyle Goldstein is director of the China Initiative at Brown University’s Watson School and concurrently serves as director of the Asia Program at the think-tank Defense Priorities._

summary: 中新社台北10月20日电 交易商称，由于担心持有大量空头头寸的外国机构投资者将在现货市场抛售期货以获取利润，台湾股市周二收低，周三10月期货合约结算日之前。台湾证券交易所基准指数在 46,163.03 点至 46,967.91 点之间波动，最终下跌 529.15 点，至 46,292.93 点，跌幅为 1.13%。成交总额为新台币 7,586.8 亿元（合 233.5 亿美元），而周一为新台币 8,667.1 亿元。该指数上午交易价格高于前收盘价
content:
中新社台北10月20日电 交易商称，由于担心持有大量空头头寸的外国机构投资者将在现货市场抛售期货以获取利润，台湾股市周二收低，周三10月期货合约结算日之前。

台湾证券交易所基准指数在 46,163.03 点至 46,967.91 点之间波动，最终下跌 529.15 点，至 46,292.93 点，跌幅为 1.13%。成交总额为新台币 7,586.8 亿元（合 233.5 亿美元），而周一为新台币 8,667.1 亿元。

交易商表示，由于美国科技股隔夜反弹引发买盘，该指数早盘交易价格高于前收盘价，但随后出现抛售，全线蔓延，导致主板在交易结束时跌至负值区域。

摩尔证券投资咨询分析师Adam Lin表示：“外国机构投资者持有的空头期货合约比多头合约多约92,000份。”

他表示：“投资者在期货结算前减持了持仓，因为他们担心更多外国机构将随之抛售，资金将因美元走强而从台湾撤出。”

据台交所称，周二外国机构投资者在主板净售股新台币795.4亿美元。本月初以来，外资机构净卖出总额已达新台币6,620.7亿元。
林说，随着投资者隔夜摆脱美国科技股上涨的影响，半导体行业的抛售加剧，特别是由于韩国存储芯片供应商三星电子公司和SK海力士公司周二上午遭受损失。

在台北，存储芯片生产商南亚科技股价下跌 3.21%，收于新台币 422.00 元；旺宏国际股价下跌 1.96%，收于新台币 100.00 元。

智能手机IC设计商联发科技下跌1.31%，收于新台币4,150.00元，而占总市值超过40%的合约芯片制造商台积电(TSMC)则表现出弹性，仅下跌0.62%，收于新台币2,405.00元。

科技板块其他方面，电源管理解决方案供应商台达电子下跌2.13%，收于新台币1,605.00元，但iPhone组装商和AI服务器制造商鸿海精密工业股份有限公司却逆势上涨0.84%，收于新台币241.50元。

林说：“非科技股也未能幸免于对外国机构抛售的担忧，这给大盘带来了压力。”

金融指数下跌2.36%，国泰金控跌3.93%，收于新台币110.00元；富邦金控跌3.15%，收于新台币153.50元。
与此同时，台塑跌4.22%，收于新台币74.90元；南亚塑胶跌2.47%，收于新台币296.00元。与此同时，和泰汽车跌1.48%，收于新台币532.00元；裕隆汽车跌1.02%，收于新台币29.10元。

“从今天较小的成交量来看，我怀疑许多投资者不愿意逢低买入，因为他们对后市持谨慎态度，”林说。 “台交所可能很快会在 46,042 点（60 日移动平均线）之前测试最近的技术支撑位。”

（弗朗西斯·黄）

结局/ASG

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 20 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan closed lower Tuesday ahead of the October futures contracts settlement date Wednesday amid fears that foreign institutional investors, who hold a large chunk of short positions, will sell in the spot market for profits in futures, dealers said.

The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended down 529.15 points, or 1.13 percent, at 46,292.93 after moving between 46,163.03 and 46,967.91. Turnover totaled NT$758.68 billion (US$23.35 billion), compared with Monday's NT$866.71 billion.

The index traded above the previous close during the morning session on buying sparked by a rebound of U.S. tech stocks overnight, but selling followed, spreading across the board to send the main board to negative territory at the end of trading, dealers said.

"Foreign institutional investors owned about 92,000 more short-position futures contracts than long-position contracts," Moore Securities Investment Consulting analyst Adam Lin said.

"Investors just trimmed their holdings before the futures settlement as they feared more foreign institutional selling will follow and funds will be expatriated from Taiwan on a stronger U.S. dollar," he said

According to the Taiwan Stock Exchange, foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$79.54 billion of shares on the main board Tuesday. Since the beginning of this month, a foreign institutional net sell has totaled NT$662.07 billion.

With investors shrugging off a U.S. tech rally overnight, selling in the semiconductor industry intensified, particularly, due to losses suffered by South Korea's memory chip suppliers Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. Tuesday morning, Lin said.

In Taipei, memory chip producers Nanya Technology Corp. shed 3.21 percent to close at NT$422.00, and Macronix International Co. ended down 1.96 percent at NT$100.00.

Smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. slid 1.31 percent to close at NT$4,150.00, while contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which accounts for over 40 percent of total market value, appeared resilient, down only 0.62 percent to end at NT$2,405.00.

Elsewhere in the tech sector, power management solution provider Delta Electronics Inc. shed 2.13 percent to close at NT$1,605.00, but iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. bucked the downturn, up 0.84 percent to end at NT$241.50.

"Nontech stocks were not spared by concerns over foreign institutional selling, adding pressure to the broader market," Lin said.

With the financial index down 2.36 percent, Cathay Financial Holding Co. lost 3.93 percent to close at NT$110.00, and Fubon Financial Holding Co. ended down 3.15 percent at NT$153.50.

Meanwhile, Formosa Plastics Corp. shed 4.22 percent to close at NT$74.90, and Nan Ya Plastics Corp. ended down 2.47 percent at NT$296.00. Meanwhile, Hotai Motor Co. lost 1.48 percent to close at NT$532.00, and Yulon Motor Co. ended down 1.02 percent at NT$29.10.

"Judging from today's smaller turnover. I suspect many investors were reluctant to buy on the dip as they were cautious about the market outlook," Lin said. "The Taiex could soon test the nearest technical support ahead of 46,042 points, the 60-day moving average."

(By Frances Huang)

# China Builds US Destroyer Replica in Desert, Sharpening Anti-Ship Missile Training

## A full-scale Arleigh Burke-class mock-up in the Taklamakan Desert could support more realistic missile-seeker testing, with implications for US naval intervention in a Taiwan conflict.

[English](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/category/english-en/)[International](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/category/news/international-en/)[News](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/category/news/)

[By **admin**](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/author/dsa-a/ "Browse Author Articles")On **Oct 20, 2026**

**Share**[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdefencesecurityasia.com%2Fen%2Fchina-us-destroyer-replica-desert-anti-ship-missile-testing%2F)[](https://twitter.com/share?text=China%20Builds%20US%20Destroyer%20Replica%20in%20Desert,%20Sharpening%20Anti-Ship%20Missile%20Training&url=https%3A%2F%2Fdefencesecurityasia.com%2Fen%2Fchina-us-destroyer-replica-desert-anti-ship-missile-testing%2F)[](whatsapp://send?text=China%20Builds%20US%20Destroyer%20Replica%20in%20Desert,%20Sharpening%20Anti-Ship%20Missile%20Training%20%0A%0A%20https%3A%2F%2Fdefencesecurityasia.com%2Fen%2Fchina-us-destroyer-replica-desert-anti-ship-missile-testing%2F)[](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/china-us-destroyer-replica-desert-anti-ship-missile-testing/)

**(DEFENCE SECURITY ASIA) — China’s construction of a full-scale replica of a U.S. Navy Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer in the Taklamakan Desert marks a significant escalation in the realism and sophistication of the People’s Liberation Army’s anti-access and area-denial warfare preparations.**

**Commercial satellite imagery captured near Ruoqiang in Xinjiang Province reveals a highly detailed three-dimensional mock-up replicating the approximate 155-meter dimensions, superstructure geometry, and radar signature characteristics of a modern Arleigh Burke Flight IIA or Flight III destroyer.**

**The replica represents far more than a symbolic training aid because it directly supports the PLA Rocket Force’s evolving mission to neutralize U.S. naval power projection capabilities during a potential Taiwan Strait conflict.**

**The development emerges as [military](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/china-us-destroyer-replica-desert-anti-ship-missile-testing/#) planners in Washington increasingly assess that any Chinese move against Taiwan would almost certainly involve attempts to delay, disrupt, or deter U.S. carrier strike group intervention in the Western Pacific battlespace.**

Teroka Pertahanan

**Unlike earlier two-dimensional ship outlines observed at the same desert range since 2021, the new structure incorporates radar reflectors, elevated superstructure simulations, and physical geometry intended to reproduce realistic radar cross-sections for advanced missile seeker testing.**

**The Taklamakan Desert range has already hosted mock-ups of Ford-class aircraft carriers, multiple destroyer silhouettes, and mobile rail-mounted maritime targets designed to simulate maneuvering warships under combat conditions.**

**Military analysts assess that the new replica is specifically optimized for validating anti-ship ballistic missiles such as the DF-21D and DF-26, alongside emerging hypersonic strike systems and AI-assisted targeting architectures.**

**The strategic objective behind these tests is not merely missile accuracy but the refinement of the entire anti-ship “kill chain,” including satellite detection, target identification, sensor fusion, terminal guidance, electronic warfare resistance, and battle damage assessment.**

**Arleigh Burke-class destroyers represent one of the most critical operational nodes within U.S. naval force posture because they provide Aegis ballistic missile defense, anti-submarine warfare, air defense coordination, and Tomahawk long-range strike capability.**

**In any Taiwan contingency, Burke destroyers would likely form the protective outer layer around U.S. carrier strike groups operating east of Taiwan or within the Philippine Sea to complicate PLA amphibious operations.**

**Although analysts caution that the development does not necessarily indicate an imminent invasion timeline, the replica underscores how deeply integrated Taiwan contingency planning has become within China’s broader military modernization and strategic deterrence doctrine.**

## **China’s Arleigh Burke Replica Signals a New Phase in PLA A2/AD Operational Maturity**

**The construction of a realistic U.S. destroyer target reflects the PLA’s transition from theoretical anti-access doctrine toward increasingly operationalized and technologically integrated anti-ship warfare preparation.**

**Earlier desert mock-ups relied heavily on flat visual outlines that primarily supported basic targeting calibration, whereas the new three-dimensional structure enables far more sophisticated radar, infrared, and terminal guidance validation under simulated combat conditions.**

**This shift is strategically important because modern naval warfare increasingly depends on multi-domain sensor fusion rather than simple visual acquisition or conventional ballistic targeting methodologies.**

**By reproducing the complex radar profile of an Arleigh Burke destroyer, the PLA can evaluate whether missile seekers can discriminate between operational combatants, electronic decoys, chaff clouds, and deceptive signature management systems during high-intensity conflict.**

**Such capability directly supports China’s anti-access and area-denial strategy designed to keep U.S. naval forces beyond effective intervention range during a Taiwan Strait contingency.**

**The DF-21D and DF-26 anti-ship ballistic missiles already represent core components of China’s regional deterrence architecture, with reported ranges capable of threatening U.S. carrier groups operating across the Western Pacific.**

**The addition of hypersonic glide vehicles and AI-assisted targeting algorithms could potentially compress U.S. reaction times while complicating existing missile defense interception windows.**

**The Taklamakan Desert range provides ideal testing conditions because the isolated environment allows live-fire experimentation without maritime traffic constraints or immediate foreign surveillance interference.**

content:
A Lifeline for Healing and Hope

My name is Lori Engel. I’m 59, homebound in Oregon. I live completely alone with life-altering neurological injuries and disabilities that have reshaped every part of my world.

My Background

I grew up as a missionary child in Brazil, where faith, service, and compassion became the foundation of my life. As an adult, I carried that forward—serving six years as a missionary teacher in Taiwan, then eleven years as a chaplain, walking alongside people in illness, grief, crisis, and loss. Caring for others wasn’t just my work; it was my identity. The last two years of my career, I was the Director of Chaplain Services for a healthcare organization.

Prior to becoming a chaplain, I was an English teacher for almost two decades, teaching both in Taiwan and at universities in the U.S.

How Everything Changed

That path shifted profoundly starting in late 2006. Over time, I sustained multiple traumatic brain injuries and a toxic reaction to Cipro that damaged my nerves and muscles. I developed serious neurological conditions, including cerebellar damage, ataxia, polyneuropathy, spasticity, severe balance impairment, swallowing difficulties, and vision disturbances, to name a few. These affect my ability to walk, stand, use my arms consistently, regulate my nervous system, or handle even basic daily tasks.

Despite these initial injuries, I continued working as a chaplain until 2015, pushing through pain and limitations to serve others, through God's grace and the aid of nutraceuticals. Additional neurological injuries in 2015 made it impossible to continue, leaving me homebound ever since, unable to drive.

Here is a brief summary of all my injuries:

My injuries consist of multiple TBIs (traumatic brain injury) from falling backward onto the kitchen tile floor, hitting the back of my head; slamming my forehead into a concrete bunk bed; and falling and hitting the side of my head here in Oregon. I also experienced medical malpractice that damaged my cervical spine. I was erroneously prescribed fluroquinolones Avelox and Cipro for 30 days straight, which severely damaged my nerves and tendons. (The FDA has issued warnings about these drugs.) Then I got a bad infection. Later, I also experienced thermal burns to my spine and base of my head.

Then, I was exposed to and living in wildfires so severe that ashes were all around me here in Oregon in 2020, which exponentially exacerbated all my autonomic, nerve, and vascular damage, as well as breathing. Then in 2021 I had Covid, which causes neurological issues in even healthy people. For me, it created additional issues.

There has been a compounded, cumulative effect of all the layered injuries. Most people struggle to comprehend such a parade of horribles, but I do have records.

It has been more than I can ever put into words. I am just thankful to be alive. I am thankful for the many years I worked as a chaplain, until there were just too many injuries.

My Daily Reality

Simple things most people take for granted—opening a package, standing at the sink, stepping outside, or even too much visual input—can overload my fragile system, causing loss of balance, neurological shutdown, or crushing exhaustion. Some days I can’t get out of bed. Others, I push through just to care for myself and my faithful dog Teddie, only to crash afterward.

I haven’t seen my family in 13 years (they live on the East Coast), and for the last 10-plus years I can’t travel. I receive no family financial support. The isolation is profound, and Teddie—my constant companion, emotional anchor, and service companion in many ways—is one of the biggest reasons I keep going, in addition to God's miraculous care.

What I Am Fighting For

Yet every day, I fight to heal and hold onto as much independence as possible. As my health allows, I write devotional pieces that integrate faith, neuroscience, and psychology—sharing insights on resilience, hope, and spiritual growth on social media. It’s a small but meaningful way I continue to give back and encourage others, even from home.

My lifeline is an intensive, carefully managed regimen: specialized therapies, targeted nutrition, and essential supplements that stabilize my brain, muscles, emotions, and overall functioning. When I can stay consistent with these protocols, I feel more like myself—steadier, clearer, hopeful. When I can’t, everything declines quickly: neurologically, physically, and emotionally.

How Your Support Helps

My disability income is severely limited (SSDI), and it does not even cover rent. Ongoing costs far exceed what I can cover. Neurological medications/nutraceuticals alone are expensive and not covered by Medicare. I also need nutritious food tailored to my conditions, basic utilities, in-home support, and care for Teddie.

I’m not asking for luxuries—only the basics that allow me to continue healing, stay safe at home, avoid further decline, and keep writing when possible.

Your monthly - or one-time - support will directly help cover:

• Essential neurological and immunological supplements to stabilize my system and medical care not covered by Medicare.

• Food and daily living necessities

• Basic in-home support and utility expenses

• Veterinary care, food, and supplies for Teddie, my vital companion

• Unexpected critical needs that protect my independence and safety

A Message of Gratitude and Hope

Every gift—no matter the size—becomes part of this lifeline. It prevents eviction. It helps me get through the hardest days, hold onto hope for continued (even if gradual) improvement.

Sharing this campaign is also a huge gift. When you’re largely invisible due to homebound disability, profound isolation, and no nearby support network, awareness can make all the difference.

After a lifetime of caring for others, I now humbly need care myself. It’s been a difficult shift, but I’m grateful for every act of kindness.God has never failed me during these long, lonely years.

It's been a long, agonizing road, but I still believe healing is possible. I still hold fast to faith that God can bring restoration, step by step—and use even my writing to touch lives. I will never stop trying.

Thank you for seeing me, for caring, and for helping carry what I cannot carry alone. Your support—financial, prayerful, or simply shared—means more than words can express.

With deepest gratitude and hope,

Lori Engel

"Out of suffering come the strongest souls."

(With friends who brought Lori food in 2017)

In 2021, after wounds discovered under hair

2026

In 2009, as a chaplain.

title: Starlux adds fourth weekly Taipei-Prague flight - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 星宇航空增加每周第四趟台北至布拉格航班 - 焦点台湾
summary: 中新社布拉格10月18日电 台湾最新的国际航空公司星宇航空周日表示，从10月1日起，该航空公司将其台北-布拉格直飞航班从8月份开通时的每周三班增加到每周四班。加上中华航空每周三班的台北-布拉格航班，此次扩建为旅客提供了台湾与捷克首都之间的每日直达航班选择。华航于2023年开通布拉格航线，并于4月增至每周三班。 Starlux 于 8 月 1 日开通布拉格航线，成为其首个欧洲目的地，成为第二个目的地
content:
中新社布拉格10月18日电 台湾最新的国际航空公司星宇航空周日表示，从10月1日起，该航空公司将其台北-布拉格直飞航班从8月份开通时的每周三班增加到每周四班。

加上中华航空每周三班的台北-布拉格航班，此次扩建为旅客提供了台湾与捷克首都之间的每日直达航班选择。

华航于2023年开通布拉格航线，并于4月增至每周三班。

星宇航空于8月1日开通布拉格航线，作为其首个欧洲目的地，成为第二家直飞捷克首都的台湾航空公司。

星宇航空发言人梁文龙表示，该航线8月客座率为82%，尽管欧洲旅游淡季，但在捷克经台湾飞往日本的旅客的帮助下，预计11月客座率将保持在80%以上。

梁表示，预计直航不仅能促进双向旅游，还能促进涉及台湾半导体供应链的投资和商业合作。

据捷克旅游局统计，2026年前8个月，台湾赴捷克游客人数达10.88万人次，同比增长5.9%。仅8月份，入境游客人数同比增长21.1%，达到15,900人。

此次扩张也正值台湾半导体供应商继台积电在德国德累斯顿的项目之后增加对中欧的投资。
其中包括TaMiCo Technology Taiwan Ltd.，该公司计划在靠近德国边境的捷克拉贝河畔乌斯季地区建造一家半导体元件清洗和表面处理工厂。

布拉格仍然是首选目的地，主要景点包括 14 世纪的查理大桥、老城广场、天文钟和佩特任缆车。

为了推广这条路线，Starlux 任命流行偶像蔡依林为品牌大使，为其热门歌曲《布拉格广场》制作新版本。

该航空公司还部署了两架空客 A350-1000 喷气客机，涂上由日本艺术家 Hajime Sorayama 创作的特殊“Sorayama Gold”和“Sorayama Silver”涂装，并于 10 月 1 日推出了从办理登机手续到机上设施的全面“AIRSORAYAMA”主题航班。

梁说，艺术主题飞机也带动了其他航线的高载客率，东京清晨航班的平均载客率约为 90%，凤凰城航班的表现也继续强劲。

（蒋明彦、高伊芙撰）

Prague, Oct. 18 (CNA) Starlux Airlines, Taiwan's newest international carrier, has increased its Taipei-Prague service to four nonstop flights a week from Oct. 1, up from three when the route was launched in August, the airline said Sunday.

Together with China Airlines' three weekly Taipei-Prague services, the expansion gives travelers a daily nonstop option between Taiwan and the Czech capital.

China Airlines launched its Prague route in 2023 and increased it to three weekly flights in April.

Starlux inaugurated its Prague route on Aug. 1 as its first European destination, becoming the second Taiwanese carrier to fly direct to the Czech capital.

Starlux spokesperson Walter Liang (梁文龍) said the route's passenger load factor was 82 percent in August and is expected to stay above 80 percent in November despite the low season for European travel, helped by Czech travelers flying to Japan via Taiwan.

Liang said the direct service is expected to boost not only two-way tourism but also investment and business cooperation involving Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain.

According to CzechTourism, Taiwanese visitor arrivals in Czechia reached 108,800 in the first eight months of 2026, up 5.9 percent from a year earlier. In August alone, arrivals rose 21.1 percent year on year to 15,900.

The expansion also comes as Taiwanese semiconductor suppliers increase investments in Central Europe following Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s project in Dresden, Germany.

They include TaMiCo Technology Taiwan Ltd., which plans to build a plant for cleaning and surface-treating semiconductor components in the Czech region of Ústí nad Labem, near the German border.

Prague remains a top destination, with major attractions including the 14th-century Charles Bridge, Old Town Square, the Astronomical Clock, and the Petřín Funicular cable car.

To promote the route, Starlux named pop icon Jolin Tsai (蔡依林) as brand ambassador to produce a new version of her hit song "Prague Square."

The airline also deployed two Airbus A350-1000 jetliners in special "Sorayama Gold" and "Sorayama Silver" liveries created with Japanese artist Hajime Sorayama, and on Oct. 1 launched fully "AIRSORAYAMA"-themed flights, from check-in to onboard amenities.

Liang said the art-themed aircraft have also driven high load factors on other routes, with early-morning Tokyo flights averaging around 90 percent and Phoenix services continuing to perform strongly.

(By Jiang Ming-yan and Evelyn Kao)

content:
## Details

**Dawns** is a community for history enthusiasts interested in understanding the big picture of human history.
 The way it works is that there is a different theme each month:

*   January: **the natural world** (kinship or commodity)
*   February: **industrial modernisation** (industrial revolutions 1-4)
*   March: **"the axial age"** (Moses, Buddha, Socrates, Laozi, Zoroaster)
*   April: **literary history** (oral to internet)
*   May: **energy** (from muscle to nuclear)
*   June: **different modes of living** (e.g. pastoralists, fishing)
*   July: **history of science** (Aristotle, Newton etc)
*   August: **politics and power** (tribes to superpowers)
*   September: **art history** (who and what is art for?)
*   October: **cradles of civilisation** (Egypt, Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Yellow River, Olmecs and Chico Norte)
*   November: **economics and trade** (bartering to bitcoin?)
*   December: **progressive revelation** (Abraham, Moses, Jesus Christ, Muhammed, Baháʼu'lláh)

There are 5 recommended texts each month - you can read one or more of them if you'd like and this will form the basis of the live discussion.

This is considered an "intentional community" which exists to study human history in the spirit of common humanity.

So it's like a community which agrees that the world needs a new meta-narrative because the old ones are mutually exclusive and seen as not inclusive enough by broad segments of the population - which is driving culture wars and distracting massively from sustainable development.

We don't purport to dictate the meta-narrative of human history - however we intend to help people build their own meta-narratives or meta-frameworks for understanding how all people are part of the same story and share common heritage.

Please join us on telegram to build friendships and feel belonging [https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns](https://www.launchpass.com/brites/dawns).

title: 15 contractors rated 'extremely poor' in Hong Kong site safety over five years
zh_title: 五年来香港15家承包商在工地安全方面被评为“极差”
summary: 香港发展局局长表示，在过去五年的季度报告中，有一家承包商在工地安全方面被评为“较差”，有 15 个承包商被评为“极差”。政府在投标评估中考虑安全分数，并可以暂停或摘牌公司。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 21 日 12:37 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 Hong香港发展局局长颜汉豪透露，在过去五年中，有一家承包商获得了“差”评级
content:
香港
香港发展局局长表示，在过去五年的季度报告中，有一家承包商在工地安全方面被评为“较差”，有 15 个承包商被评为“极差”。政府在投标评估中考虑安全分数，并可以暂停或摘牌公司。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 21 日 12:37 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港发展局局长颜汉豪透露，过去5年，有1家承包商在其季度评估报告中获得工地安全表现“差”的评级，另有15家承包商被评为“极差”。这些数字是在对立法者问题的书面答复中提供的。

恩贡解释说，政府评估公共工程合同投标时不仅考虑价格，还考虑技术评分，其中工地安全约占30%。安全绩效不合格的承包商必须立即实施改进，并可能面临暂停招标或从批准名单中除名等处罚。
发展部长表示，现行系统有效识别高风险和管理不善的合同，从而能够及早干预并迅速采取补救措施。工务部门和房屋委员会定期进行检查、安全审计和突击检查，以评估承包商的安全管理制度、风险控制措施和实际执行情况。评分过程不仅仅依赖于事故数量。

预警机制到位：当事故发生率或数量超过基准时，将采取后续行动。必要时当局也会积极配合劳工部的调查。

恩贡指出，政府近年来加强了预防措施，包括推广使用创新技术来加强工地风险识别和控制。主要措施包括采用“智慧安全工地”系统，及早发现不安全行为和潜在风险。房委会要求承包商将此类系统的安全数据输入其“AI+建筑智能平台”，以加强对安全绩效的监控并提高一线工人的安全意识。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Hong Kong's Development Secretary said one contractor was rated 'poor' and 15 'extremely poor' for site safety in quarterly reports over five years. The government considers safety scores in bid evaluations and can suspend or delist firms.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

21 Oct 2026 at 12:37 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong's Development Secretary, Ngon Hon-ho, has revealed that over the past five years, one contractor received a 'poor' rating for site safety performance in its quarterly assessment report, while 15 were rated 'extremely poor'. The figures were provided in a written reply to a lawmaker's question.

Ngon explained that the government evaluates public works contract bids by considering not only price but also technical scores, of which site safety accounts for about 30 per cent. Contractors with unsatisfactory safety performance are required to implement immediate improvements and may face penalties including suspension from tendering or removal from the approved list.

The Development Secretary said the current system effectively identifies high-risk and poorly managed contracts, enabling early intervention and prompt remedial measures. Public works departments and the Housing Authority conduct regular inspections, safety audits and surprise checks to assess contractors' safety management systems, risk control measures and actual implementation. The scoring process does not rely solely on accident numbers.

Warning mechanisms are in place: when accident rates or numbers exceed benchmarks, follow-up actions are taken. Authorities also cooperate proactively with the Labour Department's investigations when necessary.

Ngon noted that the government has strengthened preventive measures in recent years, including promoting the use of innovative technology to enhance site risk identification and control. Key measures include the adoption of 'Smart Safety Construction Site' systems to detect unsafe behaviour and potential risks early. The Housing Authority requires contractors to feed safety data from such systems into its 'AI+ Construction Intelligence Platform' to improve monitoring of safety performance and raise frontline workers' safety awareness.

title: The Three Dates for Deciding Ukraine’s Future
zh_title: 决定乌克兰未来的三个日期
summary: 在接下来的八周内，随着乌克兰进入冬季，俄罗斯计划利用寒冷的天气作为武器。它的军工厂已经制造了足够的导弹和无人机来摧毁乌克兰的电网以及数百万人赖以取暖的供暖系统。随着气温下降，远离前线的房屋对于居民来说将变得致命。在同一时间范围内，发生在千里之外的三件事可能决定乌克兰的未来。第一个是美国选举日，距离现在还有两周；基辅领导人担心，如果民主党赢得一个或两个胜利，
content:
在接下来的八周内，随着乌克兰进入冬季，俄罗斯计划利用寒冷的天气作为武器。它的军工厂已经制造了足够的导弹和无人机来摧毁乌克兰的电网以及数百万人赖以取暖的供暖系统。随着气温下降，远离前线的房屋对于居民来说将变得致命。在同一时间范围内，发生在千里之外的三件事可能决定乌克兰的未来。第一个是美国选举日，距离现在还有两周；基辅领导人担心，如果民主党赢得国会一院或两院，特朗普总统可能会在共和党完全控制华盛顿的最后几周内进一步反对他们。第二个提议是 11 月中旬在中国南部举行的峰会，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京 (Vladimir Putin) 希望在峰会上与特朗普和中国国家主席习近平会面，商讨如何结束战争，但不会让乌克兰在谈判桌上占有一席之地。第三个是定于 12 月中旬在特朗普迈阿密地区高尔夫球场举行的 G20 峰会。据顾问称，总统的愿景是在普京和乌克兰总统泽连斯基签署和平协议时站在他们中间，即使他必须对乌克兰采取强硬手段才能做到这一点。
一位不愿透露姓名的乌克兰官员坦率地讨论了内部对话，他告诉我们，很难不感到自己被排除在决定国家未来的决策之外：“看起来这一切都是在我们没有参与的情况下发生的。”这位曾经吹嘘自己可以在24小时内解决战争的美国总统现在放弃了对俄罗斯的一些制裁，并与普京达成协议，从莫斯科进口柴油，从而为俄罗斯战争机器提供了动力。他和他的盟友威胁基辅，要求泽连斯基停止攻击俄罗斯炼油厂，否则就有失去获取美国用于自卫的情报、武器和卫星通信的风险。日历现在是乌克兰的敌人——乌克兰人担心唐纳德·特朗普也是如此。特朗普对伊朗的战争似乎扼杀了共和党在中期选举中的机会。无休止的冲突以及由此导致的石油和天然气价格飙升，削弱了共和党的民调支持率，并助长了民主党赢得国会参众两院的希望。由于结束战争的努力受阻，特朗普最近将注意力转向解决乌克兰冲突，部分原因是为了降低燃油价格。但他选择的尝试方式却给他的共和党同僚带来了十月份的令人不快的意外。特朗普在美国总统中首次站在传统对手俄罗斯一边，因为俄罗斯不仅为自身的生存而战，而且还充当了抵御更广泛战争的堡垒。
特朗普与普京的柴油协议对美国能源价格的影响微乎其微，但它是莫斯科的金融生命线。[阅读：乌克兰找到了一组新目标]特朗普要求能源停火——他甚至在本月早些时候宣布了一项没有现实依据的停火协议——但他的愤怒完全集中在乌克兰对俄罗斯炼油厂的袭击上。他将能源价格上涨归咎于这些袭击，却忽视了真正的罪魁祸首，即伊朗违抗美国并关闭霍尔木兹海峡的能力。三名与他关系密切的人士告诉我们，他确信乌克兰对炼油厂的袭击在一定程度上是为了削弱共和党下个月的机会，进而削弱特朗普的机会。主席

【原文 English Original】
O ver the next eight weeks , as winter envelops Ukraine, Russia plans to use the frigid weather as a weapon. Its arms factories have already made enough missiles and drones to take down Ukraine’s electrical grid, as well as the heating systems that millions of people rely on to stay warm. Homes far from the front will become deadly for their inhabitants as temperatures fall. In that same time frame, three events taking place thousands of miles away could determine Ukraine’s future. The first is America’s Election Day, now two weeks away; leaders in Kyiv fear that if Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress, President Trump may turn even further against them in those final weeks of full Republican control of Washington. The second is a proposed summit in mid-November in southern China, where Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to meet with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to plan how to end the war—without having a seat at the table for Ukraine. The third is the G20 summit at Trump’s Miami-area golf course, scheduled to take place in mid-December. The president has visions of standing between Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as they sign a peace deal, even if he has to strong-arm Ukraine to do it, according to advisers. One Ukrainian official, speaking on the condition of anonymity to candidly discuss internal conversations, told us that it’s hard not to feel left out of decision making that will dictate the country’s future: “It looks like this is all happening without us.” The U.S. president, who used to brag that he could resolve the war in 24 hours, has tossed aside some sanctions on Russia and struck a deal with Putin to import diesel from Moscow, giving a boost to the Russian war machine. He and his allies have threatened Kyiv, demanding that Zelensky stop attacking Russian oil refineries or risk losing access to American intelligence, weaponry, and satellite communications that it uses to defend itself. The calendar is now Ukraine’s foe—and so, Ukrainians fear, is Donald Trump. T rump’s war in Iran has appeared to throttle Republicans’ chances in the midterms; the unending conflict, and the resulting surge in oil and gas prices, has eroded the GOP’s poll numbers and fueled Democrats’ hopes of taking both chambers of Congress. Stymied in his efforts to bring that war to a close, Trump recently shifted his focus to resolving the Ukraine conflict, in part to bring fuel prices down. But the way he’s chosen to try to do that has provided his fellow Republicans with a nasty October surprise . In a first for a U.S. president, Trump has sided with a traditional adversary, Russia, over a democracy that is not only fighting for its existence but also acting as a bulwark against a wider war. Trump’s diesel deal with Putin will have a negligible impact on American energy prices, but it’s a financial lifeline for Moscow. [ Read: Ukraine finds a new set of targets ] Trump has demanded an energy cease-fire—he even announced one earlier this month that had no basis in reality—yet has focused his ire entirely on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. He blames those strikes for the rise in energy prices while ignoring the real culprit, Iran’s ability to defy the United States and close the Strait of Hormuz . He’s convinced himself, three people close to him have told us, that Ukraine’s attacks on the refineries are, in part, meant to undermine Republicans’ chances next month—and, by extension, Trump. The president has ignored Moscow’s attacks on Ukraine’s electrical grid, and yesterday, hours after a drone strike on a public park killed six people, including two children, he downplayed its strikes on Ukraine’s cities, declaring that Russia had not “been doing much.” An image of one of the dead children, a 1-year-old killed as she sat in her stroller, was broadcast around the globe. More pressure could be coming. Trump aides have threatened to withhold arms sales unless Kyiv stops targeting Russian diesel plants; this week, the administration delayed approving the transfer of missiles that Ukraine needs for its defense. Ukraine in the past week has said that it has not consistently received early warnings of attacks and no longer has full Starshield satellite access, which is impeding its ability to defend itself against Russia’s new fleet of jet-powered drones. ( The Wall Street Journal reported today that Starshield’s creator, Elon Musk, ordered the slowdown . The White House and Musk had previously denied involvement.) Some in Trump’s orbit have suggested that the United States go further and stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine. Trump’s deference to Putin has been a theme for a decade, yet this new round of kowtowing has handed Republicans another obstacle ahead of the elections. In a rare act of defiance, a handful in the party have denounced the president’s decisions, including his move to undercut a Russia-sanctions bill that he signed only a month ago in honor of its champion, the late Senator Lindsey Graham. The quick betrayal of Graham’s legacy was a blow for some of his Senate colleagues; GOP aides told us that Graham’s sudden July death cost Ukraine its most vocal champion in Trump’s inner circle, and that no one has stepped up to fill that void. Michael Froman, who worked in the Clinton and Obama administrations and is now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, told us that cutting off Kyiv from American weapons or intelligence might, in fact, prolong the war because it “would undermine Ukraine’s position at the negotiating table and make it less likely Russia would be willing to negotiate on any of the key outstanding issues.” Officials with both parties predict that the Democrats will capture the House next month; the Senate appears to be a true toss-up. Kyiv will be carefully watching the results. A Democratic win next month will, in the long run, likely help Kyiv, and some of the more hopeful members of Zelensky’s camp believe that Republican defeats could force Trump to focus more on domestic issues, resulting in him leaving Ukraine alone. But other observers on both sides of the Atlantic fear that the opposite could be true. A president without a friendly Congress tends to fall back more on foreign policy, where he needs little help from Capitol Hill. Either way, the new Congress won’t be seated until January 3, leaving Trump unchecked for two more months and perhaps motivated to wield power before his party moves into the minority. Another major national election would not be for two years—plenty of time for Trump to push Ukraine without fear of voters punishing Republicans. “He could get distracted at any time,” one outside Trump ally told us. “But right now, he’s furious at Ukraine, and he wants Zelensky gone.” T wo weeks after Election Day , Trump plans to board Air Force One bound for a series of summits in Asia. Earlier this month, Trump overruled White House aides who had counseled against him calling to wish Putin a happy birthday, warning that little good would come of it. In that conversation, Trump authorized the diesel deal, and Putin suggested something grander: a meeting of the world’s great powers to divide up the world. Or at least Ukraine. Putin proposed that he, Trump, and Xi hold a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation in Shenzhen, China, in mid-November to discuss a variety of issues, including Ukraine. Trump told reporters yesterday that he is open to attending the meeting, which would be his first face-to-face encounter with Putin since their unproductive summit in Alaska last year. It is no surprise that Trump is drawn to the idea; his deference toward Putin is rivaled only by his regard for Xi, whom he hosted in lavish fashion at the White House last month. He has previously been intrigued by the idea of the three powers—China, Russia, the United States—dividing the globe into spheres of influence, although Moscow these days hardly wields the international clout of Washington or Beijing. [ Read: The deferential president ] The idea of two authoritarians and their admirer plotting to slice up sovereign nations alarmed much of the West. And how, Kyiv demanded, could Ukraine’s future be decided with no input from Ukraine? But some in Trump’s orbit have backed the idea, belittling Ukraine as a corrupt backwater with no autonomy. Putin has never viewed Ukraine as a legitimate country, and Trump has held a grudge against it since 2019, when he was impeached (for the first time) after pressuring Zelensky to dig up damaging information about Trump’s political rival Joe Biden. He and his Ukrainian counterpart had a shouting match at the White House early in Trump’s second term, causing the U.S. to briefly withhold intelligence. Since then, Zelensky has tried to flatter Trump to stay on his good side, but those niceties have vanished as the American president has demanded that Ukraine pick a new leader. Many of those in Trump’s orbit are unsympathetic to Ukraine’s plight and see the war not as a battle for the modern, rules-based world order—with its cardinal tenet prohibiting the seizure of land by force—but as an impediment to future business deals with Russia, some of which could enrich members of the president’s inner circle. Pushing Ukraine into taking a deal, even if that means it has to give up its claim on the Donbas, would open up avenues to dealmaking on Russia’s diesel, rare-earth minerals, and other resources. Zelensky has balked at any territorial concessions. “Our worry is that they are looking at this as a new Yalta Conference, to divide the world into spheres of influence,” another Ukrainian official told us. Trump’s ideal timeline for some sort of Russia-Ukraine peace agreement, as we reported last week, would be in December at the G20 summit. That bit of history, were it to occur, would take place at one of Trump’s own properties. In Trump’s first term, he pushed to host the 2020 G7 at his golf course in Doral, just outside of Miami. But Trump abandoned the idea amid bipartisan blowback over his plan to personally profit off the event. This time, there has been nary a Republican whimper of protest about Trump’s venue choice, but some have lodged complaints about the president’s other idea for the summit: to invite Putin. The Russian leader has yet to agree to show up, but if he does, it would be the first time he has attended a multilateral summit in a Western country since his invasion of Ukraine. It would allow him to take another step in shedding his status as an international pariah, though it is hard to imagine that European leaders are eager to talk with Putin. Zelensky, who has already committed to attending the G20, has made clear that he would be willing to sit down with Putin, no matter the venue, to work out an agreement to end the war. If Trump has his way over the next eight weeks, it might be not a negotiation, but a capitulation.

title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 20, 2026_Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Kenya
summary: ### Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 20, 2026 2026-10-20 17:03 * * * **Xinhua News Agency: Foreign Minister Wang Yi just concluded his visit to the four countries in Eurasia. Could you share more
content:
### Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 20, 2026

2026-10-20 17:03

* * *

**Xinhua News Agency: Foreign Minister Wang Yi just concluded his visit to the four countries in Eurasia. Could you share more information on the visit? With the trade friction between China and Europe under the spotlight, what message does China intend to convey to the European side through this visit?**

Mao Ning: From October 14 to 20, Foreign Minister Wang Yi attended the seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping, and visited Azerbaijan, Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria.

The most important message conveyed through this visit is as follows: Trust is the cornerstone of peace; friendship is an invaluable asset; cooperation is a powerful driving force; and partnership is our shared pursuit. Foreign Minister Wang Yi also noted that China’s foreign policy is featured by partnership and dialogue rather than alliance and confrontation. Underpinned by partnership, state-to-state relations, regional cooperation and China-EU relations can proceed in parallel and are fully compatible. The overall China-EU relationship is sound and stable. The disagreements on trade issues in the course of our growing cooperation can be resolved through dialogue, and should not affect our overall relations. China and Europe share extensive common interests, as we both champion multilateralism, stay committed to the UN’s centrality, and remain ready to pursue political settlements of international and regional disputes through dialogue. The two sides should respect and appreciate each other, help each other succeed, and jointly shoulder the international responsibility on world peace and development.

**RT: This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers’ and Peasants’ Red Army. Russian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Maria Zakharova recently compared China’s efforts towards building a community with a shared future for humanity and advancing Belt and Road cooperation to a new Long March as she spoke highly of China’s development achievements. Would you like to comment on this? How does the Long March spirit inspire China’s diplomacy in the new era?**

Mao Ning: We noted the positive comments of Ms. Zakharova. The great Long March spirit has always inspired the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and make remarkable development achievements. On the new Long March towards the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, China will uphold the independent foreign policy of peace, and work with Russia and other countries in solidarity to promote peace and development and jointly build a community with a shared future for humanity.

**Phoenix TV: We noted that today marks a full year since the establishment of the International Organization for Mediation (IOMed). Does the spokesperson have any comment?**

Mao Ning: Over the past year since its establishment, the IOMed has received broad support and positive response from the international community. The number of founding member states has risen to 48. It has successfully mediated international commercial dispute cases and received high recognition from the disputing parties.

The IOMed is committed to providing a new platform for all parties to settle disputes in a peaceful and friendly way. It is an important public good for the rule of law presented to the international community. It is hoped that more countries would join the IOMed and make good use of it, together making new contributions to the peaceful resolution of international disputes and to promoting world peace and development.

**AFP: The U.S. government has instructed its agencies to stop using AI tools from the Chinese firm DeepSeek, which it said could present multiple threats, including the possible transfer of sensitive data to China. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this?**

Mao Ning: China consistently opposes overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing tech and trade issues. We will resolutely safeguard Chinese businesses’ lawful rights and interests.

**Kyodo News: It is reported that U.S. President Donald Trump said that he is open to a trilateral meeting with Chinese and Russian presidents. I wonder if China will accept the offer.**

Mao Ning: I have no information to share at the moment.

律政司司长林定国周一启程前往文莱出席第十六届中国-东盟检察长会议，会上将探讨如何保障数码时代的儿童。他将讨论跨境合作打击针对青少年的网络犯罪，并介绍香港的经验

文莱政府宣布，律政司司长林定国周一下午启程前往文莱，出席第十六届中国-东盟检察长会议及相关区域会议。

林郑月娥作为中国官方代表团的一员出席此次高级别会议，并计划在一场致力于保护数字时代儿童的全体会议上发表讲话。他与东南亚国家联盟成员国代表的讨论将集中于加强国际合作，应对针对青少年的网络犯罪威胁。
此次访问之际，人们越来越担心影响全球年轻人的数字威胁。技术的快速进步为年轻人创造了广泛的发展机会，但同时也带来了前所未有的安全风险，特别是未经同意的亲密图像传播和深度换脸技术的滥用。由于针对儿童的非法在线活动很容易跨越国界，区域执法和司法机构认为跨境伙伴关系至关重要。

在会议期间，林郑月娥将介绍香港现有的旨在保护儿童免受网络伤害的法律架构，同时概述该市未来旨在应对新兴数字危险的政策措施和监管举措。除全体会议外，林郑月娥还将与中国代表团成员和东盟官员一起参加双边讨论，以扩大相互交流并促进跨司法管辖区更紧密的工作关系。

陪同林郑月娥正式出访的有刑事检控专员周天行及数名政府律师。律政司司长预计于10月23日结束任期返港。在他缺席期间，律政司副秘书长张国钧代理律政司司长。

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam Ting-kwok departed for Brunei on Monday to attend the 16th China-ASEAN Prosecutors-General Conference, where he will address safeguarding children in the digital era. He will discuss cross-border cooperation against cybercrime targeting youth and present Hong Kong's le

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 16:53 HKT · 2 min read

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam Ting-kwok departed for Brunei on Monday afternoon to participate in the 16th China-ASEAN Prosecutors-General Conference and related regional meetings, the government announced.

Lam is attending the high-level gathering as part of the official Chinese delegation, where he is scheduled to address a plenary session dedicated to safeguarding children in the digital era. His discussions with representatives from member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations will centre on strengthening international collaboration to counter cybercrime threats directed at youth.

The visit comes amid growing concern over digital threats affecting young people globally. While rapid technological progress has created extensive developmental opportunities for youth, it has simultaneously introduced unprecedented safety risks, notably the non-consensual distribution of intimate images and the misuse of deepfake technology. Because illicit online activities targeting children easily cross national borders, regional law enforcement and judicial bodies view cross-border partnerships as critical.

During the conference, Lam will present Hong Kong's existing legal architecture designed to shield children from online harms, while outlining the city's future policy measures and regulatory initiatives aimed at tackling emerging digital dangers. In addition to the plenary sessions, Lam will join bilateral discussions alongside members of the Chinese delegation and ASEAN officials to broaden mutual exchanges and foster closer working relationships across legal jurisdictions.

Lam is accompanied on the official trip by Director of Public Prosecutions Anthony Chau Tin-hang and several government counsel. The justice secretary is scheduled to wrap up his engagements and return to Hong Kong on October 23. During his absence, Deputy Secretary for Justice Horace Cheung Kwok-kwan is assuming the role of acting secretary for justice.

source: 新闻汇总 - 茉莉花新闻网

content: 茉莉花评论 文 / 孔灵犀 西班牙人上街要求降租金、停止驱逐。限租能压低房租，可它多不出一套房，而西班牙缺的正是房子。纽约强制搬人要经法院，文中所引的中国两条规则讲提前通知：护着租客，和找得到房，是两回事。 10月3日，西班牙马德里、瓦伦西亚等城市举行了约50场住房游行，西班牙政府说，光是马德里就有约7万人上街。前一天，议会以178票对172票、184票对166票，否决了政府为平息抗议提出的两项法令，里面有把2028年前到期的租约延长两年。抗议者要求降租金、停止驱逐。可是，限租、延长租约这些办法，到底帮得了谁？ 我的看法是：限租能压低租金，短期内对已经住进去的人尤其有用，一些地方的新租约也设了上限；可限租多不出一套房，还在找房的年轻人租不租得到房，还要看新房建得够不够。纽约和中国正好可以对照：纽约有争议、没和解的驱逐案要由法官裁决，房东胜诉后签发驱逐令，中国下文的两条规则写的是提前通知；可在纽约，法律护着租客，租房照样难。 西班牙央行在2025年年报里算过：2021年到2025年，西班牙新建成的住房比新增的家庭少了约75万套。光是2025年，新增家庭就有24万户，新建成的住房只有9.2万套，缺口还在扩大。房子不够，租金就往上走：房产网站Idealista的统计显示，今年9月底，在西班牙租房每平方米要15.1欧元，比一年前贵5.6%。 央行把限租的好处和代价都说了：限租在短期内特别能减轻已签租约的租户的负担；可要是长期实行，房东的实际收入下降，投资出租房的劲头跟着下降，新出租的房子会比不限租时少。 纽约：强制搬人要经法院，空房却极少 纽约的法律尊重租客的权利：按规矩，把租客赶出门的只能是执行官或者警长，别人动手赶人，就是非法驱逐。纽约州的“正当理由驱逐”法（Good Cause Eviction）2024年4月20日生效，受这部法律保护的房子，房东没有正当理由不能结束租约，这部法律靠法院执行。美国宪法第十四修正案写着，各州不经正当法律程序，不得剥夺任何人的生命、自由或财产。在我看来，纽约这套先审后搬的程序，就是这条原则落在租房上的样子：租客的话要听，房东的诉求也要先由法官裁决。 一个驱逐案是这样走的：房东先向法院递交诉状，写明起诉的理由；案子先分到调解庭，法官要房东和租客谈着解决。租客的答辩，是向法院陈述抗辩理由和反诉；开庭日期可能改期；双方还可以提动议，请求法院采取某项行动。进入开庭审理的，双方当庭举证，由法官作出决定；房东胜诉的，法院判决房东有权让租客搬走，法官再签发驱逐令。房东雇执行官执行驱逐令的，执行官由市长任命；动手之前，接到驱逐令的官员还要至少提前14天书面通知租客。美国广播公司纽约台（ABC7）2024年11月的调查发现，纽约市的驱逐案平均要两年；房东们说，驱逐令至少要六个月才能执行。前者算整个案子，后者只是最后一步。案子拖成几年，部分原因是疫情以来法院积案多、资源有限，不全是程序要花的时间。ABC7报道的一位布朗克斯区房东，当了几十年护士，在法院打赢了官司，又等了一年多才等到法官签发驱逐令，到报道时还在等执行官去执行。这套程序两边都护着：租客不会被人直接赶出门，房东的权利也要经法官裁定、由官员落实；代价是慢，房东要等。 可在纽约找房一样难。纽约市住房保护与发展局2024年3月6日在市议会作证时说，2023年全市出租房的净空置率只有1.41%，供给跟不上需求。 中国：这两条规则靠提前通知保护租客 《民法典》第七百三十条规定，租期没有约定或者约定不明确，依据第五百一十条的规定仍不能确定的，视为不定期租赁，双方都可以随时解除合同，只要在合理期限之前通知对方。也就是说，依法算作不定期租赁的，房东在合理期限之前通知租客，就能解除合同，这一条没有要求房东说明理由，也没有要求房东先到法院起诉。2025年9月15日起施行的《住房租赁条例》加了一层保护：房东依法解除合同，要通知租客，给租客留出搬走的合理时间，不得用暴力、威胁或者其他非法方式逼租客解约、搬走。这两条保护租客的办法是提前通知和留出搬家时间，条文里没有先走法庭程序这一环，纽约那样要经法院裁决的程序，在这两条规则里找不到对应的东西。 三地比起来，西班牙和纽约相同的是缺房：西班牙新建成的住房赶不上新增的家庭，纽约空房极少。不同的是法律怎么护着租客：纽约靠法院走完程序，中国的这两条规则靠提前通知，西班牙连延长租约的法令都没通过。落到租房的人身上：在纽约，住进去的租客住得稳，想新租一套房的人却很难找到；在中国，依法算作不定期租赁的租客，房东在合理期限之前通知就能解除合同。 支持限租的人也有证据。西班牙央行说，加泰罗尼亚等地被定为住房紧张区的城镇，新租约的租金设了上限；央行引用的一项2023年的研究发现，加泰罗尼亚2020年到2021年的限租让租金下降了4%到6%，短期内没有减少出租房。我同意，限租能把租金压下来；可压低租金和多出房子是两回事，2025年西班牙新建成的住房，仍然赶不上新增的家庭。还在找房的年轻人要的，不只是一份便宜些的租约，而是先签得到一份租约。 所以我的答案是：限租帮得上已经住进去的人，可它补不上缺的房子；还在找房的年轻人租不租得到房，很大程度上要看新房建得够不够。对美国来说，要紧的是守住这套两边都护着的程序，同时多盖房，让空房多起来。 纽约的驱逐案，2024年的调查显示平均要两年；2023年全市出租房的净空置率，只有1.41%。法院的程序保得住已经住进去的人，保不住还在找房的人。 文中事实来自：BBC中文、路透社、西班牙央行2025年年报、Idealista、纽约市住房保护与发展局、美国广播公司纽约台、澎湃新闻政务号、司法部、美国国家档案馆、纽约州参议院、纽约房屋法庭解答中心

据台湾媒体报道，10 月 19 日，一名 38 岁台湾女子在山梨县富士河口湖一家酒店被发现死亡，经确认为台湾空降勤队队长的女儿，而现场被捕的 27 岁台湾女子则与诈骗团伙有关。

死者名叫Ching Yun-jung，当时正在跟团去日本旅行。 10月19日上午8点左右，她未能出现在集合地点，酒店工作人员前往检查她的房间，发现她躺在床上，没有生命体征。司法尸检证实，她因颈部左侧刺伤深至颈动脉而失血过多而死亡。
当时，27岁的犯罪嫌疑人杨敏汉在房间里被发现。警方检获一把刀身长约12厘米、血迹斑斑的菜刀，并以涉嫌违反枪支和剑持有管制法的罪名将她逮捕。 10 月 21 日，她被移送检察官。警方尚未确认她是否会面临谋杀指控，并正在调查两名妇女之间的关系以及死亡情况。

台湾媒体报道称，死者的父亲是国家空降勤兵团团长景彦元。他原定于10月22日出席立法院会议，但因处理女儿事务而请假飞往日本。

嫌疑人的背景也引起了人们的关注。据镜报媒体援引法庭记录，一名同名女子因向诈骗团伙提供两张银行账户卡及密码，导致六名受害者将资金转入账户，于2025年8月被高雄地方法院以洗钱罪判处有期徒刑三个月及新台币一万元罚金。一些台湾媒体用“疑似”一词将前案与被捕女子联系起来，但身份匹配尚未完全确认。
此案引发质疑，因为报道最初称两名女子分别报名参加巡演且互不相识，但后来网友发现她们的社交媒体账户互相关注，而死者还发布了为他人支付超过新台币一万元的帖子。据报道，嫌疑人承认在旅途中购买了这把刀，但没有承认杀死了这名女子。

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

23 Oct 2026 at 05:56 HKT · 2 min read

A 38-year-old Taiwanese woman found dead at a hotel in Fujikawaguchiko, Yamanashi Prefecture, on 19 October has been identified as the daughter of Taiwan's National Airborne Service Corps chief, while the 27-year-old Taiwanese woman arrested at the scene has been linked to a fraud group, according to Taiwanese media.

The deceased, identified as Ching Yun-jung, was on a tour group trip to Japan. When she failed to show up at the meeting point around 8am on 19 October, hotel staff went to check her room and found her lying on the bed with no vital signs. A judicial autopsy confirmed she died from excessive blood loss after a deep stab wound to the left side of her neck that reached the carotid artery.

The 27-year-old suspect, Yang Min-han, was found in the room at the time. Police seized a bloodstained kitchen knife with a blade about 12cm long and arrested her on suspicion of violating the Firearm and Sword Possession Control Law. She was transferred to prosecutors on 21 October. Police have not yet confirmed whether she will face murder charges and are investigating the relationship between the two women and the circumstances of the death.

Taiwanese media reported that the deceased's father is Ching Yen-yuan, head of the National Airborne Service Corps. He had been scheduled to attend a Legislative Yuan session on 22 October but took leave to fly to Japan to handle his daughter's affairs.

The suspect's background has also drawn attention. According to court records cited by Mirror Media, a woman with the same name was sentenced by the Kaohsiung District Court in August 2025 to three months' imprisonment and a NT$10,000 fine for money laundering after providing two bank account cards and passwords to a fraud group, leading to six victims transferring money into the accounts. Some Taiwanese media have used the word 'suspected' in linking the previous case to the arrested woman, and the identity match has not been fully confirmed.

The case has raised questions because reports initially said the two women had separately signed up for the tour and did not know each other, but netizens later found their social media accounts were following each other, and the deceased had posted about covering more than NT$10,000 for someone else. The suspect reportedly admitted buying the knife during the trip but has not admitted to killing the woman.

# Censorship in Pakistan Goes From ‘Pleasant’ to ‘Unpleasant’

Authorities have directed satellite TV channels to refrain from broadcasting or providing live coverage of “unpleasant incidents,” meaning shootings, blasts and terrorist attacks.

By **Asif Ullah Khan**

October 22, 2026

[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fcensorship-in-pakistan-goes-from-pleasant-to-unpleasant%2F&title=Censorship+in+Pakistan+Goes+From+%E2%80%98Pleasant%E2%80%99+to+%E2%80%98Unpleasant%E2%80%99 "Share on LinkedIn")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fcensorship-in-pakistan-goes-from-pleasant-to-unpleasant%2F "Share on Facebook")[](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Censorship+in+Pakistan+Goes+From+%E2%80%98Pleasant%E2%80%99+to+%E2%80%98Unpleasant%E2%80%99%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fcensorship-in-pakistan-goes-from-pleasant-to-unpleasant%2F "Share on Bluesky")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Censorship+in+Pakistan+Goes+From+%E2%80%98Pleasant%E2%80%99+to+%E2%80%98Unpleasant%E2%80%99&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fcensorship-in-pakistan-goes-from-pleasant-to-unpleasant%2F "Share on X")

Credit: [Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Pakistan](https://tse3.mm.bing.net/th/id/OIP.8-BkEqrkngQulDAi9IVk1QHaE7?r=0&rs=1&pid=ImgDetMain&o=7&rm=3)

Ad

The famous Pakistani satirist and playwright, Anwar Maqsood, once said at the Karachi Literature Festival: “The biggest lie in Pakistan is PTV’s weather report. Outside it is scorching hot, but the news announces: ‘The weather across the country is pleasant.'”

The man, a master of puns and wordplay, used the weather analogy to highlight the censorship imposed on the state broadcaster to keep people away from the harsh realities of the country. He used “scorching hot” as a metaphor for unemployment, inflation, poverty and social unrest.

Now, things have gone from “pleasant” to “unpleasant.”

The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) on October 13 directed satellite television channels to refrain from broadcasting or providing live coverage of “[unpleasant incidents](https://cpj.org/2026/10/pakistan-media-regulator-orders-new-restrictions-on-tv-coverage-of-attacks-and-other-unpleasant-incidents/),” meaning explosions, blasts, firing and terrorist attacks.

“All satellite TV channel licensees are once again hereby directed to refrain from broadcast, re-broadcast and live coverage of any unfortunate/unpleasant incident such as explosion, blast, firing, terrorist attack etc,” the notification said, adding, “Satellite TV channels must broadcast only such verified information, warranted by the concerned department/law enforcement agency.”

The notification also directed channels to “effectively use time delay mechanism” and ensure the constitution of an independent editorial board in accordance with PEMRA laws, a Supreme Court judgment in suo motu case No. 28 of 2018, and an Islamabad High Court order issued on September 5, 2022.

Before the PEMRA notification, Pakistani satellite TV channels had refrained from broadcasting the “[most unpleasant](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2023/jun/21/imran-khan-pakistan-tv-prime-minister-army)” – the name of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan and his image. Following the May 9, 2023, protests triggered by Khan’s arrest, PEMRA asked television licensees to ensure that “hate mongers, rioters, their facilitators and perpetrators” were “completely screened out from media.” Although it did not name Khan, television channels got the message.

Now, TV anchors have devised a new nomenclature while referring to news regarding Khan’s court proceedings. The preferred terms are “chairman Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)” or “PTI chief.” One TV anchor satirically uses “Kasim ke Abba” (father of Kasim), which is the name of Khan’s elder son.

Recently, Pakistani journalist and author Mohammed Hanif, in his satirical blog on [BBC Urdu](https://www.facebook.com/mohammed.hanif.3720190), said people of his age had seen posters saying, “Please avoid political discussions in Pakistani restaurants.” Hanif says that, though he has not seen any restaurant owner pushing guests out for indulging in political discussion, this rule will now be implemented by Pakistan’s cyber authorities.

Any comment or discussion can be construed as anti-national or as disturbing public peace because the cyber authorities have not specified what constitutes such content. So, even a harmless post can invite the government’s wrath if a comment below it is seen as an attack on a government department. In the end, Hanif suggests that the safest way to avoid the midnight knock on your door is to discuss cooking recipes.

content: 作者：呉祚來   央廣 Rti 2026-10-23 圖片來源：其他 後習時代，會不會重蹈大清覆轍？(AI圖∕程寬厚) 我們無法預測，中共政權什麼時間被終結，但透過對大清最後十年的比照，還是能看到專權帝國難以擺脫的政治困境。後習時代，是指習近平生命結束後，也可以是指習不再是中共最高領導人的時代。 一、大清為朝代終結製造了必要條件 大清被終結，史書上都歸功於「辛亥革命」，其實，終結大清的，是大清朝廷，多重因素可以說一個都不能少，大清退出歷史舞臺，是朝廷自己拆臺的結果。 最重要的因素，一是大清君主立憲不真誠，並沒有像英國確立的君憲制那樣，透過虛君政治，確立議會主權，導致立憲派與地方實力人物在歷史時刻選擇了地方獨立；其次是經濟與財政方面：1910年，上海橡膠股票泡沫破裂，引發錢莊倒閉，使川漢鐵路部分籌款遭受損失。1911年清廷推行鐵路幹線國有政策，地方路權、股款補償與外債安排交織，牽動四川廣大紳商農民的切身利益，激起保路運動。成都血案繼而激起大規模武裝反抗。清廷調湖北部分新軍入川，削弱了武漢駐軍力量，為革命黨人創造了有利時機。 武昌起義最初是一次新軍兵變，如果侷限於武漢一地，仍有可能被優勢清軍鎮壓。但革命黨人、新軍軍官與立憲派等共同參與組建湖北軍政府，並通電全國，各省相繼宣布獨立，朝廷已難以僅靠軍事鎮壓恢復統治。此時朝廷重新啟用被下野的袁世凱，結局是在各省獨立、南北和談、袁世凱施壓，以及段祺瑞等北洋將領共和兵諫電報的共同作用下，迫使大清遜位。不僅大清被終結，兩千多年的君主帝制，也被終結。 回過頭來看，從清末新政到王朝覆亡，不過十年；從正式宣布預備立憲算起，更只有五年左右。政治改革遲遲未能建立信用，經濟危機與地方維權總爆發，軍隊兵變，地方與中央切割，中央政權隨之崩解。 有人會說，搞君主立憲，與國際接軌的市場經濟，導致大清潰敗，還不如不搞這些新東西，封閉的大清更安全，只要權力在手，朝廷就不會出現嚴重的安全隱患。看看明朝就知道了，明朝沒有搞君憲，雖然晚明已透過白銀與商品貿易參與世界經濟，結果呢，災荒、戰爭、財政困境與官府腐敗相互交織，最終導致大規模動亂。不搞政治改革，並不能避免帝制朝廷的統治危機。 相比之下，大清朝廷因為有經濟市場化、有地方諮議局及立憲派在歷史時刻參與政治協商，使革命初期的「驅逐韃虜、恢復中華」逐漸轉向五族共和。高舉鐵血十八星旗的革命軍，部分帶有強烈的排滿與民族復仇色彩，一些地方已經發生針對滿人的屠殺。而透過南北和談，透過共和共識，最終以談判完成清帝退位，減少了繼續大規模戰爭的風險。從這個意義上說，大清得到了最不壞的結果。 二、習近平面臨大清難題 大清是滿洲統治集團透過征服進入中原、承接中華帝制的王朝，在君主專制這一統治形態上，與明朝沒有本質區別。大明主要是被農民起義摧垮的，然後才是清軍入關問鼎成功。大清搞政治改革，一個重要參照是日本。日本明治維新後國力強大，日俄戰爭劃時代的勝利，使大清朝廷震撼，進一步推動了清廷仿照日本搞君憲體制。 鄧小平是透過利用資本主義來拯救社會主義危機，但三四十年之後，經濟與社會變化也不斷給中共體制帶來新的挑戰，習近平則選擇進一步強化集權與黨治，強調國有經濟的地位與軍委主席負責制。不禁使人想起慈禧謝幕之後，載灃收攏權力，強化皇族對軍政的控制，袁世凱被下野就是例證；習近平則對中共軍方高級將領進行持續整肅。 習近平承續鄧、江、胡時代的「不搞西方那一套」政治原則。在這一政治邏輯中，像大清搞預備立憲，有了更活躍的公共輿論與省級諮議局，反而可能使統治者被置於更危險的境地。 但大清要「進步」，要發展市場經濟，不得不官商合作，不得不發展鐵路，為了統治安全，也不得不建立新軍。這些新因素增強了國家能力，也產生了新的社會力量與政治訴求，朝廷如果只要前者，卻拒絕容納後者，統治矛盾便不斷積累。 習近平面臨同樣的悖論，要與世界同步獲得豐富的資訊，卻又害怕網際網路自由危害黨國安全，要讓更多的企業家走向世界，卻又擔心他們轉移資產與移民海外，要利用民營經濟提高國內就業，卻對他們永遠不放心，害怕民營做大了就有政治訴求。 所以，習時代選擇了逆政治改革、逆世界潮流而動，黨國可以控制的領域，做強做大，傾國家之力來發展，而更多的屬於市場的領域，透過嚴厲的管控，使其生存與發展受到限制。 大清困境是進退維谷，如果能及時走向英式立憲，透過限制皇權完成自我改革，或許能夠降低被革命推翻的風險。習近平親自提出了自我革命，並不是革共產黨專制的命，而是在國內黨內清除政治異己，壓制反對的聲音，還是用毛澤東的手段，將黨國權力集於一身，黨天下變成習天下。 個人集權越徹底，糾錯與權力繼承的風險就越可能積累；主動改革越能落實為可信的制度，和平轉型的機會才可能越大。習近平與大清面臨相似的困境，真正觸及權力結構的「自我革命」，才可能成為化解這一困境的出路。 在習尚有威權的時間窗口，可以自上而下地開啟政治轉型，逐步建立全國議員直選、軍隊國家化、司法獨立的制度與過渡安排，像當年鄧小平搞改革開放一樣，結束文革之後，開啟新的歷史方向； 也可以用漸進的方式，實現政治轉型，例如：在海南搞政治實驗區，真正的民選議員與市長，海南網路與媒體開放，司法獨立；也可以分階段推進全國市縣一級的政治改革，還權於民。畢竟習近平稱自己是延安的兒子，那麼，兌現父母輩當年的延安承諾，是千載難逢的歷史機遇。 結語 大清留給後人的警示，不只是改革太遲，更是統治者始終不肯承認：國家的前途不能永遠服從一家一姓的權力安全，最後失去難得的歷史窗口期。 後習時代會不會重蹈覆轍，主動權在習近平手上。個人集權越深入，其他權威與組織的自主性越弱，繼任者面對的就越可能是一個權力高度集中、政治信任卻十分脆弱的局面。 後習時代到來時，中共面臨的是慈禧謝幕後的困境，還是毛澤東去世之後的變局？不同的結果，都可能引發程度不一的震盪，如果出現類似袁世凱去世後中央權威瓦解的局面，後果可能更悲劇，甚至出現軍閥割據、國家分裂的風險。 作者》 吳祚來   獨立學者，專欄作家。

title: Four KJ-3000 Radar Jets At Chinese Factory Point To Serial Production
zh_title: 中国工厂的四架 KJ-3000 雷达喷气机即将批量生产
