title: China's tech self-sufficiency could raise conflict risk: U.S. Expert - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 美国专家：中国科技自给自足可能引发冲突风险 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月20日电 一名美国科技专家周二警告说，中国在技术上更加自给自足的努力可能会降低北京面对国际制裁和供应链中断的脆弱性，从而增加台海发生军事冲突的风险。加州大学全球冲突与合作研究所高级研究员吉米·古德里奇（Jimmy Goodrich）在台北举行的一次会议间隙向中央社表示，中国对全球食品、能源和技术供应链的依赖仍然是“让北京犹豫不决”采取冒险军事行动的一个因素。
content:
中新社台北10月20日电 一名美国科技专家周二警告说，中国在技术上更加自给自足的努力可能会降低北京面对国际制裁和供应链中断的脆弱性，从而增加台海发生军事冲突的风险。

加州大学全球冲突与合作研究所高级研究员吉米·古德里奇(Jimmy Goodrich)在台北举行的一次会议间隙向中央社表示，中国对全球食品、能源和技术供应链的依赖仍然是“让北京犹豫”是否在台海采取冒险军事行动的一个因素。

然而，中国从俄罗斯入侵乌克兰的事件中吸取了西方国家如何利用经济制裁的教训，并正在寻求建立古德里奇所说的能够承受外部压力的“堡垒经济”。

他说：“随着中国变得更加自给自足，我确实相信这确实会增加冲突的风险，因为一个更加自给自足的中国将是一个更加自信和更具侵略性的中国。”

古德里奇强调，他不认为北京想要爆发战争，但表示，如果中国领导人认为某些红线已被跨越或面临国内政治压力，他们可能会感到被迫采取行动。
他指出，中国国家主席习近平年事已高、经济长期放缓以及潜在的国内政治危机等因素可能会改变北京的计算，但他也承认这种情况仍然是推测性的。

## 中国不断增长的技术能力

古德里奇在其职业生涯早期曾在中国科技领域工作了七年，他在台湾政府资助的国防安全研究院组织的一次会议上介绍了他对中国不断扩大基础科学投资的研究后发表了上述言论。

他在演讲中警告说，北京对科学基础设施的大规模投资最终可能会支持半导体、人工智能和先进武器系统的突破，从而可能削弱台湾的技术优势。

他说：“台湾和美国现在应该为中国在 2030 年代的技术竞争力可能远超今天做好准备。”

古德里奇表示，中国日益增长的科学能力也可能对台湾所谓的“硅盾”产生长期影响，即台湾在先进半导体制造领域的主导地位有助于阻止中国对台湾采取军事行动。

美国半导体工业协会（SIA）负责全球政策的前副会长古德里奇被中央通讯社要求详细阐述他的预测，他指出中国在存储芯片方面的快速进步。
他说：“五年前，中国还没有内存产业。”他补充说，中国现在在生产 3D NAND 闪存和 DRAM 方面“可以说比台湾本土的内存产业更先进”。

古德里奇表示，中国在成熟节点芯片生产（使用较旧的成熟技术制造半导体）方面也具有高度竞争力，但由于缺乏极紫外（EUV）光刻机，中国在先进制造方面继续面临挑战。

用于制造最先进芯片的EUV光刻机由荷兰设备制造商ASML独家生产，但根据荷兰出口限制，ASML禁止将其出口到中国。

尽管如此，古德里克

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 20 (CNA) China's efforts to become more technologically self-sufficient could increase the risk of a military conflict across the Taiwan Strait by reducing Beijing's vulnerability to international sanctions and supply chain disruptions, a U.S. technology expert warned Tuesday.

Jimmy Goodrich, a senior fellow at the University of California Institute on Global Conflict and Cooperation, told CNA on the sidelines of a conference in Taipei that China's reliance on global supply chains for food, energy and technology remains one factor that "makes Beijing hesitate" to take risky military action across the Taiwan Strait.

However, China has drawn lessons from Russia's invasion of Ukraine as to how Western countries use economic sanctions and is seeking to build what Goodrich described as a "fortress economy" capable of withstanding external pressure.

"As China becomes more self-sufficient, I do believe it does increase the risk around conflict because a more self-sufficient China will be a more confident and a more aggressive China," he said.

Goodrich stressed that he did not believe Beijing wanted a war, but said Chinese leaders could feel compelled to act if they perceived certain red lines had been crossed or faced domestic political pressure.

He cited Chinese President Xi Jinping's (習近平) advancing age, a prolonged economic slowdown and a potential domestic political crisis as factors that could alter Beijing's calculations, while acknowledging that such scenarios remained speculative.

## China's growing technological capabilities

Goodrich, who spent seven years working in China's technology sector earlier in his career, made the remarks after presenting his research on China's expanding investment in fundamental science at a conference organized by the Taiwanese government-funded Institute for National Defense and Security Research.

During his presentation, he warned that Beijing's massive investments in scientific infrastructure could eventually support breakthroughs in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and advanced weapons systems, potentially eroding Taiwan's technological advantages.

"Taiwan and the United States should be preparing now for a China that could be far more technologically competitive in the 2030s than it is today," he said.

Goodrich said China's growing scientific capabilities could also have long-term implications for Taiwan's so-called "silicon shield" -- the idea that its dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing helps deter Chinese military action against the island.

Asked by CNA to elaborate on his forecast, Goodrich, a former vice president for global policy at the U.S.-based Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA), pointed to China's rapid progress in memory chips.

"China five years ago had no memory industry," he said, adding that the country is now "arguably more advanced than Taiwan's own domestic memory industry" in producing 3D NAND flash memory and DRAM.

Goodrich said China had also become highly competitive in mature-node chip production -- the manufacturing of semiconductors using older, established technologies -- but continued to face challenges in advanced manufacturing because it lacked extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines.

EUV lithography machines, used to manufacture the most advanced chips, are produced exclusively by Dutch equipment maker ASML, which is prohibited from exporting them to China under Dutch export restrictions.

Nevertheless, Goodrich said China would face significant challenges catching up with Taiwan in leading-edge chipmaking, as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) could adopt similar innovations to those developed by Chinese competitors while applying them to more advanced transistor technologies.

He said Taiwan also benefited from a global research and development ecosystem that China lacks, giving it a significant competitive advantage.

## Maintaining Taiwan's technological edge

To maintain its technological edge, Goodrich urged Taiwan to invest more in fundamental research, universities and workforce development, while considering the establishment of "joint innovation centers that aren't just housed within TSMC."

One model he suggested was Belgium's Interuniversity Micro-Electronics Center (imec), an independent research institute that brings together industry and academia for collaborative semiconductor research.

Goodrich also called for stronger scientific cooperation with the U.S. and greater involvement by Taiwanese companies in research and development there.

"It would be really great to see more Taiwanese companies doing research and development in the U.S. as well," he said.

(By Sunny Lai)

title: The New Kalashnikov: Governing the Poor Man’s Autonomous Drone
zh_title: 新卡拉什尼科夫：管理穷人的自主无人机
source: Small Wars Journal by Arizona State Univ
summary: 摘要 廉价的商用无人机配备了现成的制导软件，为民兵和代理人提供了一种曾经为国家保留的精确打击形式。乌克兰已经展示了这种方法，而中国对民用飞机和零部件的控制使其难以关闭。联合国在日内瓦举行的会谈可以为高端国家系统制定规则，但它们并不是为了监管只有在转换后才成为武器的两用部件。因此，实际的应对措施是供应方：对使车载自主运行的硬件进行更严格的控制，对平台制造商承担义务
content:
摘要 廉价的商用无人机配备了现成的制导软件，为民兵和代理人提供了一种曾经为国家保留的精确打击形式。乌克兰已经展示了这种方法，而中国对民用飞机和零部件的控制使其难以关闭。联合国在日内瓦举行的会谈可以为高端国家系统制定规则，但它们并不是为了监管只有在转换后才成为武器的两用部件。因此，实际的应对措施是供应方：对使机载自主运行的硬件进行更严格的控制，对平台通常军事化的制造商承担义务，以及一个可以比条约更快行动的零部件生产盟友小联盟。扩散问题 尽管人们普遍认为，最危险的自主武器并不一定是人们在头条新闻中看到的那些华而不实的武器。今天在不起眼的棚屋里用商业部件建造的小型系统，明天部署在全球任何地方对抗美军，可能会危险得多。日内瓦会议继续讨论高端自主武器的道德和战略影响；然而，《特定常规武器公约》并不是作为监管商业供应链的机制而设计的，这种机制可以将四轴飞行器变成武器。民兵和叛乱组织已经在使用商用的、主要是中国制造的四轴飞行器来携带炸药。
这越来越多地涉及采用开源或商用计算机视觉和导航软件来实现更自主或半自主的功能，从而产生更有效的攻击能力。其战略意义不容忽视。廉价的、支持人工智能的神风特攻队无人机正在迅速降低精确打击的成本，并赋予非国家行为者曾经为传统军队保留的能力。虽然像中国自主隐形轰炸机这样的威胁为迄今为止未经证实的中国军事霸权迫在眉睫的故事提供了方便的复制品，但它们也占据了头条新闻。然而，美国安全面临的更直接、也更近在眼前的挑战是由商用组件组装而成的系统的大规模扩散。好消息是，我们不必等到大国战略竞争才进入强加成本的领域。坏消息是它已经存在，而且会一直存在。中国在商用无人机和军民两用零部件方面拥有近乎绝对的主导地位，这给北京带来了巨大的结构性优势，使合作伙伴和代理人能够在中国保持战略距离的同时对美国军队施加成本。新卡拉什尼科夫冲锋枪在很多方面都与 21 世纪的 AK-47 类似，它通过步兵战斗的民主化永久改变了 20 世纪的战争。
它这样做是因为它便宜、坚固、几乎不需要培训即可操作，而且更重要的是，因为苏联愿意将其变成7.62×39的地缘政治工具。商用无人机现在正在做类似的精确打击工作。就政策而言，区别在于 AK-47 是作为武器出现的，而无人机只有在改装后才成为武器。前沿部署部队和维持航行自由的能力是美国在印太和中东地区的联盟和威慑的核心。到目前为止，挑战这种力量投射一直是一项代价高昂的活动。然而，低成本自主和半自主无人机的普及正在改变

【原文 English Original】
Abstract Cheap commercial drones, fitted with readily available guidance software, are giving militias and proxies a form of precision strike once reserved for States. Ukraine has already shown the method, which China’s hold on civilian airframes and components makes hard to shut down. UN talks in Geneva can set rules for high-end state systems, but they were not built to police dual-use parts that become weapons only after conversion. The practical response is therefore supply-side: tighter controls on the hardware that makes onboard autonomy work, obligations on manufacturers whose platforms are routinely militarized, and a small coalition of component-producing allies that can move faster than a treaty. The Proliferation Problem Popular belief notwithstanding, the most dangerous autonomous weapons are not necessarily the flashy ones one sees in the headlines . Small systems built today from commercial parts in unassuming sheds and deployed tomorrow against US forces anywhere around the globe might very well be far more dangerous. Meetings in Geneva continue to grapple with the ethical and strategic implications of high-end autonomous weapons; however, the CCW was not designed as a mechanism for policing the commercial supply chains that can turn a quadcopter into a weapon. Militias and insurgent groups are already adapting commercially available, primarily Chinese-made quadcopters to carry explosives. This increasingly involves adapting open-source or commercially available computer vision and navigation software for more autonomous or semi-autonomous functions, yielding ever more effective attack capabilities. The strategic significance is difficult to miss. Cheap, AI-enabled kamikaze drones are rapidly lowering the cost of precision strikes and giving non-state actors capabilities once reserved for conventional militaries. While threats like Chinese autonomous stealth bombers make convenient copy for a hitherto unproven story of looming Chinese military supremacy, they also take the headlines. The more immediate challenge for US security, and the one closer to hand, however, is the mass proliferation of systems assembled from commercially available components. The good news is that we do not have to wait for great power strategic competition to enter the realm of cost-imposition. The bad news is that it is already here, and it is here to stay. China has near-absolute dominance in commercial drones and on dual-use components, which gives Beijing a great structural advantage, enabling partners and proxies to impose costs on US forces while China maintains strategic distance. The New Kalashnikov In many ways, what is happening is the 21st-century analog of the AK-47, which permanently altered 20th-century warfare by democratizing infantry combat. It did so because it is cheap, rugged, requires almost no training to operate, and, importantly, because of the Soviet Union’s willingness to turn it into a 7.62×39 geopolitical instrument. Commercial drones are now doing comparable work for precision strike. For policy, the difference is that the AK-47 arrived as a weapon while a drone becomes one only after conversion. Forward-deployed forces and the ability to maintain freedom of navigation are central to US alliances and deterrence in the Indo-Pacific and the Middle East. Until now, challenging this power projection has been an incredibly costly exercise. The spread of low-cost autonomous and semi-autonomous drones, however, is changing the equation by dramatically lowering the cost of contesting this presence. Indeed, the uncomfortable reality that has emerged over the past several years is that the cost and technical barriers to fielding lethal capability have collapsed rather dramatically . Non-state actors do not need a world-beating defense industrial base and eye-watering budgets to field increasingly capable drone swarms. Non-state actors require civilian drone frames , 3D-printed munitions , object recognition, tracking, and navigation software that are all widely and publicly available on platforms such as GitHub , often adapted or combined with commercial flight controllers . The future truly is a Google search away. Policymakers, who can hardly be blamed for not possessing a deep understanding in all things artificial intelligence – or technology in general – are trapped in an outdated paradigm that treats AI as a monolith rather than a spectrum of capabilities. Ukraine Already Wrote the Manual We do not have to hypothesize the nature of the strategic threat. The Russo-Ukrainian war has already made it plain at a terrible cost. Moscow has brought human suffering at an extraordinary scale in 21st-century Europe, yet the words of one of Ukraine’s foremost writers, Lesya Ukrainka , written more than a century ago, remain strikingly apt: those “who have not lived amidst the storm do not know the value of strength”. Ukraine has shown strength in industrial form, as the country has spent the past years demonstrating what cheap commercial frames, 3D-printed warheads, and increasingly autonomous terminal guidance are capable of. The method is mass-produced and cheap. Mass production, low costs, and a last-mile brain mean that a drone costing less than an entry-level iPhone can destroy a tank worth more than an oceanfront penthouse in Fort Lauderdale. Meanwhile, the operator no longer needs to be a particularly gifted flyer. Reports of drones selecting and striking with little or no real-time piloting are no longer speculative . With the lines blurring, the lessons are not limited to Ukraine, as state and non-state forces may now field remarkably similar stacks . The recipes in the Big are comparatively simple: pair cheap commercial airframes with open-source or adapted autonomous navigation and terminal guidance software, then season to taste with fiber-optic links . Serve with gusto. Cooks can significantly reduce vulnerability to traditional electronic warfare jamming and can threaten forward-deployed US forces at a fraction of the traditional cost of building an air force. Closing the Governance Gap Digesting the threat is further complicated by global diplomatic -and administrative- frameworks being fundamentally mismatched to the pace and character of AI-enabled warfare. The Group of Governmental Experts (GGE) is the right forum for developing rules and principles governing state responsibilities, such as how a system is characterized, whether it can meet distinction and proportionality, and who remains responsible when it engages. Traditional arms control mechanisms are built for identifiable weapons categories, but they work far less well in a dual-use commercial ecosystem in which the weapon appears only at conversion. The GGE, however, works by consensus, and consensus moves slowly. Russia has frequently used consensus procedures to slow binding outcomes while China has taken a relatively clear position in Geneva, but both continue to enable and encourage the spread of lower-tier drone technology and components to proxies and partners . Consequently, when it comes to governing agile, dual-use commercial technologies, existing multilateral institutions and mechanisms are struggling to keep pace. What makes this rapidly emerging threat different is accessibility . High-end autonomous systems still require industrial depth and political backing. A drone assembled from commercial parts in a garage does not. Such parts can now be turned into a usable strike capability at a price that non-state actors can readily absorb. It is easy for policymakers to focus on the most visible and expensive systems, yet by doing so they will keep missing the cheaper ones that spread far more easily. The United States cannot realistically ban the civilian staples of such systems , as many, like smartphone processors, commercial optical sensors, and agricultural drone motors, are ubiquitous in legitimate commercial markets. Unlike international agreements, which usually take years to negotiate and formalize, the hardware development cycle is much shorter. Denying the Stack, Not the Algorithm The United States should therefore pivot to a pragmatic supply denial strategy. Yet while the strategy is sound, putting it into practice is not. Dual-use controls face a deep structural problem. The same components that underpin legitimate commercial applications can, with comparatively little modification, support terminal guidance and autonomous navigation for attack drones . Consequently, any effective supply denial regime must differentiate between legitimate end uses and transactions that present a meaningful risk of diversion without effectively shutting down civilian markets and inadvertently facilitating large-scale economic disruption. This is an intrinsically dynamic and fraught task , and one of the central problems of autonomous systems governance. Not only does this problem involve discerning the commercial technologies most critical to national security, but it also entails imposing effective constraints that are workable even as commercial technology races ahead of regulatory cycles. Skeptics will contend that because open-source computer-vision models — from general-purpose detectors to specialized weights trained to recognize military drones — are already mirrored across thousands of public repositories , the software genie is out of the bottle. And the sceptics will be right. They will, however, be missing the point and the physical reality of fielding autonomous capability at scale. Even when the software is freely available, a host of practical limitations stand in the way of turning it into reliable, long-range attack systems. There are specialized low-power edge chips that can run inference without rapidly draining batteries or overheating. Energy-dense batteries that determine endurance are a necessity. Airframes and motors that set payload and range limits are a must. So are munitions integration that turns a commercial platform into a weapon. Finally, much operational learning is required to reliably deploy these systems under electronic-warfare conditions. There is no way of denying that chips are a very important choke point, but they are not the only one. Rather than targeting a single component in isolation, dual-use export controls must target the combination of enabling hardware. By tightening controls across physical and software layers on both domestic and foreign suppliers, the United States can raise the costs and lower the reliability of proliferated autonomous systems, reducing strategic uncertainty before international consensus on governing autonomous weapons is reached. Building a Minilateral Denial Coalition It is paramount that Washington takes an interagency approach to the problem. The US should build a minilateral technology denial coalition with key component-producing allies, specifically Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and relevant European States. By harmonizing export restrictions on dual-use microcontrollers, optical sensors, and drone motors across manufacturing hubs, the coalition can bottleneck the supply chain for non-state actors. Battlefield exploitation of recovered airframes should feed dual-use control lists at commercial speed so the items that actually appear on last-mile drones are the ones that get scrutinized. Instead of treating export controls and multilateral norm setting as separate tracks, Washington should treat supply denial as one practical instrument within a broader autonomous systems governance approach. In the short term, the most pressing security concern is uncontrolled proliferation of the technologies that allow non-state actors to field autonomous systems. A focused multilateral export control arrangement, drawing on the Missile Technology Control Regime ( MTCR ) but aimed at the critical dual-use components of small autonomous drones, can raise the threshold for proliferation while diplomatic processes continue. While missiles and drones are very different beasts, the MTCR provides a useful model because it targeted tangible delivery systems and related technologies rather than abstract concepts. It would be quite an overstatement to call the MTCR faultless, as its record is quite mixed. Nonetheless, a similarly focused regime targeting critical physical components of the autonomous drone supply chain could prove more agile than broad treaty efforts, and the United States has reinterpreted aspects of the MTCR for drone exports. The first step is exploiting hardware and dual-use chokepoints through targeted export thresholds . One may attempt a rather futile blanket ban on basic microcontrollers, but there is a far better way, as controls should focus on performance and characteristics, and power thresholds. These enable real-time onboard autonomy in small airframes, low-power edge accelerators, high-end optical sensors, and related components that significantly improve autonomous targeting and navigation. Restricting the most capable of these items and applying tighter scrutiny to diversion pathways could push proliferators toward less capable, more jammable, and/or shorter-range configurations. Making Manufacturers Own the Conversion Risk The second most important step is to impose enforceable strict due diligence and security obligations on major manufacturers. Drones may seem to appear out of thin air, but they must be manufactured somewhere. There are a myriad of Chinese drone producers, but the market is dominated by a handful of giants, with the most notable of them being DJI, whose platforms are routinely modified for military use by proxies and non-state actors. In mid-August, the company won a partial victory in its long legal battle with the US government as an appeals court ordered a lower court to reconsider designating the firm as a “Chinese military company.” The case illustrates why designation needs to be paired with specific obligations to the manufacturer and the penalties for their non-fulfilment. No manufacturer of any equipment is. However, when firms knowingly profit from platforms that are regularly diverted to armed conflict while refusing to adopt reasonable measures to prevent this from happening, governments should be prepared to impose market access restrictions and sanctions. DJI has largely shifted its US GEO system from automatic flight restrictions toward advisory warnings. In a similar vein, any additional limitations imposed by manufacturers, firmware modifications, or other restrictions that make militarization more difficult should be encouraged or outright required as a condition of access to the Western markets. Enforcing this liability, however, requires using existing regulatory architecture rather than creating yet another framework. Where manufacturers’ platforms do not include cryptographically signed, secure-boot firmware that makes unauthorized flight-controller overrides more difficult, Washington should condition access to specified US software and technology on compliance with those security requirements, and use export control authorities including, where applicable, the Foreign Direct Product Rule ( FDPR ). Furthermore, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control should consider targeted sanctions against foreign distribution and modification networks that facilitate the transformation of civilian airframes into weapons. If a manufacturer is unwilling to make its civilian technology resistant to cheap conversion to military use, it should be completely cut off from Western markets. Lastly, Washington should require major platforms and repositories hosting dual-use target-recognition AI to adopt end-user screening and threat-reporting protocols for high-risk models. The goal is to add friction to the otherwise easy-to-download terminal-guidance software. Acting at Market Speed To state the glaringly obvious, the democratization of automated lethality is here, and it is going to stay. We cannot un-invent open-source algorithms, nor can we recall the millions of civilian quadcopters already in circulation. Slow as it may be, the UN establishes vital long-term benchmarks for meaningful human control and legal accountability. These are of great importance. But protecting forces and commercial shipping today also requires agile supply-side tools that raise the cost of turning commercial drones into autonomous or semi-autonomous weapons. Since China can effectively leverage dual-use commercial technologies, inaction risks handing the strategic advantage to Beijing. The US can act swiftly and move almost as fast as the market does to adopt export controls, corporate oversight, and screening measures on dual-use technologies. Until long-term rules catch up, these will serve as effective policy levers in regulating autonomous systems. Two clocks are running. In November, the High Contracting Parties decide what to do with GGE elements such as characterization, international humanitarian law, human judgment, and responsibility that stays with people. The other clock is the conversion cycle on commercial frames. Export thresholds and conversion-resistant firmware are crucial for governing the second clock. Washington cannot treat denial as a substitute for international rules and expect to have much to say about control when it gets to Geneva. But the reverse is equally problematic, as Geneva will not stop a commercial drone from being turned into an autonomous weapon if the components are already in the hands of those who want such a weapon. By then, the last mile will already have been fielded. The post The New Kalashnikov: Governing the Poor Man’s Autonomous Drone appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

**Hillary Johnson**

# Hong Kong Photojournalism Trip

Hi everyone, my name is Hillary Johnson, and I’m a photographer living in Chicago, working all over the Midwest and in Hong Kong. I have two main threads to my photography practice, photojournalism and fine art. Though it feels awkward, I confess, I’m pushing ahead because I need your help. I’m going to Hong Kong on November 12 to cover the protest and the election of a new cabinet in Hong Kong. You might wonder why bother giving money to me or why my voice particular needs to be added to this news event, or even why this matters to you at all. I hear that and I’ll do my best to answer your questions. I’ll also explain what you can do if you’re interested in helping out. A little bit about me: in addition to being a photographer I’m also someone who studies a martial art called Ving Tsun. This art is extremely popular in Hong Kong for various reasons that I won’t go into right now but if you’re curious you can ask me and I’ll be happy to answer. It was the practice of this martial art that introduced me to my husband, Matt Johnson who runs a kung fu school here in Chicago. This martial art has a code of ethics that involves being a good citizen, being humble, promoting peace, and standing up for what is right and protecting those who need protection from bullies and so forth. I made my first trip to Hong Kong a couple of years ago and I’ve been back a few times since then. Though I’m someone who likes spend a lot of time in remote locations being quiet and letting the busyness of my mind and heart settle down, I felt 100% in love with the city of Hong Kong, it’s culture, it’s people, and of course with my kung fu family there. As a result it has been difficult watching the news and worrying about this place I love so much and the people who live there. My concern for all of this led me to do a story for the Chicago Reader. Here's a link to that: https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/photos-hong-kong-protest-freedom/Content?oid=73815391I’m extremely grateful to the reader for giving me the time and space that it did. I made all the photographs, did all the interviews, and wrote all the text with guidance from the amazing Reader staff. In the process of working on that story I began to see, that much that was going on in Hong Kong seems to not quite be making it into the news. This made me want to go to Hong Kong and do more. The stories we have been seeing her only the tip of the iceberg. I’m interested in the stories of ordinary people, their everyday life, and what they do. What are their day jobs? How do they prepare for protesting? How do they support each other in the midst of such extreme difficulty? I want to understand the impact of what’s happening in this interaction between the Beijing mainland Chinese government in the city of Hong Kong in the Hong Kong people. It’s interesting that Hong Kong has roots and connections stretching out from the city, all over the globe. While working on the story I’ve met many people here in Chicago who have a deep connections to Hong Kong. I want to go and photograph an interview to help amplify the voices of those people not being heard as much as they might be. Why do the events Hong Kong matter to you wherever you might live? Here are a few reasons: Number one. Hong Kong people are simply asking for fundamental human rights to be recognized. Number two. The Hong Kong people are asking for the promises made by the Chinese government to be kept. Number three. The Hong Kong people want their freedom. All people everywhere around the world want their fundamental human rights, they want promises to be kept and they want freedom. If we all look into our own hearts I believe we will see this truth is self evident. What’s happening in Hong Kong matters to all of us, because all of us want the same things; freedom, respect- both given and received, dignity, and agency. Further, for those of us living in other parts of the world, if we think that what’s happening in Hong Kong cannot happen to us wherever it is that we happen to live, I think if you forgive me, that view is naïve. The road to tyranny is a slippery slope. First one right is eroded, then another, then another. For this trip to Hong Kong all the groundwork is in place. Because of the network being built up over the years and as a result of my recent work, there are people on the ground in Hong Kong ready to help with making connections, translation, safety and getting around and so forth. My intention is to get to Hong Kong do my work at the photographer and then do my best to get those stories out into the world so that everyone can know what is going on. But I need help with the expenses. Here is a list: Airfare and hotel around $2100-2400 depending on flight detailsTransportation in Hong Kong When the MTR is shut down taxis may be necessary - estimating maybe $300Money to pay translators and other fixtures and facilitators estimating $300-500A laptop to process photos while I’m there so I can send them out to editors at various news outlets - around $200-300I’m hoping to raise $3500. to cover all of that as well as some of my bills while I’m away so that the lights and heat are still on when I return home. Addition I’ll provide links to news outlets as well as the story I did for the reader so that you can get more information about the situation over there. I’ll also link or attach a video that I made about the story. As things when I’m planning to offer in addition to publicly thinking everyone who supports this is the creation of a private Facebook group where I post updates photos and video from my time in Hong Kong. This content will be exclusively for anyone who supports this trip. I’m excited to announce that someone already made a first donation of $500 before even launched this campaign which let me adjust the amount needed to $3500Honestly I wasn’t even planning on doing this but so many people said to me that they wanted to support the trip and believe in the mission of supporting truth and openness and democracy, that I pushed past my own discomfort and jumped

Taekwondo athlete Xiao Xiang-wen. CNA photo Oct. 14, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 19 (CNA) Taekwondo athlete Xiao Xiang-wen (蕭翔文) won Taiwan's first gold medal at the Nagoya Asian Para Games after successfully defending his men's K44 under-58kg title on Monday.

Xiao defeated Uzbekistan's Fayoz Valijonov in the final, winning the first round 8-2 and the second 18-6.

After the victory, Xiao and his coach, Wu Yen-ni (吳燕妮), made a lap around the court carrying the Chinese Taipei flag to celebrate his win.

The 2026 Asian Para Games are being held in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan, from Oct. 18 to 24. Taiwan has sent 71 athletes to compete.

# German orchestra Staatskapelle Berlin to make Taiwan debut in November

10/19/2026 05:23 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

Renowned conductor Christian Thielemann leads an orchestra in this undated photo for illustrative purposes. Photo courtesy of Management of New Arts

Taipei, Oct. 19 (CNA) The Staatskapelle Berlin, a German orchestra with more than 450 years of history, will make its Taiwan debut in November under renowned conductor Christian Thielemann, the Taipei-based Management of New Arts (MNA) said Monday.

MNA said in a statement that the Staatskapelle Berlin will give three concerts in Taiwan, beginning Nov. 21 at the National Concert Hall in Taipei with a performance of Mozart's Piano Concerto No. 21 and Bruckner's Symphony No. 4.

The orchestra will perform again at the National Concert Hall on Nov. 22 before making its Kaohsiung debut on Nov. 24 at the National Kaohsiung Center for the Arts (Weiwuying). Both concerts will feature Richard Strauss' Four Last Songs and An Alpine Symphony, it said.

Thielemann became music director of the Berlin State Opera and Staatskapelle Berlin in 2025, succeeding several distinguished figures who have led the renowned German institution, including Richard Strauss, Wilhelm Furtwängler and Daniel Barenboim, MNA said.

In a 2023 interview with German broadcaster BR-Klassik, he recalled conducting the symphony too slowly in his early 20s because he was so emotionally absorbed in the music.

He said years of experience had taught him to find the right tempo and rhythmic flow in Bruckner's compositions.

The Staatskapelle Berlin also has a history of performing Bruckner's music. Under former music director Daniel Barenboim, the orchestra recorded the composer's nine numbered symphonies and performed the cycle at venues in Vienna, New York and Paris, MNA said.

(By Chao Ching-yu and Ko Lin)

title: 欧盟对华关税波及乌克兰，钢铁巨头称
summary: 乌克兰最大钢铁公司之一的老板呼吁欧盟取消对该国产品的进口限制，认为该国在旨在遏制中国等廉价进口产品的措施中被“打包在一起”了。 乌克兰 Metinvest 首席执行官尤里·日尔热诺夫（Yuriy Ryzhenkov）告诉 BBC，最近对进口钢铁征收的关税对欧盟是“不公平的”，且是在“未考虑乌克兰所处情况”的情况下实施的。 他表示希望看到为乌克兰进入欧盟市场开辟“至少一个例外”。 欧盟委员会发言人表示，欧盟在制定钢铁政策时“已考虑到乌克兰的艰难处境”。 该贸易集团最近对钢铁进口
content: 乌克兰最大钢铁公司之一的老板呼吁欧盟取消对该国产品的进口限制，认为该国在旨在遏制中国等廉价进口产品的措施中被“打包在一起”了。 乌克兰 Metinvest 首席执行官尤里·日尔热诺夫（Yuriy Ryzhenkov）告诉 BBC，最近对进口钢铁征收的关税对欧盟是“不公平的”，且是在“未考虑乌克兰所处情况”的情况下实施的。 他表示希望看到为乌克兰进入欧盟市场开辟“至少一个例外”。 欧盟委员会发言人表示，欧盟在制定钢铁政策时“已考虑到乌克兰的艰难处境”。 该贸易集团最近对钢铁进口实施了限制，以保护成员国钢铁制造商。 它规定每年可免税进入欧盟的钢铁数量上限为 1830 万吨，较 2024 年水平减少了 47%。 该政策中有一些针对特定国家的配额，但总体目标是减少可进口的钢铁数量，因为成员国难以与中国和土耳其等国的廉价进口产品竞争。 尽管欧盟与乌克兰之间存在自由贸易协定（FTA），但该协定并不阻止欧盟引入单独的贸易保护措施。 “乌克兰在制定措施时被‘打包在一起’，未考虑乌克兰的处境，”日尔热诺夫说，并指出与俄罗斯的战争。 “进入欧洲市场对生存至关重要，”他补充道。“欧盟当局实施的限制性措施没有帮助。” “我认为乌克兰被与进入欧盟的所有其他进口商同等对待是不公平的。” 乌克兰钢铁行业估计，钢铁出口到欧盟最终可能下降约 50% 至 60%。 欧盟表示，乌克兰的特定钢铁配额保证了金属出口，但承认这一水平“低于往年”。 “尽管战争仍在继续，乌克兰仍然是欧盟重要的钢铁出口国，”一位发言人表示，并补充称，它已“提供补偿”给其最大供应商，其中包括乌克兰。 Metinvest 首席执行官尤里·日尔热诺夫表示，欧盟钢铁配额对乌克兰是“不公平的” 钢铁产品是乌克兰经济的基础。在 2022 年俄罗斯全面入侵开始之前，冶金和采矿约占乌克兰国民收入的 10%，占其出口总额的三分之一。欧盟是其最大的客户。 但行业一直遭受持续的俄罗斯轰炸之苦。 自 2022 年冲突开始以来，乌克兰的所有钢铁厂都曾遭受过轰炸，但日尔热诺夫表示，袭击最近“显著加剧”。 他在 9 月曾提到，乌克兰“首次”连续约 150 年没有生产“任何一吨钢铁”，他补充道。 自战争开始以来，近 800 名 Metinvest 工人已丧生。 日尔热诺夫表示，该公司已“改善了”其钢铁厂中工人可在空袭中避难的覆盖区域。 “我们能做的唯一事情就是设计程序来保护人员安全，遵守这些程序，并尽量降低风险。” “不幸的是，你无法覆盖整个钢铁厂以避免其受损。” 日尔热诺夫表示，他预计即将到来的冬天将是“我们历史上最艰难的一个”。 “我们处于困境之中，除了欧盟之外没有其他市场可以进入，而我们可用的市场减少了 60%，这对行业生存没有帮助。”

content:
A Book about Anti-Communist Movies

We are on the eve of the announcement of the lineup at the first annual Anti-Communist Film Festival. Our headline film is **The Lives of Others.**

I’ve spent over a year talking to Hollywood studios about licensing, visiting movie theaters to make my case (as you might expect, some were not thrilled with the idea), and finally getting a sponsor with the great folks at the Victims of Communism Foundation.

**There’s one more thing I’d like to do. I have a 20,000-word essay about my favorite anti-communist movies, and I'd like to publish it next year as a book and companion to the film festival.** Excerpts from the essay have been published on Hot Air, Chronicles, and on the Victims of Communism website. I’d like to publish the entire essay in paper format, something that people can hold. A samizdat, which during the Cold War was a book or pamphlet that was forbidden in communist countries and was passed around from hand to hand by dissidents.

**Most importantly, what I am calling Freedom’s Fury: A Guide to Anti-Communist Movies would be something that cannot be digitally erased.**

In his forthcoming book Reds: A Global History of Communism, journalist Paul Mason explores how communists want us to forget the past:

I do not want to “take control” of the memory of Marx, any more than the memory of the Russian Revolution or the Spanish Civil War. But I do want to prevent the Communist Party of China from taking control of them. Because, as [philosopher Walter] Benjamin reminds us: “not even the dead are safe from the enemy.” Just as postwar fascism fought to expunge the facts about the Holocaust, we are now seeing—in Putin’s Russia, Xi’s China, and political movements aligned to them in the global south—systematic distortions of the events described here. And it will get worse. In occupied Ukraine, new statues of Lenin are being erected. In Russia, plaques commemorating victims of the Great Purge are being torn down, and the last museum of the Gulag has been closed. In China, all critical writing about Mao is dismissed as “historical nihilism.”

Mason then notes how his own book may be censored:

As you read each chapter, I want you to imagine how it might be written in a future dominated by the brain-frozen clichés of Chinese communism. The Beijing propaganda machine has been busy eradicating the truth about the Tiananmen Square Massacre for nearly forty years. What might it achieve if given the unchallenged right to curate the facts about 1848, 1917, or indeed 1789? Far from being yesterday’s problem, the struggle for the truth about the history of communism may have only just begun. If so, Benjamin’s words on the eve of its darkest and finest hours bear repeating: Every line we succeed in publishing today—no matter how uncertain the future to which we entrust it—is a victory wrested from the powers of darkness.

**American communists would like nothing more than to censor the Anti-Communist Film Festival and forget it ever existed, even before it begins.**

title: US bans use of China’s DeepSeek by gov’t agencies
zh_title: 美国禁止政府机构使用中国的 DeepSeek
summary: 美国政府周一下令其机构停止使用中国初创公司 DeepSeek 的人工智能工具，因为两国正在争夺快速发展领域的主导地位。深探。照片：Matheus Bertelli/Pexels。美国国土安全部发布通知，宣布禁止 DeepSeek 开发的产品以及第三方使用 DeepSeek 创建的工具，并表示必须将它们从 IT 设备中删除。该部门可以向民事机构发出指示，但不能向军队或情报部门发出指示。华盛顿国防部没有回应法新社的要求
content:
美国政府周一下令其机构停止使用中国初创公司 DeepSeek 的人工智能工具，因为两国正在争夺快速发展领域的主导地位。深探。照片：Matheus Bertelli/Pexels。美国国土安全部发布通知，宣布禁止 DeepSeek 开发的产品以及第三方使用 DeepSeek 创建的工具，并表示必须将它们从 IT 设备中删除。该部门可以向民事机构发出指示，但不能向军队或情报部门发出指示。华盛顿国防部没有回应法新社的置评请求。 “DeepSeek 的模型呈现出多种威胁向量，”周一通知所附的一份文件称。该部门警告称，如果美国政府雇员或供应商使用 DeepSeek 人工智能工具，“可能会导致敏感数据传输到（中国）”。它说，其服务器位于中国，那里的法律体系允许政府“广泛的权力”访问私营公司的基础设施。法新社已联系 DeepSeek 寻求评论。美国国土安全部总部位于华盛顿特区。照片：维基共享资源。 DeepSeek 是中国顶尖的人工智能实验室之一，它于 2025 年 1 月凭借一款低成本、高性能的聊天机器人震惊了整个行业，挑战了美国主导地位的假设。该公司在 4 月份发布了期待已久的新型号 V4，并在本月更新了更快、更轻量级的 V4 版本。
美国指责DeepSeek和其他中国顶尖人工智能公司系统性窃取美国竞争对手开发的尖端模型的能力。尽管该领域竞争激烈，中美两国仍于9月同意建立人工智能事件的“沟通渠道”。预计当两国领导人下个月在中国深圳举行峰会时，这个话题将再次出现。

【原文 English Original】
The US government on Monday ordered its agencies to stop using artificial intelligence tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, as the countries race for dominance in the fast-moving sector. Deepseek. Photo: Matheus Bertelli/Pexels. A notice from the Department of Homeland Security announced the ban on products developed by DeepSeek — and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties — saying they must be removed from IT devices. The department can issue direction to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services. Washington’s Department of Defense did not respond to an AFP request for comment. “DeepSeek’s models present multiple threat vectors,” said a document attached to Monday’s notice. Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors,” the department warned. Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said. AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment. Headquarters of the US Department of Homeland Security in Washington DC. Photo: Wikicommons. DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance. The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April, and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4. The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals. Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents. The topic is expected to arise again when the countries’ leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen .

广告

（德国之声中文网）美国政府周一（10月19日）下令联邦机构停止使用中国人工智能工具“深度求索”（DeepSeek）。

美国国土安全部的通告宣布，禁止使用深度求索开发的产品，以及第三方使用深度求索创建的工具。通告称，必须从IT设备中移除相关工具。

周一的这份通告中写道：“深度求索的模型存在多种威胁途径。”

国土安全部警告说，使用深度求索人工智能工具“可能导致敏感数据传输（向中国），倘若美国政府雇员或供应商使用的话”。

该通告说，深度求索的服务器位于中国，该国法律体系下，政府拥有“广泛的权限”访问私有公司的基础设施。

美国曾指责深度求索等中国顶尖的人工智能公司系统性窃取美国公司研发的先进模型能力。

尽管中美在AI领域面临激烈竞争，9月，两国间仍达成一致，设立人工智能领域的对话机制。

预计该议题也将出现在下月美中领导人会晤的日程上。11月中旬，美国总统特朗普与中国国家主席习近平预计将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会期间举行会晤。

## “大量个人数据存储在中国”

周二，中国外交部发言人在被问及此事时表示：“中方一贯反对泛化国家安全概念、将科技经贸问题政治化。我们将坚决维护中国企业合法权益。”

路透社写道，按照深度求索自身的隐私政策，大量个人数据被存储在中国，包括向其AI程序提出的请求，以及上传的文档。除美国外，还有一些国家出于安全隐忧禁用深度求索。

比如澳大利亚。去年2月，澳大利亚在所有政府设备上禁用深度求索，因担忧构成安全风险。捷克去年7月禁止该国公共行政部门使用深度求索的任何服务，原因是担忧数据安全。台湾去年2月禁止政府部门使用深度求索的服务，因视其为安全风险。此外，台湾也就深度求索的审查以及数据流向中国表示忧虑。还有一些国家正在对深度求索的安全性进行审查。

zh_title: 潜水甲虫蛋挞吸引爱冒险的美食家来到广东餐馆

content:
中国
佛山一家餐馆的蛋挞是中国南方的传统美食，上面放着整个甲虫，这种蛋挞已经走红，吸引了来自香港和其他地方的食客。售价28元的三件套自10月以来每天已售出约20份订单。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 19 日 20:08 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

广东佛山的一家餐厅凭借一种非传统的甜点而引起了烹饪界的轰动：整只潜水甲虫栖息在新鲜出炉的蛋挞上。这道菜吸引了中国南方各地爱冒险的美食爱好者，其特色是可食用的水生甲虫，俗称“水蟑螂”，传统上称为“龙石”，是中国南方民间美食的长期组成部分。

这种昆虫与经典点心的新颖搭配在社交媒体上疯传，促使包括香港在内的邻近地区的美食博主和食客前往这家店体验大胆的品尝体验。创始人是一位姓潘的餐馆老板，他说这个想法来自于他对传统粤菜食材的终生熟悉以及重新发明本地点心的愿望。
准备昆虫需要精心照顾。潘表示，甲虫必须首先彻底除臭，去除残留的沼泽气味，然后才能油炸以获得酥脆的质地。油炸过程需要精确的温度调节，以确保精致的翅膀保持完整并具有视觉吸引力，然后将每只甲虫放置在温暖的、充满蛋奶冻的馅饼壳上。

潘形容成品甜点的质地让人想起吃标准的片状蛋挞，上面放着脆脆的薯片。除了新颖的吸引力之外，潜水甲虫在传统的南方草药文化中也占有一席之地。潘指出，民间医学长期以来将昆虫视为多种健康益处，包括缓解夜尿、增强肾活力和滋养肤色。根据广东人的饮食习惯，食客通常会剥去坚硬的外翅壳，然后将整个昆虫与甜糕点一起食用。

该糕点套餐自10月份上架以来，一直保持着28元三份的价格，每天稳定保持在20份左右的销量。这种奇异的外观引起了广泛的好奇，吸引了来自附近广州的游客以及从香港过境的游客。
这道菜也在网上获得了更广泛的关注，吸引了一位来自北京的有影响力的人，她专程南下，现场直播自己品尝甜点，还有一位意大利美食视频博主，为国际追随者记录了品尝体验。

China
A Foshan restaurant's egg tarts topped with whole diving beetles, a traditional southern Chinese delicacy, have gone viral and drawn diners from Hong Kong and beyond. The 28 yuan set of three has sold about 20 orders daily since October.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 20:08 HKT · 2 min read

A Foshan restaurant in Guangdong has become an unlikely culinary sensation with an unconventional dessert: whole diving beetles perched on freshly baked egg tarts. The dish, which has captivated adventurous food lovers across southern China, features edible aquatic beetles known colloquially as "water cockroaches" and traditionally called longshi, a longtime part of southern Chinese folk cuisine.

The novel pairing of the insects with a classic dim sum favourite has gone viral on social media, prompting food bloggers and diners from neighbouring areas, including Hong Kong, to visit the shop for a bold tasting experience. The creator, a restaurateur surnamed Pan, said the idea came from his lifelong familiarity with traditional Cantonese ingredients and a desire to reinvent local dim sum.

Preparing the insects requires meticulous care. According to Pan, the beetles must first be thoroughly deodorised to remove any lingering swampy scent before being deep-fried to achieve a crisp texture. The frying process demands precise temperature regulation to ensure the delicate wings remain intact and visually appealing, before each beetle is positioned atop a warm, custard-filled tart shell.

Pan described the texture of the finished dessert as reminiscent of eating a standard flaky egg tart topped with a crunchy potato chip. Beyond their novelty appeal, diving beetles hold a niche spot in traditional southern herbal culture. Pan noted that folk medicine has long attributed various wellness benefits to the insects, including alleviating nocturia, boosting kidney vitality, and nourishing the complexion. In line with Cantonese eating habits, diners typically peel away the hard outer wing cases before consuming the entire insect together with the sweet pastry.

Since the pastry set hit the menu in October, it has been priced at 28 yuan for a serving of three pieces, maintaining a steady daily sales volume of roughly 20 orders. The bizarre appearance has generated widespread curiosity, drawing visitors from nearby Guangzhou as well as travellers crossing the border from Hong Kong.

The dish has also gained broader online traction, attracting an influencer from Beijing who journeyed south specifically to livestream herself sampling the dessert, along with an Italian food vlogger who documented the tasting experience for international followers.

content: 文章来源：纽约时报 作者：CHOE SANG-HUN 周四，朝鲜与中国开通了两国间最大的边境通道——新鸭绿江大桥。尽管旨在遏制朝鲜经济及核武器计划的国际制裁依然存在，此举表明双边贸易正在不断增长。 最近几周，从边境江段返回的旅客反映，已有卡车和客车经由这座双向四车道、长约三公里的大桥从中国驶入朝鲜。这座桥梁连接中国丹东市与坐落于鸭绿江畔的朝鲜城市新义州，鸭绿江构成了两国间的大部分边界。 据中国官方媒体报道，这座桥梁通车距朝俄启用横跨图们江边境、规模小得多的首座公路桥仅相隔一个月。两座跨境桥梁的相继启用凸显出平壤正在深化与这两大主要盟友的关系。 据中国官方媒体报道，中国国务院总理李强在开通仪式上发表视频致辞时表示，新大桥“不仅将有力促进两国经贸合作，也将进一步密切双方人员往来”。报道称，朝鲜内阁总理朴泰成亦通过视频致辞。 随着平壤向对乌克兰作战的莫斯科提供武器和军事人员援助，俄罗斯建造了公路桥，以弥补其与朝鲜间单一铁路连接的不足。随着朝俄关系不断强化，中国也着手扩大对朝贸易，力求保持对该邻国的经济影响力。 早在2024年，莫斯科与北京联手解散了负责监督制裁执行情况的联合国专家小组，从而削弱了针对朝鲜的国际制裁。两国还敦促华盛顿放宽对朝限制，主张制裁并未能阻止朝鲜研发核武器。 分析人士警告称，这些新建桥梁可能成为朝鲜的贸易通道。受制于联合国禁止煤炭和劳工等关键出口并严控燃料进口的制裁措施，朝鲜经济此前已承受重压。 此前，新义州与丹东主要依靠拥有83年历史的中朝友谊桥相连，该桥仅设一条单轨铁路和一条公路。这座老化的桥梁无法承载20吨以上的货车，且需严格保持每小时约4.8公里的限速。2009年，中国提议建造桥面更宽的新鸭绿江大桥，作为将朝鲜进一步纳入自身经济辐射范围的更广泛举措之一。 该工程于2014年竣工，耗资约3.29亿美元且全额由中方承担。但因朝方耗时修建连接道路、海关检查站及配套设施，通车时间被推迟了12年。 平壤方面也担忧对华依赖进一步加深。数十年的国际制裁使朝鲜在几乎所有对外贸易上均依赖中国；在联合国安理会将朝鲜主要出口产品列入黑名单后，该国对华贸易逆差急剧攀升。 位于首尔的国家安保战略研究院分析师金奎范（音）表示：“从朝鲜的角度来看，新鸭绿江大桥的开通可能促使中国商品更快捷、更大规模地进入，却无法确保朝鲜能大幅增加对华出口。”他指出：“若贸易逆差与对华依赖持续加深，这没有理由成为朝鲜所乐见的前景。” 分析人士指出，在同意大桥通车前，朝鲜可能争取过某些优惠条件，以便利本国对华出口，并为更多朝鲜劳工在华务工创造机会。 朝鲜领导人金正恩面临着双重挑战，既要进口重建其经济所需的中国原材料和设备，又需筹集硬通货。朝鲜主要通过走私、向海外输出劳工、网络行动以及盗窃加密货币等非法手段来实现了外汇目标。 金正恩以新冠疫情为由严打自华走私消费品，同时要求国内增产此类产品。他还试图通过吸引中国游客前往朝鲜各地新建的沿海与山区度假胜地，来缓解长期的贸易失衡状况。 随着平壤在乌克兰战争期间向莫斯科靠拢，中国加快了与朝鲜重新接触的步伐。去年，中国领导人习近平邀请金正恩与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京出席北京的阅兵式。疫情期间暂停的京平客运列车已于3月恢复运行，习近平6月访问了平壤。 中国官方数据显示，今年上半年朝中官方贸易额达15亿美元，创下2017年联合国全面制裁完全落地以来的最高水平。

content:
官方媒体援引地方当局的消息称，中国偏远的西藏地区发生强烈地震，造成至少 16 人死亡、46 人受伤。布达拉宫，西藏拉萨。资料照片：维基共享资源。周四晚上 10:33（格林威治标准时间 1433）发生的 7.0 级地震中，超过 300 栋房屋倒塌。官方通讯社新华社称，官员们仍在评估损失情况，救灾工作正在进行中。中国中央电视台（CCTV）援引当地官员的话说，受伤人数为 46 人，其中 11 人伤势严重，339 间房屋倒塌或受损。中央电视台发布的视频显示，地震发生时，餐厅里的工作人员纷纷逃离，超市货架上的物品纷纷掉落。美国地质调查局称，震中位于那曲地区东北偏东约190公里、自治区首府拉萨东北390公里的山区。撞击深度约为10公里。美国地质勘探局绘制的 2026 年 10 月 22 日西藏地震地震震动图。照片：美国地质调查局。据央视报道，该地区已启动三级地震灾害应急响应。震中位于巴庆县马如乡。据新华社报道，镇副镇长拉旺达波表示，镇政府明显有震感，办公室墙壁出现裂缝。该机构表示，县城的电力和电信服务中断。
据新华社报道，已派出300多名警察参与救援工作，地区消防救援总队已调集347名人员前往受灾地区。闭路电视画面显示，救援人员爬过受损的建筑物，其中一些建筑物的屋顶已经倒塌，并载着一名人员。它还显示救援人员用手电筒照射其他受损的建筑物，士兵们排队准备部署。中国的地震比较常见。 2025年1月，西藏定日县发生地震，造成至少126人死亡。据官方媒体报道，2023 年 12 月，中国西北部偏远的甘肃省发生地震，造成至少 127 人死亡。那次地震是中国自 2014 年以来最严重的一次地震，当时西南部的云南省有 600 多人死亡。 2008年四川省发生大地震，造成约9万人死亡或失踪，其中包括约5,000名学童。

【原文 English Original】
A strong earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured 46 in China’s remote Tibet region, state media said, citing local authorities. Potala Palace, Lhasa, Tibet. File photo: Wikicommons. More than 300 houses collapsed in the 7.0 magnitude quake, which struck on Thursday at 10:33 pm (1433 GMT). Officials were still evaluating the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, state news agency Xinhua said. China Central Television (CCTV) put the number of injured at 46, 11 of them seriously, with 339 houses collapsed or damaged, citing local officials. Videos posted by CCTV showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck. The epicentre was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said. It struck at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres. USGS Shakemap of the earthquake that struck Tibet on October 22, 2026. Photo: US Geological Survey. A level-III earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, CCTV reported. The epicentre was in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua. Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said. More than 300 police officers have been dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported. Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, and carrying one person, footage on CCTV showed. It also showed rescue workers shining flashlights on other damaged buildings and soldiers lining up ready to be deployed. Earthquakes in China are relatively common. In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county. In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China killed at least 127 people, according to state media. That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the southwestern province of Yunnan. A huge tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left some 90,000 people dead or missing, including around 5,000 schoolchildren.

## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AI[Subscribe](https://news.google.com/subscriptions)

US crude oil exports to Asia are set to hit multi-year lows after the Iran war disrupted global shipping and pushed the cost to lease a tanker for the Pacific journey to a record of almost $80 million.

Asian refinery orders for US crude for delivery in November tumbled roughly 50% to [24 million to 26 million barrels](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/terminal/TNAJ8QN3N09H) this month sequentially, according to traders who asked for anonymity because they weren’t authorized to publicly comment. If that pace of orders holds through the end of this month, it would mark a seven-year low, based on ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa.

## Details

Hello fellow maniacs of horror and welcome to Omaha Horror Community: Fright Club!

Happy Halloween my Ghosts and Ghouls! It's the most glorious time of the year and the weather finally matches the spooky season we live and love year round. The theme for this month will be Universal horror movies and the films on the chopping block this month are a mystery but will still be up for a vote on the day of the event!

The movie viewing will be preceded by themed trivia with prizes to be won and I’ll be ordering pizza and bringing snacks as well. Thirsty? Legend Comics and Coffee has an amazing selection of drinks for you to choose from!

For those interested, after the official event is over, we’ll head out into the Benson area to hang out some more.

This event is 18+ unless accompanied by an adult and please feel free to invite your friends!

content: 2026-10-21   明豪的博客 2015年12月，美国哈佛大学尼曼新闻基金会授予中国资深记者杨继绳“莱昂斯新闻良知与正义奖”。杨继绳因故未能出席颁奖礼，以书面答谢词表达了他对新闻职业的理解。他说，记者既是一个卑鄙的职业，也是一个崇高的职业；既是一个平庸的职业，也是一个神圣的职业；既可以浅薄无知、趋炎附势，也可以学识渊博、洞察社会，承担公共良知。“是卑鄙还是崇高、是平庸还是神圣、是浅薄还是高深，在于从业者本人的良知、人格和价值取向。”这段话，我读来深有感触。 杨继绳以《墓碑》等著作，记录长期被遮蔽的历史。他的职业自白，不是书斋里的道德训诫，而是一位老记者对新闻、权力与良知关系的切身认识。十余年过去，新闻传播生态已发生巨变。传统媒体衰落，社交平台兴起，人人都有麦克风，人人都可以成为信息发布者。自媒体、独立记者、公民记者、网络意见领袖，纷纷登上公共舆论舞台。传播的技术门槛降低了，新闻的伦理门槛却没有因此消失；相反，当信息传播越来越自由，媒体人的良知与人格反而更加重要。 一、新闻可以有立场，事实不能有立场 记者不是没有价值观的人。一个记者可以信仰自由民主，可以同情弱者，可以反对专制，也可以拥护某种政治理念。真正的问题在于，当事实与立场发生冲突时，他选择忠于事实，还是忠于立场？职业记者与政治宣传员的根本区别，就在这里。政治宣传往往以预设结论组织材料，选择性呈现事实；新闻工作则应从事实出发，经过调查、核实与分析形成判断。前者要求事实服从立场，后者要求立场接受事实检验。 一个人如果只传播有利于自己政治立场的消息，对不利的事实视而不见，已经背离了新闻的完整性；如果进一步移花接木、断章取义、编造情节、制造谣言，则是在主动破坏公共社会赖以形成理性判断的事实基础。新闻自由保障表达的权利，却不赋予任何人歪曲事实的特权。 二、公民记者的兴起，不等于新闻伦理的废除 互联网打破了传统媒体对信息发布的垄断，这是社会进步。尤其在新闻自由受到压制的社会，普通公民通过手机记录现场、保存证据、传播被封锁的信息，具有不可替代的公共价值。但公民记者首先应当是事实的记录者，而不是谣言的搬运工。 当下某些自称公民记者、独立媒体人的网络传播者，缺乏基本的事实核查意识，却热衷于发布所谓内幕、独家、爆料。一张来历不明的图片，一段经过剪辑的视频，一则匿名账号的传言，甚至几句毫无出处的道听途说，都可以经过耸人听闻的标题包装，迅速传播。消息真假尚未查明，政治判断已经完成；证据尚未出现，道德审判已经开始。一旦有人质疑，便以政治立场回应事实问题，以道德标签代替证据。 更有甚者，长期传播未经证实的消息，面对反证拒不纠错，甚至将质疑者视为敌人。误传可能源于无知、疏忽和判断失误；故意造谣则是对事实的主动背叛。两者不能混为一谈，也不能仅凭报道错误便推定传播者主观恶意。但一个人如果反复传播不实信息，又拒绝承担核实与纠错责任，其公共信誉就理应受到质疑。 公民记者的称号不是道德勋章，独立媒体的招牌也不是新闻诚信的保证书。有没有记者证并不重要，重要的是有没有记者应当具备的事实意识与责任伦理。 三、摆脱了政治审查，为什么没有摆脱宣传思维？ 这是当下海外中文自媒体尤其值得反思的问题。一些人在政治立场上反对中共专制，在传播方式上却仍然沿用党国宣传的逻辑。他们痛恨官方制造谎言，却对有利于自己立场的谣言格外宽容；批评官方封锁信息，却热衷于选择性呈现事实；反对政治洗脑，却又以煽动情绪、制造敌人、操纵舆论的方式争夺受众。这种矛盾，不能仅仅用职业训练不足解释。 长期的政治宣传环境，不仅塑造了人们接受信息的习惯，也可能塑造其生产信息的方式。在这种思维中，事实不是需要尊重的客观对象，而是实现政治目的的工具；新闻不是发现真相的过程，而是争夺话语权的武器。只要政治目标被认为正确，传播手段便可以不择；只要攻击的是自己反对的权力，谎言似乎也能获得正当性。于是，一些人虽然在政治立场上完成了转变，却没有在认知方式和公共伦理上完成转变。他们反对的可能只是宣传机器所服务的政治权力，而不是宣传机器制造谎言的逻辑本身。 反对专制，并不天然意味着具备自由公民的人格；摆脱政治控制，也不等于摆脱了被政治宣传塑造的思维方式。 真正的思想解放，不只是改变政治立场，更是学会尊重事实、独立判断、容忍异议，并接受公共理性的约束。否则，反对者也可能在自己的传播实践中复制自己所反对的东西。 四、当谎言成为政治武器，谁在获利？ 自媒体时代，谎言还有一套现实的利益机制。严谨的调查需要时间，耸动的传言只需要几秒钟；核实事实需要成本，编造故事几乎没有门槛。一篇经过反复求证的报道，未必获得多少关注；一则迎合受众偏见的惊人消息，却可能迅速收获大量流量。流量可以转化为粉丝、打赏、广告、商业机会乃至政治影响力。于是，部分传播者逐渐从追求事实转向经营情绪，从调查真相转向迎合受众。他们关心的不是事情究竟怎样发生，而是怎样讲述才能引起愤怒、恐惧、仇恨或者狂欢。 尤其值得警惕的是，某些政治自媒体逐渐形成了一种奇特的传播生态：谣言被揭穿了，可以悄悄删除；下一个谣言出现了，继续传播。昨天的错误无人追究，今天的谎言照样收获掌声，传播者与受众之间形成相互迎合的关系。受众需要符合自己政治期待的消息，传播者便不断提供这样的消息。事实是否可靠，反而退居其次。久而久之，公共讨论不再围绕证据展开，而成为不同阵营之间的情绪对抗。 更严重的是，虚假指控可能伤害无辜者，而反复传播的谣言，也会使真正有价值的调查报道受到连带怀疑。谎言最终不仅损害被攻击者，也损害传播者所声称追求的公共目标。 一个人不能一面谴责官方宣传机器制造谎言，一面又以同样的方法经营自己的传播事业。 五、新闻良知不仅需要勇气，更需要谦卑 杨继绳认为，真正的职业记者会选择崇高、神圣、深刻与凶险，而远离卑鄙、平庸、浅薄和舒适。在新闻自由受到压制的社会，敢于揭露真相，可能付出失业、监禁乃至生命的代价，这种勇气值得尊重。但新闻良知并不只有勇敢一个维度。敢于批评权力的人，未必天然具有事实判断的能力；敢于揭露黑暗的人，也未必不会陷入偏见。 新闻工作还需要知识上的谦卑。承认自己可能判断错误，承认信息存在局限，承认尚未查明的事情不能轻易下结论。尤其要学会说三个字：我不知道。这三个字，看似平常，却是许多自媒体人最不愿意说出口的话。因为“不知道”不够刺激，“尚待核实”不够吸引眼球，“证据不足”更不容易制造流量。但正是这种克制，构成了新闻职业最重要的理性品质。 记者不是先知，评论者也不是法官。新闻的职责是尽可能接近事实，而不是永远表现得正确。真正尊重事实的媒体人，既应当有揭露他人错误的勇气，也应当有承认自己错误的诚实。 六、新闻自由与新闻责任，不可分离 新闻自由是现代文明的重要制度成果。它使公众能够获得多元信息，使政府权力接受监督，使社会不至于完全陷入官方叙事的垄断。但新闻自由的价值，不仅在于允许人们说话，更在于为公共社会提供发现事实、交换意见、纠正错误的条件。如果媒体人放弃事实核查，沉迷于谣言传播，热衷于操纵情绪，那么，即使拥有充分的表达自由，也未必能够形成健康的公共舆论。新闻自由与新闻良知，因而不可分离。前者解决权力能否任意压制表达的问题，后者解决传播者如何负责任地使用表达自由的问题。 没有新闻自由，媒体容易沦为权力的工具；没有新闻良知，媒体也可能沦为流量、资本、派系与个人野心的工具。对于那些以公共利益、社会正义、民主自由为旗帜的传播者而言，尤其需要明白：公共信誉不是自封的，而是在一次次面对事实、权力、利益和诱惑的选择中积累起来的。杨继绳说，记者的职业选择，最终取决于良知、人格和价值取向。这句话放在今天，仍然振聋发聩。 在新闻受到权力控制的时代，敢于说出真相是一种勇气；在人人都可以自由发声的时代，坚持不说谎话，同样是一种勇气。媒体人的良知，不仅在于敢于揭露别人的谎言，更在于拒绝制造自己的谎言。不因权势而隐瞒真相，不因利益而歪曲事实，不因立场而放弃核实，不因错误而拒绝纠正。 反对谎言的立场，不能赋予任何人说谎的特权。新闻可以批判一切权力，但新闻本身也必须接受事实的审判。 2026年10月21日 附： 杨继绳：记者，就是真相的记录者、挖掘者和保卫者 我是很热爱记者这个职业的。我在这个岗位上摔打四十多年，据我的体验和观察，我是这样评价记者这个职业的： 这是一个卑鄙的职业，这个职业可以混淆是非，颠倒黑白，制造弥天大谎，欺骗亿万受众；这是一个崇高的职业，这个职业可以针砭时弊、揭露黑暗、鞭挞邪恶、为民请命，担起社会良心的重责。 这是一个平庸的职业，回避矛盾，不问是非，明哲保身，甘当权势的喉舌；这是一个神圣的职业，胸怀天下，思虑千载，批评时政，监督政府，沟通社会，使媒体成为立法、司法、行政之外的第四权力。 这是一个浅薄的职业，只要能够写出通顺的记叙文，不需要多少学识，不需要卓越的见解，听话顺从，就能如鱼得水；这是一个深不可测的职业，记者不是专业学者，他需要从整体上研究社会、把握社会，无论有多么渊博的学识、有多么卓越的洞察力，在复杂多变的社会面前，都会感到学力不足，力不从心。 这是一个舒适而安全的职业，出入于宫阙楼台，行走于权力中枢，灯红酒绿的招待会、歌舞升平的庆典，访大官，见要人，春风得意，风光无限。 如果用文章与权势投桃报李，今日的书生可能是明日的高官，今日穷酸可能是明日的富豪；这是一个艰难而危险的职业，且不谈穿梭于枪林弹雨中的战地记者，就是在和平环境中，调查研究，探求真相，跋山涉水，阻力重重，除暴揭黑，千难万险。一旦触及到权势集团的痛处，不测之祸从天而降。 是卑鄙还是崇高、是平庸还是神圣、是浅薄还是高深，在于从业者本人的良知、人格和价值取向。真正的职业记者会选择崇高、神圣、深刻、凶险，鄙视和远离卑鄙、平庸、浅薄、舒适。 然而，在卑鄙与崇高、平庸与神圣之间，没有鸿沟、没有高墙，黑白之道，全凭自己把握。如果一脚踏进了黑道，就会被钉在历史的耻辱柱上，自己写的白纸黑字，是永远抹不掉的证据。“卑鄙是卑鄙者的通行证，高尚是高尚者的墓志铭”这条黑色定律在记者职场十分盛行。要不被这一黑律逼向卑鄙之路，就得无所畏惧，勇于献身。 这也是我对新闻良知与正义的理解。 （2015年12月，美国哈佛大学尼曼学会授予杨继绳“莱昂斯新闻良知与正义奖”，称杨“是一个榜样，值得那些希望记录人类黑暗而艰难斗争的人学习”。随后，因故未能出席颁奖礼，杨继绳以文字的形式发表这篇答谢词。以上为答谢词节选）

# Support Cecilia’s Over Seas Detention Release

Help Bring Cecilia Home: Urgent Legal Support for US Citizen Detained in China My name is I. Denise Torres, and I'm reaching out with an urgent request to help my daughter Cecilia, a US-born citizen currently detained in China. Our family faces mounting legal expenses that are far beyond our financial means, and time is critical. Our Immediate Need Following the guidance of the US Consulate, we must retain specialized legal representation in China who is specifically an English speaking attorney that can navigate the Chinese legal system on Cecilia's behalf. Legal representation for international clients in criminal matters in China can range from several thousand to hundreds of thousands of yuan China Legal Experts depending on case complexity and duration. For families like ours, working-class Americans with limited resources, these costs are insurmountable without help. The US Consulate has recommended a qualified law firm experienced in representing foreign nationals. Cecilia has not been formally charged at this time and the funds are intended solely to support the current legal process related to her detention. However, we need to secure their services immediately, which requires: Attorney retainer and representation fees for an English-speaking Chinese defense lawyer Communication and translation services to facilitate family contact Personal care expenses for Cecilia during detention, including medical necessities Ongoing legal advocacy through the completion of her case Why Legal Representation Is Critical Cecilia is alone in a detention facility with severely limited communication rights and no phone calls, no family visitation, and no direct contact with us. The US Consulate has been extraordinarily supportive, but they can only conduct welfare checks once per month and cannot intervene in China's legal proceedings. A private attorney is her only opportunity for: Regular advocacy visits (every two weeks, as permitted) Direct communication link between Cecilia and our family Professional legal representation through required proceedings Monitoring of her wellbeing and medical needs The Medical Urgency Cecilia manages diabetes requiring three insulin injections daily. She experiences related complications including severe stomach issues and pain. Ensuring she receives proper medical care during detention is essential, and legal representation is critical to advocating for her health needs. The Process and Timeline Under guidance from the US Consulate, I cannot share specific details about the circumstances of Cecilia's detention, as doing so could compromise the legal process. What I can share is that we're working through official channels and following all recommended procedures to bring her home safely. Both Cecilia and I are US-born citizens. She is a compassionate, selfless young woman who would help anyone in need. Now she needs us to help her. Our goal is to cover estimated attorney fees for legal representation, communication services that allow us to stay connected with our daughter, and personal care expenses during her detention. Legal fees in China vary significantly based on lawyer experience, case complexity, and whether specialized English-language services are required Lawzana. International representation for US citizens detained abroad requires substantial financial resources that our working-class family simply doesn't have. Every Day Counts Without proper legal representation, Cecilia faces this situation alone—unable to communicate with her family, uncertain about the process ahead, and managing a serious medical condition in a foreign country. Every contribution, no matter the size, brings us closer to securing the legal help she desperately needs. How You Can Help Donate any amount you can afford—every dollar helps Share this campaign widely across your networks Keep Cecilia in your thoughts—this support means everything to our family The US Consulate continues monitoring her welfare, but only an attorney can advocate for her case, facilitate our communication, and work toward her safe return home. Our Gratitude Thank you for taking time to read Cecilia's story. Your generosity during this incredibly difficult time gives us hope. As a mother watching my daughter face this ordeal from thousands of miles away, your support is a lifeline. With deep gratitude and hope, Irma Denise Torres
